articles.title: Las Guerreras K-pop vs el equipo 7 de Naruto: cómo recrear esta pelea con IA
articles.text:
Una imagen generada con inteligencia artificial (IA) puede enfrentar a Las Guerreras K-pop con el equipo 7 de Naruto a partir de referencias visuales y un prompt detallado.
El proceso puede hacerse desde el navegador, sin instalar aplicaciones de origen desconocido ni utilizar programas externos que pidan permisos innecesarios.
La clave está en ordenar las imágenes antes de escribir el prompt. Las referencias permiten conservar los rasgos de las protagonistas de la película de Netflix y de los personajes del anime, mientras que el texto define la acción, las posiciones, los ataques y el escenario.
La escena puede mostrar a las tres guerreras frente a Naruto, Sasuke y Sakura en un campo de batalla, con efectos de energía y elementos propios de cada universo.
Qué imágenes conviene elegir como referencia para generar la ilustración
El primer paso es seleccionar una imagen grupal de Las Guerreras K-pop en la que se distingan con claridad los rostros, peinados, prendas y accesorios de las tres integrantes.
Una foto de cuerpo entero o tomada desde la cintura ayuda a que el generador diferencie a cada personaje y reduzca el riesgo de que mezcle los vestuarios o repita rasgos faciales.
Asimismo, hay que conseguir una referencia del equipo 7 con Naruto, Sasuke y Sakura. La imagen debe mostrar sus atuendos, peinados y elementos identificables, como la banda ninja, el traje naranja de Naruto, la ropa oscura de Sasuke y el vestuario rojo de Sakura.
Dónde se cargan las imágenes sin descargar aplicaciones
Las imágenes pueden adjuntarse en el chat de Gemini, la herramienta de inteligencia artificial de Google. El acceso se hace desde la página oficial en un navegador actualizado, una alternativa que evita la descarga de archivos desde sitios no verificados o aplicaciones que no pertenecen a desarrolladores identificados.
Dentro de la conversación, los archivos se cargan mediante el botón de adjuntar o con la función de arrastrar y soltar. Conviene enviar las dos referencias en un único mensaje para que la herramienta reciba toda la información visual antes de generar la escena.
Luego es necesario comprobar que las miniaturas aparezcan completas y que no haya recortes, imágenes borrosas ni figuras ajenas que puedan alterar el resultado.
Qué prompt permite obtener una primera versión de la pelea
El pedido debe indicar el estilo, los participantes, las posturas y los efectos. Un prompt es el siguiente: “Crear una ilustración de acción estilo anime. Tres guerreras K-pop inspiradas en las referencias visuales luchan contra Naruto, Sasuke y Sakura en una arena destruida. Ubicar a las guerreras a la izquierda y al equipo 7 a la derecha. Mostrar un plano panorámico, movimiento, escombros, destellos de energía y expresiones de combate”.
Después se pueden sumar detalles para separar los ataques. Por ejemplo: “Naruto sostiene una esfera azul de energía en la mano; Sasuke concentra rayos azules alrededor de su brazo y empuña una espada; Sakura avanza con el puño levantado”.
Cómo ajustar los errores de la imagen generada con IA
La primera creación de la IA debe revisarse por partes. Es común que una imagen con inteligencia artificial presente manos con dedos adicionales, accesorios repetidos, ojos desalineados, armas deformadas o personajes que no respetan su ubicación.
Las correcciones funcionan mejor cuando son breves y específicas. Se puede solicitar: “Mantener tres guerreras”, “corregir la mano derecha de Naruto”, “eliminar el arma duplicada”, “poner a Sakura detrás de Sasuke” o “hacer que el escudo violeta esté frente a la guerrera de cabello trenzado”.
Qué hacer antes de descargar y compartir el resultado
Una vez elegida la versión final, el archivo puede descargarse desde la misma conversación. Antes de publicarlo en redes sociales, enviarlo por mensajes o incluirlo en una nota, corresponde identificarlo como una imagen creada con IA. Esa aclaración lo distingue de una pieza de Netflix o de los titulares de derechos de Naruto.
El material debe presentarse como una recreación hecha por usuarios y sin vínculo oficial con las producciones originales. Conviene evitar usos que induzcan a error sobre su origen o que lo hagan pasar por una imagen promocional auténtica.

articles.title: Les Français téléchargent trois fois plus vite que les Japonais, selon ce nouveau classement nPerf
articles.text:
La France décroche la première place du classement nPerf du débit descendant fixe, donc en téléchargement, parmi les pays à richesse comparable. Au troisième trimestre 2026, l’Hexagone dépasse les 360 Mbit/s de moyenne, loin devant plusieurs grandes nations européennes.
Le débit descendant fixe de la France, autrement dit sa vitesse de téléchargement, fait la course en tête apprend-on ce lundi 19 octobre puisqu'entre juillet et septembre 2026, l'Hexagone a pris la première place du classement nPerf réservé aux pays à richesse comparable. La plateforme indépendante, nourrie par des millions de tests de connexion chaque année, a passé au crible les nations dont le PIB par habitant se situe entre 35 000 et 60 000 dollars. Dans le top 10, l’écart entre la tête et le dernier classé dépasse les 240 Mbit/s !
360 Mbit/s, le chiffre qui place la France sur la première marche
Avec 360,20 Mbit/s (mégabits par seconde) en moyenne sur réseau fixe, la France devance la Slovénie (316,45 Mbit/s) d'environ 44 Mbit/s, puis le Canada (292,46 Mbit/s). L'Espagne, quatrième avec 265,72 Mbit/s, garde une sérieuse marge sur le Royaume-Uni (174,85 Mbit/s) et l'Italie (173,01 Mbit/s). Ces deux poids lourds européens, presque à égalité, doivent se contenter du milieu de tableau.
Concrètement, à quoi correspondent ces 360 Mbit/s ? Le débit se compte en mégabits par seconde, alors que la taille d’un fichier s’exprime en octets, et un octet vaut huit bits. La connexion française avale donc environ 45 mégaoctets chaque seconde. Du coup, un fichier de 2,15 Go arrive en moins de 50 secondes. De quoi lancer une grosse mise à jour en allant chercher son café et la retrouver terminée avant la première gorgée. Sur les vidéos en haute définition et autres contenus volumineux, ces secondes gagnées finissent vite par s’additionner.
Un classement taillé sur mesure, mais des écarts bien réels
Plus bas dans le top 10, le contraste est plutôt saisissant, et beaucoup ne s'en doutent peut-être pas. Cinquième, Israël s'arrête à 197,07 Mbit/s, soit 163 Mbit/s de moins que la France. La Finlande (136,72 Mbit/s) et la Tchéquie (134,70 Mbit/s) se suivent à deux petits mégabits d'écart. Le Japon, qu'on imagine volontiers à la pointe, ferme la marche de ce classement, avec 115,95 Mbit/s. Les foyers français téléchargent ainsi plus de trois fois plus vite que les Japonais.
Faut-il pour autant sabrer le champagne pour autant ? Pas trop vite. nPerf ne compare ici que des pays de richesse voisine, mesurée par le PIB par habitant, c’est-à-dire la richesse produite chaque année rapportée au nombre d’habitants. Tous ceux qui dépassent 60 000 dollars par habitant sont donc écartés d’office.
Pour situer la France face à ces nations plus riches, il faut se tourner vers d’autres classements. Autre nuance, ces moyennes proviennent de tests lancés par les internautes eux-mêmes depuis l’application ou le site de nPerf. Elles traduisent donc leur expérience réelle, mais dépendent aussi de qui teste, et avec quel abonnement. C’est une belle médaille pour la France, donc, mais à relativiser au final, puisque remportée dans sa catégorie uniquement.

articles.title: Anthropic says its workforce has been getting older, but is also spending more time in meetings
articles.text:
Anthropic says its workforce has been getting older, but is also spending more time in meetings
Anthropic isn't making so many junior hires, it turns out
- Anthropic says it is no longer hiring so many junior/entry-level roles
- Many technical workers are becoming AI managers, and so are spending more time in meetings
- The company says its "deep adoption" makes it a useful "early warning system" for AI's impacts
One of the biggest AI developers in the world has released a brand-new study on how AI is transforming its own workforce - but we're not sure whether it's good or bad news.
Starting off with the bad news, Anthropic uncovered a considerable drop in junior workers – junior workers accounted for just 14% of technical staff by mid-2026, down from 21% in early 2025.
The proportion of junior employees among the company's new technical hires fell even more dramatically in the same period, from 27% to just 9%.
Is AI replacing some workers, but not all?
Ultimately, the paper concludes that artificial intelligence is handling more and more entry-level roles, therefore Anthropic hasn't needed to hire as many junior workers.
In fact, hiring on the whole has seemingly dropped thanks to AI-induced productivity gains. "[Anthropic] has hired less per dollar of revenue than an earlier generation of large tech companies," the company explained.
Crucially, the Claude maker isn't reporting a declining technical workforce. Quite the opposite, as it continues to grow, but those technical workers are now handling higher-level, managerial-type roles.
AI's biggest impact at Anthropic has been the number of code commits per engineer, up 5.1x from the end of 2025 to mid-2026. Data queries per data scientist (up 3.1x), contracts per legal worker (up 3.1x) and deals per salesperson (up 1.7x) are also all trending upward.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Humans remain in the loop
More broadly, the company sees many workers transitioning into decision-making roles, and that's increased the amount of time they spend in meetings. A 20% median increase was observed across the workforce.
"Engineers described becoming leaders and managers of agents; non-technical employees described doing more and more of the strategic parts of their job."
Despite massive productivity gains through automation, Anthropic also confirmed that some roles just have to remain human. They include things like sales calls and interviews.
Still, human workers are seen as something of a bottleneck in the world of AI. Claude spends around 80% of interactive session time waiting for human input, the research revealed.
Looking ahead, Anthropic has projected where we could be heading and how things could change with all employers. One of the biggest shifts could come in hiring, where a new set of skills is likely to be prioritized – including "autonomy and judgment."
A more optimistic approach admits that hiring is indeed falling, but job opportunities could actually be exploding. "One possibility is single-person start-ups, each with a human founder steering swarms of agents to rake in billions in revenue."
Ultimately, Anthropic says its "deep adoption of AI... makes it a useful case," and that it exists as an "early warning system" – so maybe we look at AI companies to see how AI is going to impact jobs?

articles.title: Cuánto cuesta la criptomoneda ethereum este día
articles.text:
Ethereum es una plataforma digital que adopta la tecnología de cadena de bloques (blockchain) y expande su uso a una gran variedad de aplicaciones, mientras que ether es su criptomoneda nativa. En el mundo de las finanzas digitales es común que la criptomoneda sea llamada como la red, aunque en realidad no son lo mismo.
La plataforma ethereum, creada en el 2015 por el programador Vitalik Buterin, buscaba ser un instrumento para aplicaciones descentralizadas y colaborativas sobre las que se pueden hacer contratos inteligentes (dAPPs)
Al igual que el bitcoin, el valor de ether se disparó en un corto periodo de tiempo. En enero de 2016, ether cotizaba alrededor de un dólar y actualmente tiene un máximo histórico de 4.953,73 dólares.
El precio de la criptomoneda de ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 2407.26 dólares por unidad.
Esto quiere decir que el activo digital registró un cambio del 0.62 las últimas 24 horas, así como una variación del 0.0 % en los últimos 60 minutos.
Actualmente, ethereum se encuentra en el lugar #2 de popularidad en el mercado digital. Cabe mencionar que el máximo histórico que ha alcanzado esta criptodivisa es de 4891.7 dólares por unidad.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: GhostAction Attackers Plant Credential Stealer Disguised as Font in 94 GitHub Repositories
articles.text:
The threat actor behind the GhostAction supply chain attack has expanded beyond injecting malicious GitHub Actions workflows into compromised projects to phish open-source developers and deliver a stealer malware disguised within a fake font file.
The latest evolution, detailed by OpenSourceMalware, signals that the attackers are actively refining their modus operandi in response to steps taken by GitHub to prevent the workflow from running.
According to the threat intelligence platform, the threat actor registered the domain "my-github[.]com" and pointed it at "193.32.204[.]199," the same IP address that's used as an exfiltration endpoint for data harvested from running the malicious workflow.
The domain was registered on October 9, 2026, 17 days after "my-gitlab[.]com" was registered. It's unclear if the latter code-hosting-themed domain is operated by the same threat actor.
"It follows the same my-<code-host>.com naming pattern, making it a useful pivot, but current infrastructure does not directly connect it to GhostAction," security researcher Paul McCarty said. "They use different registrars, registrant records, Cloudflare nameserver pairs, IP addresses, ASNs, and DNS designs, and no shared certificate or account artifact has been recovered."
Since then, the "my-github[.]com" domain has been used in a phishing email impersonating a GitHub security alert to target an open-source maintainer the same day it was registered. The message, sent from "noreply@my-github[.]com," warned of a new login to their GitHub account from Moscow, Russia, and instructed them to click on a link to secure their account.
The deceptive page, per OpenSourceMalware, is said to have acted as a reverse proxy, harvesting the victim's password and two-factor authentication (2FA) code, and injected JavaScript that authorized an OAuth app with permissions to modify their workflows so as to facilitate a GhostAction-style attack.
The fake login page also includes JavaScript to silently authorize a GitHub OAuth device flow with repo, workflow, and read:org scopes, granting it broad permissions to read/write repositories, modify Actions workflow files, and gain visibility into organization membership and related organizational data.
The idea is the same as device code phishing, where the end goal is to obtain an access token from GitHub and exfiltrate it to "my-github[.]com" on TCP/8443.
"The script receives a device code and user code, loads /login/device, extracts GitHub's forms from the returned HTML, and submits them automatically," McCarty explained. "It inserts the user code, locates an authorization form, adds authorize=1, and posts the approval through the victim's authenticated proxied session."
"The victim does not need to type the device code or consciously approve the OAuth application. This kit goes further by automating the user-code and authorization steps through the reverse-proxied session."
By stealing a repository-scoped OAuth token, it gives the attacker a reusable API credential. Furthermore, the permissions granted through the stealthy OAuth authorization are consistent with GhostAction's ability to enumerate repositories and inject malicious workflow files under ".github/workflows/."
"The actor can now combine repository-scale automation with individual social engineering against people whose accounts provide access to projects, organizations, registries, and downstream users," OpenSourceMalware said.
To make matters worse, the campaign has also been observed incorporating a second-stage component that persists on developer machines even after the malicious workflow has been removed.
Specifically, the approach takes a leaf out of North Korea's playbook by committing three different files -
- A Microsoft Visual Studio Code (VS Code) tasks.json file with a "runOn: folderOpen" trigger that causes it to run automatically when the folder is opened in the application.
- A "public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2" file that contains a stealer payload designed to harvest AWS keys, PyPI tokens, npm tokens, Git logins, Kubernetes cluster credentials, SSH private keys, and AI provider credentials for Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini. The font file name is the same as one used in North Korea's PolinRider campaign from January 2026.
- A second GitHub Actions workflow that's activated if the infostealer never runs.
This causes VS Code to auto-run the credential stealer, which, besides collecting data, installs a cron job that runs attacker-supplied code every five minutes. The collected data is sent to the same server over plain HTTP on port 8080. A total of 94 compromised repositories with the second-stage component have been identified.
As for the second CI workflow, it's the same as the original malicious workflow, but with added credential formats to look for and a fallback that uploads findings to a secret GitHub gist if the POST fails. The second workflow goes by the following names -
- lint.yml
- ci-check.yml
- build-check.yml
- repo-health.yml
- audit.yml
- code-review.yml
- test-suite.yml
- cache-cleanup.yml
OpenSourceMalware said the 94 repositories belong to 66 owners, out of which 15 have since been deleted, renamed, or made private. Of the still accessible repositories, most of them appear to have been largely abandoned, with one of them left untouched for more than nine years. Sixty-five of the 79 went without a commit for more than a year.
"Stage 1 needs GitHub to run the workflow," OpenSourceMalware said. "On October 9, GitHub started preventing the malicious workflow from running, and the waves on October 10 and 12 extracted no secrets. Stage 2 adds a launcher that doesn't need a runner at all, and it arrived six days after the block. We can’t say the block caused it. We can say the operator moved to a place GitHub's controls don't reach."
To mitigate the threat, developers should revoke GitHub access and tokens from a clean device, change their passwords, audit their repositories, rotate every credential the workflows can reach, and alert users who have cloned the repositories.
"We don't know who the operator is, but their work suggests limited experience," Jenn Gile, co-founder of OpenSourceMalware, told The Hacker News. "The stealer's environment-variable filter misses most API keys, its home-directory search can time out and discard its own results, and a single IP handles exfiltration, phishing, and noisy internet scanning. That last mistake is why searching for the IP still finds infections."

articles.title: Ray-Ban Meta : les lunettes enregistraient l’audio sans le consentement des utilisateurs
articles.text:
Des propriétaires de Ray-Ban Meta ont découvert des enregistrements audio qu’ils n’avaient jamais demandé à leurs lunettes de réaliser. Meta affirme avoir corrigé le dysfonctionnement, mais plusieurs questions restent sans réponse concernant la confidentialité des conversations.
Les Ray-Ban Meta ont beau ressembler à des lunettes classiques, elles embarquent des caméras, des microphones et un assistant IA capable de répondre à nos questions. Une technologie pratique au quotidien, à condition de pouvoir lui faire confiance. Or, plusieurs utilisateurs ont récemment découvert que leurs lunettes enregistraient certaines conversations sans qu’ils aient demandé quoi que ce soit à Meta AI. Plus inquiétant, les fichiers audio et leurs transcriptions étaient ensuite conservés dans l’application du constructeur. Meta assure avoir réglé le problème, mais cet incident rappelle les difficultés que soulèvent ces appareils capables de nous écouter à tout moment.
Des conversations enregistrées sans prononcer « Hey Meta »
L’affaire a été révélée le 13 octobre par Android Authority, après plusieurs témoignages publiés sur Reddit. L’un des utilisateurs concernés affirme avoir constaté le même comportement sur trois paires de Ray-Ban Meta, appartenant à deux générations différentes. Ses lunettes auraient activé leur assistant vocal au milieu de conversations ordinaires, sans qu’il ait prononcé la commande « Hey Meta ».
Il assure pourtant avoir désactivé l’option permettant de poursuivre les échanges avec l’assistant sans répéter cette formule. Cela n’aurait pas empêché les activations intempestives.
Le problème ne s’arrêtait pas là. En consultant l’historique de Meta AI, l’utilisateur aurait découvert des enregistrements audio accompagnés de leurs transcriptions textuelles. Des conversations qui n’étaient donc pas seulement entendues par les microphones, mais également enregistrées par l’application.
Selon son témoignage, le phénomène serait apparu après une récente mise à jour du logiciel des lunettes. Aucun élément ne permet toutefois de confirmer que celle-ci est responsable du dysfonctionnement.
D'autres propriétaires ont rapporté des comportements similaires, mais les témoignages restent peu nombreux. Il serait donc prématuré d’affirmer que toutes les Ray-Ban Meta étaient concernées. En revanche, l’existence d’un dysfonctionnement semble bien confirmée par la réaction du constructeur.
Meta affirme avoir corrigé le bug, sans expliquer son origine
Interrogée par nos confrères, Meta a répondu que le problème était désormais résolu. L’entreprise rappelle également que les utilisateurs peuvent consulter, gérer et supprimer les journaux vocaux de leurs interactions avec Meta AI depuis les paramètres de l’application. Une réponse plutôt brève, qui laisse plusieurs interrogations en suspens.
Meta ne précise pas combien d’appareils ont été touchés, ni ce qui provoquait ces activations involontaires. Le constructeur n’indique pas davantage si les enregistrements concernés ont été transmis à ses serveurs ou s’ils ont fait l’objet d’autres traitements.
Comme le souligne Ars Technica, ce dysfonctionnement intervient dans un contexte déjà délicat pour les lunettes connectées de Meta. En mars dernier, nous avions appris que des sous-traitants pouvaient accéder à des vidéos particulièrement intimes captées par les Ray-Ban Meta. Une enquête qui soulevait déjà de sérieuses questions sur le traitement des données personnelles collectées par ces appareils.
Meta a pourtant renforcé certaines protections, notamment pour empêcher les enregistrements lorsque le voyant lumineux extérieur est masqué. Mais ces dispositifs ne répondent pas au problème révélé cette semaine : un assistant vocal qui se déclenche alors que son propriétaire ne lui a rien demandé.
Reste que ces lunettes demandent à leurs propriétaires, mais aussi aux personnes qui les entourent, d’accepter la présence permanente de microphones et de caméras. Le voyant lumineux peut signaler un enregistrement, encore faut-il que l’utilisateur remarque son activation.
Pour ceux qui portent leurs Ray-Ban Meta toute la journée, l’incident pose finalement une question assez simple : comment être certain que ses lunettes n’enregistrent rien lorsqu’on ne leur demande rien ?

articles.title: WhatsApp desarrolla un navegador propio para abrir links sin salir del chat en iPhone
articles.text:
WhatsApp desarrolla un navegador integrado para iPhone que permitirá abrir cualquier enlace compartido en un chat sin abandonar la aplicación. La función se encuentra en preparación dentro de la beta para iOS y ampliará una opción previa, limitada a determinados enlaces comerciales que cumplían requisitos técnicos.
El cambio puede resultar útil para quienes reciben o envían varios links durante una conversación, ya que evitará el salto automático a Safari, Chrome u otro navegador instalado en el dispositivo. La navegación quedará separada del chat, de modo que el usuario podrá consultar una página y regresar a la conversación sin interrumpirla.
La novedad fue detectada en la actualización 26.41.10.72 de WhatsApp beta para iOS, disponible mediante TestFlight. Por ahora, la herramienta continúa en desarrollo: no está lista para su lanzamiento general y WhatsApp no ha comunicado una fecha para habilitarla entre el público.
La función supera la limitación de los enlaces comerciales
WhatsApp ya introdujo una opción para abrir enlaces comerciales dentro de la aplicación. Esa herramienta apareció en la actualización 25.14.10.72 de la beta de iOS y permitió consultar ciertas páginas de empresas sin cambiar a Safari.
Sin embargo, aquella versión estaba restringida a vínculos que cumplían condiciones concretas. El sitio web debía utilizar HTTPS, un requisito técnico destinado a asegurar la conexión. Por esa razón, gran parte de los enlaces compartidos habitualmente en las conversaciones no podía abrirse dentro de WhatsApp.
El nuevo navegador integrado de WhatsApp elimina esa limitación. La compañía trabaja en un sistema compatible con cualquier enlace enviado o recibido dentro de la pantalla de chat, sin importar si procede de una empresa o de otro contacto.
La propuesta mantendrá una alternativa para quienes prefieran usar el navegador habitual. Desde el menú de tres puntos será posible elegir la opción para abrir la página en Safari, Chrome o cualquier otra aplicación definida como navegador predeterminado.
La activación se realizará desde los ajustes de WhatsApp
La herramienta no se activará de forma automática. WhatsApp añadirá una nueva opción llamada “Navegador integrado” dentro de los ajustes de la aplicación. Allí, cada usuario podrá decidir si desea abrir los enlaces directamente en la pantalla de conversación.
Cuando esta opción se active por primera vez, aparecerá una hoja inferior con una explicación sobre su funcionamiento. El aviso indicará que los vínculos pueden consultarse sin salir de WhatsApp, en lugar de abrirse en el navegador predeterminado del iPhone.
Los usuarios podrán volver al navegador predeterminado en cualquier momento. Esa posibilidad permite alternar entre la navegación interna de WhatsApp y Safari, Chrome u otras aplicaciones instaladas en el dispositivo.
El navegador integrado funcionará en todos los chats y con cualquier enlace compartido. La amplitud de esa compatibilidad constituye la principal diferencia respecto a la herramienta anterior, que se limitaba a ciertos vínculos comerciales.
La sesión de navegación no afectará la conversación
Al abrir un enlace con el navegador integrado, la navegación se realizará en una sesión separada del chat. El usuario podrá desplazarse por el sitio web sin alterar el contenido de la conversación que dejó abierta.
El sistema también incluirá opciones para administrar la información almacenada durante la navegación. La pantalla de configuración contará con una sección destinada a gestionar datos, desde la que se podrán borrar las cookies y la caché de los sitios visitados dentro de WhatsApp.
Los datos de navegación se almacenarán localmente en el dispositivo, con un funcionamiento comparable al de Safari. WhatsApp no podrá ver los enlaces compartidos en la conversación ni cuáles abren los usuarios. Apple tampoco podrá acceder a esa información, de acuerdo con la explicación de la función.
TestFlight permite probar la beta en iPhone
El acceso a las versiones beta de WhatsApp para iOS se realiza mediante TestFlight, la plataforma oficial de Apple para probar aplicaciones en desarrollo. El proceso comienza con la descarga de TestFlight desde la App Store y su instalación en el iPhone.
Después, es necesario abrir desde el dispositivo el enlace oficial de invitación de la beta de WhatsApp. Si hay espacio disponible, se mostrará la ficha del programa en TestFlight. El usuario deberá aceptar las condiciones e instalar la versión de prueba, que reemplazará temporalmente la aplicación estable.
El principal obstáculo es la disponibilidad de plazas. Apple establece un número máximo de probadores por aplicación, por lo que el programa suele aparecer como completo. Para conseguir un cupo, es necesario revisar periódicamente el enlace o seguir los avisos sobre vacantes.
Las versiones beta pueden presentar errores, cierres inesperados, fallos en las notificaciones o un consumo mayor de batería. Antes de salir del programa o desinstalar la aplicación para regresar a la versión oficial, es fundamental crear una copia de seguridad de los chats para evitar la pérdida de información.

articles.title: Popcorn Studio AI secures $1 million to expand AI-powered filmmaking platform
articles.text: UAE-based creative technology startup Popcorn Studio AI has secured a $1 million pre-seed funding package, led by Emirati entrepreneur and investor Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, to support product development and international expansion. Founded in 2026 by Egyptian entrepreneurs Shady Essam and Mohamed Hedar, Popcorn Studio AI operates an AI-powered video production platform that enables filmmakers, content creators, agencies and brands to produce cinematic content through an integrated workflow. The platform offers AI tools for scriptwriting, character development, scene generation, voiceovers, lip-syncing and post-production, with a particular focus on Arabic-language content and regional dialects. The funding will support the development of Popcorn's AI technology, expansion of its product suite and growth across the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, alongside international partnerships. Popcorn Studio AI has also announced an AI filmmaking competition associated with the El Gouna Film Festival, featuring a $70,000 prize pool to support emerging filmmakers. Press release: Popcorn Studio AI, the Dubai-based artificial intelligence platform transforming how films and video content are created, has announced a $1 million funding package, marking a significant milestone in its mission to reshape the future of creative production. The funding, led by Emirati serial entrepreneur and investor Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, will support Popcorn's next phase of growth, including continued AI technology development, international expansion, and the evolution of its creative platform. Founded by Egyptian entrepreneurs Shady Essam and Mohamed Hedar, Popcorn Studio AI is challenging one of the creative industry's longest-standing limitations: the belief that producing high-quality cinematic content requires substantial budgets, large production teams, and complex technical workflows. Popcorn is building a future where a compelling idea, rather than access to expensive production infrastructure, determines what can be brought to life. From an Idea to a Film. Without the Traditional Barriers. Unlike conventional AI video generators that require creators to navigate multiple tools, complex prompts, and disconnected production workflows, Popcorn brings the creative process together within one integrated platform. Through its specialised AI studios, creators, filmmakers, agencies, and brands can develop concepts, build characters, generate cinematic scenes, create commercial videos, and produce multilingual content using advanced generative AI models. A defining strength of the platform is its focus on Arabic-language content — including native Arabic lip-sync capabilities and support for regional dialects — addressing a major gap in the global AI video landscape. Built in Dubai with international ambitions, Popcorn combines advanced AI technology with a deep understanding of regional culture, language, and storytelling. Its vision extends beyond making video production faster or more affordable. The company aims to establish an entirely new creative infrastructure where filmmakers can experiment more freely, brands can produce content at scale, and emerging storytellers can bring ambitious ideas to the screen. A New Chapter for AI-Powered Filmmaking Popcorn's growth comes at a time when artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing the economics of the global creative industry. What once required weeks of planning, expensive equipment, physical locations, and large production crews can increasingly be developed through AI-powered creative workflows. Yet the company's founders believe the greatest opportunity is not simply automation but creative empowerment. "Technology has always changed how stories are told. Cinema evolved from silent films to sound, from film reels to digital cameras, and now we're entering the next chapter with artificial intelligence," said Shady Essam, Co-Founder and CEO of Popcorn Studio AI. "Our ambition isn't to replace filmmakers. It's to remove the barriers between imagination and execution. We want to make it possible for anyone with a powerful story to create something extraordinary, regardless of their budget, location, or technical background." The company's momentum has also extended into the filmmaking community, with Popcorn announcing an AI filmmaking competition connected to the El Gouna Film Festival, featuring a $70,000 prize pool. The initiative reflects Popcorn's commitment to supporting emerging filmmakers and accelerating the adoption of AI-powered storytelling across the region. Strategic Investment to Accelerate Global Ambitions For Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, the investment reflects a conviction that the MENA region is positioned to lead the next chapter of AI-driven content creation — and that Popcorn has the team and the technology to make that happen. "POPCORN Studio AI represents exactly the kind of bold, regionally rooted technology I look for. The content market across the Middle East and North Africa is enormous, and AI is still in its earliest stages here. Shady and Mohamed have the vision, the execution capability, and a product that's already resonating. I am proud to back them at this stage." — Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, Investor With this funding in place, Popcorn Studio AI is focused on expanding its product suite, scaling its user base across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt, and building the partnerships that will bring AI-powered filmmaking to a new generation of creators worldwide.

articles.title: Thanks, AI: The PlayStation 6 could be priced over $1,000 as leaker claims its memory and storage alone cost Sony $680 thanks to the AI-drive component crisis
articles.text:
The PlayStation 6 could cost over $1,000 as leaker claims its memory and storage alone will cost Sony $680
The most expensive games console ever?
- A leaker has claimed the PlayStation 6’s storage and memory alone could cost $680
- That lines up with past predictions that the console will cost $1,000 or more
- Sony has remained silent on the potential cost of its next-generation device
It’s no secret that the ongoing AI-driven RAM crisis has pushed component prices to extraordinarily unpleasant highs, and that’s made everything from graphics cards to new smartphones more expensive. Now, it looks like the misery could be spreading to the upcoming PlayStation 6, with some predictions indicating that an eye-watering price tag of $1,000 or more could be on the horizon.
That idea comes from renowned leaker KeplerL2 on the NeoGAF forums, who recently argued that the procurement cost to Sony of the PlayStation 6’s memory and storage alone comes to $680. That’s before we even consider other components like the GPU, CPU, and motherboard, and it makes for grim reading for anyone hoping for a reasonably priced console from Sony.
The context here is that KeplerL2’s comment was made in response to another forum member. That person had expressed doubts over KeplerL2’s previous prediction that the total bill of materials for the PlayStation 6 would come to $960. That prediction was made in July 2026, and with prices only increasing since then, the final bill to Sony could easily push past the $1,000 mark — especially if the RAM and storage come to $680 before anything else is factored in.
While some games consoles have historically been sold at a loss in order to drive software sales, Sony has said in recent months that “As a principle, we do not intend to sell hardware at significant losses.” That suggests that if the PlayStation 6’s bill of materials really does come to $960 — or more — then that’s likely to be close to the price that consumers will be asked to pay.
More bad news for PlayStation fans
KeplerL2 is a well-known leaker in the world of consoles and computing hardware, and in recent weeks they have made claims surrounding console release dates, the performance of the next Xbox, and AMD’s own version of DLSS 5. Their past track record gives them a degree of credibility, but as with every so-called leak and rumor, it’s sensible to treat it with a dose of skepticism until it is confirmed.
Still, given the way hardware prices are going, it wouldn’t be too surprising to see the PlayStation 6 debut at $1,000 or more. Costs of the priciest PlayStation components — including the memory, storage, and GPU — are way up compared to when the PlayStation 5 launched and are showing no signs of slowing down. In fact, they could get worse over the next year or two.
Sony has not made any comments on which way prices for the PlayStation 6 might go, so we’ll have to wait and see for now. But combined with the news that Sony is planning to ditch physical discs altogether in the near future, the future could be tough for PlayStation gamers.

articles.title: From Email-to-Case to the Boardroom: How Inherited Agents Break Governance Built for Software
articles.text:
In Salesforce Agentforce, the recommended way to make an agent respond to events is a Flow: a record is created or a case is updated, and the Flow passes data into the agent's prompt. Separately, Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case turn inbound customer messages into case records; it is how airlines and hotels run support intake. Both are standard, documented, as-designed features. Chained together, they produce this path:
public internet → email → case record → agent prompt → agent action → case comment → outbound reply
An unauthenticated outsider now has a route into an internal agent's instructions, and the agent's reply leaves through the same door. Nothing was misconfigured. The finding, documented by researchers in August 2026, is a clean example of how agents that arrive inside existing platforms fail: through the application around them, not the model inside them.
The risk is in the application, and the application is the thing nobody re-reviewed
Which intake features are enabled, which triggers fire, which objects are exposed to guest users, which automation passes untrusted data where, and which model version the agent is quietly calling underneath: these are the variables that decide whether the Agentforce chain is a support-queue nuisance or a data exposure. A vendor risk review performed once at procurement sees none of them, because the agent did not exist at procurement. A prompt filter watching the agent's inputs does not know that a particular input originated from a stranger, because prompt filters do not understand Email-to-Case.
Securing an inherited agent therefore means understanding its host application at the depth its own admins do. That depth is the one thing a questionnaire and a scanner both lack. The City-Forum campaign, an active worldwide data-theft operation against Salesforce and ServiceNow instances running since March 2025, was found in exactly this territory: the gap between platform features and the configurations enterprises actually run.
Builders are multiplying, and some of them are agents
The platforms have made agent creation as accessible as making a slide deck. Marketing operations builds an agent to pull pipeline reports. Finance builds one to reconcile invoices. Each rides its creator's permissions, because that is what makes it useful. Shadow AI was an employee pasting data into a chatbot. Shadow agents are that employee's access, running unattended, multiplied across everything they were ever granted.
Increasingly, agents also build agents. A coding agent tagged into a chat channel can scaffold and deploy another agent as easily as it opens a pull request; an orchestration platform spins up sub-agents to divide a task, each with its own connections and none with its own review. Any governance model that assumes a human requested each agent is quietly obsolete.
Why governance keeps producing a document
Ask a large enterprise about agent governance and the answer is usually a document: an acceptable-use policy, a monthly committee, a set of principles nobody disputes and nothing enforces. Ask the operational question, how many agents are running right now, what can they reach, and who owns each one, and the document does not know.
The OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 now describes the sharpest version of this gap under its "No Governance" category: a skill deployed and managed inside a third-party platform is unreachable by external scanners (OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 whitepaper, ast10-top10-whitepaper-2, published at owasp.github.io). The tools an enterprise points at the problem from outside cannot see inside the venues where most agents live. Governance fails most often because the rules get written before the security team can see the things the rules apply to.
The stack, bottom-up, with a test for each layer
The working order is bottom-up, and each layer is the precondition for the one above it. A practical way to check whether a program is real is to apply an operational test at each level.
| Layer | What it has to produce | The operational test | 
| Discovery | A continuously refreshed population across app configs, OAuth grants, network, endpoint, email metadata, and browser | Is the discovered count several multiples of the list IT keeps? If not, discovery isn't reaching where agents live. | 
| Posture | Every platform's agent-relevant settings, measured against how they should be configured | Can the team list the intake features and guest-user exposures wired to agent triggers on its top three platforms? | 
| Identity and ownership | An identity and a named owner per agent, with a lifecycle | Pick an agent at random. Does a human raise a hand within a day when asked "whose is this?" | 
| Usage | Who is building what, through which surface, with what data | Is there a sanctioned path that ships a business team's agent with secure defaults, or only a block? | 
| Agent controls | Least privilege against observed need, approval and quarantine for new agents, risk tiering that reflects each agent's full context | Does the same finding on a sandboxed dev agent and a customer-facing one show different severities? | 
| Runtime | Live inspection and intervention | Is it fed by the five layers above, or deployed first and enforcing blind? | 
The cost of paper compliance
The EU AI Act's penalties carry GDPR-level weight: up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover for prohibited practices, up to €15 million or 3% for other violations. Every framework converging on it assumes the stack above exists. GDPR already showed what happens when it does not. British Airways (£20 million) and Marriott (£18.4 million) were not fined for having imperfect policies. Everyone has imperfect policies. They were fined because compliance existed on paper and could not be evidenced operationally when regulators asked. A governance practice built bottom-up generates that evidence as a byproduct: the inventory, the owners, the configurations, the review history.
Some platforms are designed to produce exactly that record. One leading example is Reco, which discovers agents across multiple vantage points, including the ones that never touch SSO, and assigns each a risk profile before any policy can be applied to it.
The Agentforce chain at the top of this article is not an exploit. It is a configuration, and configurations are governable, provided someone can see them. Chapters 1 to 3 of Into the Expanse cover the shift, the three launch vectors, and the governance practice in full: https://www.reco.ai/agent-ecosystem-security

articles.title: Office, Defender, Copilot… Microsoft dans le viseur du Royaume-Uni pour ses logiciels trop bien intégrés
articles.text:
Le régulateur britannique estime que Microsoft tire un avantage considérable de l'intégration de ses logiciels professionnels. Après cinq mois d'enquête, il envisage des interventions qui pourraient concerner Copilot, Defender et les offres commerciales du groupe.
La Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), qui avait ouvert en mai dernier une enquête sur les pratiques de Microsoft susceptibles de limiter la concurrence sur le marché des logiciels professionnels, vient de franchir une nouvelle étape. L'autorité britannique de la concurrence propose de placer l'entreprise sous un régime de surveillance renforcée, estimant que les liens techniques et commerciaux entre ses produits compliquent le recours à des solutions concurrentes. Si cette proposition aboutit, Microsoft pourrait être contrainte d'ouvrir davantage ses logiciels aux éditeurs tiers et de revoir certaines de ses offres groupées, notamment autour de Copilot et Defender.
Une intégration qui décourage la concurrence
Pour parvenir à cette conclusion, la CMA s'est intéressée à la manière dont Microsoft tire parti de sa position sur plusieurs marchés, des systèmes d'exploitation aux suites bureautiques, en passant par la cybersécurité et les logiciels pour serveurs. Dans les entreprises, l'utilisation de plusieurs produits Microsoft facilite leur déploiement, leur administration et leur sécurisation depuis un environnement commun. Un avantage pratique auquel s'ajoutent les remises accordées aux clients qui regroupent leurs licences, rendant les offres de l'éditeur particulièrement intéressantes.
Mais plus une entreprise s'équipe chez Microsoft, plus il peut lui coûter de choisir un autre fournisseur. Remplacer un logiciel peut lui faire perdre des réductions négociées sur l'ensemble de ses licences, tandis que les fonctionnalités déjà comprises dans ses abonnements rendent les solutions concurrentes moins attractives. C'est notamment le cas de Defender, dont la présence dans les offres Microsoft 365 peut décourager le recours à un autre éditeur de cybersécurité.
À ces avantages commerciaux s'ajoutent des difficultés techniques, plusieurs concurrents dénonçant un accès moins complet aux données, aux API ou aux fonctions internes des logiciels Microsoft, qui limite les possibilités d'intégration de leurs propres produits. Un déséquilibre dont pourrait également profiter Copilot sur le marché de l'intelligence artificielle, grâce à son intégration directe dans les applications Microsoft 365.
La CMA envisage donc d'imposer un accès plus équitable aux données et aux fonctionnalités des logiciels Microsoft, aussi bien pour les éditeurs de cybersécurité que pour les fournisseurs d'assistants IA. Elle pourrait également faciliter le choix d'un autre assistant par défaut, demander la commercialisation séparée de certaines fonctions de Copilot et revoir les conditions de licence de Windows Server et SQL Server, qui peuvent pénaliser les entreprises préférant un hébergeur concurrent d'Azure.
Teams, un précédent européen aux résultats limités
Pour rappel, Microsoft a déjà été amenée à revoir ses offres groupées en Europe. En septembre 2025, elle s'était engagée auprès de la Commission européenne à commercialiser Office 365 et Microsoft 365 sans Teams, à des tarifs inférieurs, et à améliorer leur interopérabilité avec les services concurrents.
Mais un an plus tard, ces concessions semblent avoir eu peu d'effet sur les habitudes de travail des entreprises. La séparation des licences n'a pas entraîné de migration significative vers les concurrents de Teams, les organisations continuant de privilégier son intégration à Office et les investissements déjà réalisés dans l'environnement Microsoft.
Les autorités britanniques pourraient désormais aller plus loin que la seule séparation des licences, en intervenant directement sur les conditions techniques et commerciales qui entretiennent cette dépendance. Pour cela, la CMA propose d'attribuer à Microsoft le statut de Strategic Market Status (SMS), prévu par la législation britannique sur les marchés numériques. Cette désignation ne constituerait pas une condamnation, mais permettrait d'imposer ultérieurement des obligations ciblées, après de nouvelles procédures. La consultation publique est ouverte jusqu'au 13 novembre, avant une décision définitive attendue au plus tard le 13 février 2027.

articles.title: Pasos para canjear los códigos de Free Fire este 19 de octubre de 2026: gana diamantes gratis
articles.text:
Garena habilitó una nueva ronda de códigos de Free Fire para este lunes 19 de octubre de 2026. Las combinaciones permiten a los jugadores con cuentas registradas intentar reclamar premios dentro del videojuego, entre ellos diamantes, trajes, skins de armas, cajas y otros objetos de disponibilidad limitada.
El acceso a cada beneficio depende de la región de la cuenta, la vigencia de la clave y los cupos de canje disponibles. Por ese motivo, conviene ingresar los códigos cuanto antes y utilizar únicamente el portal oficial de recompensas de Garena, que evita problemas de validación y riesgos de seguridad.
Cuáles son los códigos de Free Fire disponibles este 19 de octubre de 2026
La lista para la jornada incluye más de 15 combinaciones. Cada una debe copiarse como aparece, en mayúsculas y sin espacios antes o después de la secuencia. Un carácter incorrecto puede impedir que el sistema acepte el código.
- H8YC4TN6VKQ9.
- FP9O1I5U3Y2T.
- 6KWMFJVMQQYG.
- FE2R8T6Y4U1I.
- B1RK7C5ZL8YT.
- FQ9W2E1R7T5Y.
- FU1I5O3P7A9S.
- FT4E9Y5U1I3O.
- FFR4G3HM5YJN.
- F7F9A3B2K6G8.
- FA3S7D5F1G9H.
- FM6N1B8V3C4X.
- UPQ7X5NMJ64V.
- 4ST1ZTBZBRP9.
- BR43FMAPYEZZ.
- FF6YH3BFD7VT.
- FK3J9H5G1F7D.
- S9QK2L6VP3MR.
- FZ5X1C7V9B2N.
Las claves pueden tener restricciones territoriales y un número limitado de usos. Por esa razón, que una combinación figure en la lista no garantiza que funcione para todas las cuentas ni que entregue el mismo objeto a todos los usuarios.
Dónde se ingresan los códigos de recompensa de Free Fire
El canje se realiza en el sitio oficial reward.ff.garena.com. El jugador debe acceder desde un navegador, iniciar sesión y seleccionar el método de vinculación que corresponda a la cuenta utilizada habitualmente en Free Fire.
El portal admite perfiles asociados con Google, Facebook, Apple, Huawei o VK. La vinculación previa es necesaria para que el premio llegue al perfil correcto. Las cuentas de invitado no pueden utilizar el sistema hasta que queden enlazadas con una de las plataformas habilitadas.
Cuál es el proceso para reclamar diamantes y otros premios
Después de iniciar sesión, el usuario debe localizar el campo de canje, pegar o escribir una de las claves y confirmar la solicitud. Si el código continúa activo, tiene cupos disponibles y es válido en la región de la cuenta, la página mostrará un mensaje de confirmación.
Las recompensas pueden tardar hasta 24 horas en aparecer en el buzón interno del juego. Para comprobar la acreditación, el jugador debe abrir Free Fire con el mismo perfil que vinculó en el portal. Si el objeto no aparece de inmediato, conviene esperar ese plazo antes de repetir la operación con otra clave.
Qué significa el mensaje de código de Free Fire es inválido o expirado
El aviso “código inválido o expirado” indica que la combinación ya no puede utilizarse. Puede ser porque venció el período de activación, se agotaron los canjes disponibles o la clave no está habilitada para la región desde la cual se intentó validarla.
Además, puede tratarse de un error de escritura. Los códigos combinan letras y números que pueden parecerse entre sí, como la letra O y el número 0, o la letra I y el número 1. Antes de realizar un segundo intento, es clave revisar cada carácter y eliminar posibles espacios añadidos al copiar la secuencia.
Cuáles recompensas pueden otorgar los códigos de Garena en el juego
Los diamantes gratis se encuentran entre los beneficios más buscados porque permiten adquirir artículos en la tienda virtual de Free Fire. Con esta moneda, los jugadores pueden acceder a elementos estéticos, pases, accesorios y otros contenidos que forman parte de las campañas disponibles dentro del juego.
Asimismo, las claves pueden habilitar trajes, skins de armas, personajes, emotes, cajas y objetos coleccionables. El premio final depende de cada código y de la campaña activa, así que no todas las combinaciones otorgan diamantes ni entregan el mismo contenido a todos los perfiles.
En aniversarios, fechas conmemorativas y eventos especiales, Garena suele incorporar artículos temáticos que no forman parte del catálogo habitual. En esos casos, los códigos incluyen prendas, accesorios y otros objetos vinculados con una campaña puntual.

articles.title: Tactful AI attracts fresh investment from Hatem Dowidar ahead of 2027 Series A
articles.text: Egypt-based AI startup Tactful AI has secured an undisclosed investment from Hatem Dowidar, former Group CEO of e&, as part of an extension to its pre-Series A round , initially announced in February 2026 and co-led by Foras AI and M Empire. Founded in 2016 by Mohamed Elmasry and Mohamed Hassan, Tactful AI develops an agentic AI-powered customer experience platform that enables businesses to manage customer interactions, automate workflows and analyse conversations across multiple channels. The company is preparing to introduce next-generation agentic AI technology that will allow enterprises to build and modify customer experience workflows in hours rather than months while maintaining human oversight and approval processes. The investment comes as Tactful AI, which operates teams in Cairo and Cambridge, UK, prepares to launch its next-generation platform and pursue a Series A funding round in 2027. Press release: Tactful AI, a startup specialising in agentic AI-driven customer experience (CX) infrastructure, announced that Hatem Dowidar, former Group CEO of e&, has joined its investor roster through a direct investment in the company's Pre-Series A extension round. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. The move comes as Tactful AI prepares to roll out its next leap in Agentic AI technology—a shift expected to serve as a crucial inflection point for enterprise capability, operational agility, and proactive market responsiveness. Dowidar brings a quarter-century track record in telecommunications and technology. He served as Group CEO of e& from 2020 through March 2026, having joined the company as Chief Operating Officer in 2015. Prior to e&, Dowidar spent 16 years in executive leadership roles at Vodafone, including CEO of Vodafone Egypt. Commenting on the investment, Mohamed Elmasry, Co-founder and CEO of Tactful AI, said: "Hatem Dowidar spent over 25 years leading major tech powerhouses serving millions of customers across the Middle East and Africa. Very few leaders share his depth of understanding and strategic clarity regarding what large enterprises require before trusting new, customer-facing technologies. His support and trust come at a pivotal moment as we take our boldest step yet toward defining a new era of agentic AI-driven customer experience." Hatem Dowidar added: "Enterprises across the region are actively seeking practical, reliable solutions to integrate AI into their customer operations safely and at scale. Tactful has successfully deployed this infrastructure in live production environments. Seeing the capabilities of their next-generation technology convinced me that this team has everything it takes to set the industry benchmark, both regionally and globally." While most current AI applications remain limited to answering routine queries, Tactful AI’s next-generation technology bridges this gap by addressing a core enterprise challenge: building, modifying, and evolving end-to-end CX workflows directly within the enterprise. This approach compresses development cycles from months to hours while maintaining human-in-the-loop oversight and sign-offs at every step. The company plans to reveal further technical details in the coming months. The upcoming technology builds on a unified infrastructure already proven in live production, driving rapid growth. The platform seamlessly integrates engagement, orchestration, governance, analytics, advanced automation, and agentic AI. This technical momentum is reflected in the company's financial performance since January 2025: Tactful AI recorded an 11.7x increase in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) and a 32x surge in monthly customer conversations processed through the platform. Its client portfolio includes Elaraby Group, Raneen, 2B, Lucky One, Erada Finance, and Simplex. This extension follows Tactful AI’s initial Pre-Series A round announced in February 2026, co-led by Foras AI and M Empire. The company aims to build on this investor momentum as it prepares for a Series A funding round in 2027.

articles.title: Why the $649 Mac mini M4 is a smarter buy than Apple’s new M6
articles.text:
Before spending more on Apple's latest Mac mini M6, take a look at the M4 model with $150 off at Best Buy
A 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU provide plenty of performance
The Apple Mac mini has been one of our favorite mini PCs since we first tried it out, with the M4 model. Now, Apple has launched the new M6-powered model, but before you jump in, I still think the M4 edition is worth checking out for general desktop PC duties like running office software, and content creation.
For a very limited time, the Mac mini M4 is down to the $649 (was $799) at Best Buy - a full $150 cheaper than the Mac mini M6 over at Amazon. The diminutive Mac mini M4, released in 2024, packs impressive performance into a tiny 5 x 5-inch design at a price that makes it worth considering over the newer M6 model.
• Best for: Home and office workers, students, and anyone who wants a compact Mac for everyday computing, photo editing, and occasional video projects.
• Why it matters: You get a 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16GB of unified memory, and 256GB SSD for $130.99 less than the newer M6 Mac mini at Amazon.
Today's best Apple Mac mini (M4) deal
This compact desktop features an Apple M4 chip with 10-core CPU and GPU, 16GB unified memory, 256GB SSD, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, Gigabit Ethernet, and Apple Intelligence support.
Why we recommend it
In his 5-star review of Mac mini M4, our expert Matt said: "Before Apple announced its new M4-series Macs and MacBooks I made a prediction that the Mac mini would be the most interesting out of all of them — and I was right. Apple has made what was already the best small form factor PC even better thanks to a more compact design, and it packs the new M4 and M4 Pro chips — all while offering incredible value for money as well. I can't recommend this Mac enough."
The Apple Mac mini M4 might be small, but its 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU are certainly mighty and provide plenty of processing power. You also get 16GB of unified memory, and a 256GB SSD. There are three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, Gigabit Ethernet, and two front-facing USB-C ports. You can also connect up to three external displays.
We rank it as the best mini PC for Apple users. And because this is an Apple silicon Mac, it supports Apple Intelligence, so you don't need the latest M6 model to access Apple's AI features.
Price context & historical value
Best Buy is selling the M4 Mac mini for $649, saving you $150 off the usual $799 price. Alternatively, Amazon has the newer M6 Mac mini for $779.99, down from $899, saving you $119.01, or approximately 13%.
Both models have 16GB of unified memory and a 256GB SSD, but the M6 offers a faster 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, compared with the M4's 10-core CPU and GPU. It also has Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and 2.5Gb Ethernet, compared with Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3, and Gigabit Ethernet on the M4.
At just $130.99 more, the M6 could be worth the extra money if you regularly edit videos, work with demanding applications, or plan to keep your Mac for several years. That said, the discounted M4 model remains a very capable and more affordable mini Mac.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Mac mini M4 if...
You want a compact Apple desktop for everyday computing, office work, photo editing, and occasional video projects. It offers 16GB of memory, excellent connectivity, and access to the macOS ecosystem for less than the newer M6.
❌ Skip the Mac mini M4 if...
You regularly edit demanding video projects, work with complex graphics, or run local AI applications. The M6's faster CPU, GPU, and AI hardware could justify paying extra. I'd also consider the M6 if you want the latest wireless connectivity and faster Ethernet.
Also consider
This compact desktop features Apple's M6 chip with 12-core CPU and GPU, 16GB unified memory, 256GB SSD, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and 2.5Gb Ethernet connectivity.
