articles.title: Cuántos dólares necesito para comprar un Tesla Roadster que vuela de Elon Musk
articles.text:
Tesla impresionó con la nueva generación de su Roadster en el centro de ensayos de SpaceX en McGregor, Texas, con una demostración en la que el deportivo eléctrico subió una pared, circuló boca abajo y aterrizó en el aire con propulsores propios, como si estuviera volando.
Nueve años después de aquel primer prototipo de 2017, Elon Musk confirmó una fecha de producción (2028) y reabrió las reservas, aunque el auto sigue sin un precio de venta definitivo.
Cuánto cuesta reservar el Tesla Roadster
Tesla no ha revelado el precio final de ninguna de las versiones del Roadster. Lo que sí publicó son los montos para reservar las dos configuraciones pensadas para circular por carretera.
La versión Performance exige un depósito de 50.000 dólares, divididos en 5.000 dólares el día de la presentación y otros 45.000 dólares dentro de los diez días siguientes, bajo riesgo de cancelación.
La versión Thrust, con propulsores adicionales para mejorar la aceleración, requiere un anticipo de 250.000 dólares, con el mismo esquema de pago inicial y un saldo de 245.000 dólares en diez días. Esta reserva está limitada a un pedido por cliente.
La versión Rocket, la más extrema, no tiene reserva pública: solo se ofrece por invitación directa de la compañía, sin precio anunciado.
El monto pedido para el Performance equivale a la misma cifra que Tesla solicitó en 2017, cuando el precio de acceso proyectado para el Roadster original era de 200.000 dólares, una cotización que ya no es vigente para el modelo de 2026.
El contrato de reservación en México, según la página oficial de Tesla, data de 2017 y aclara que el pago solo otorga una prioridad aproximada de entrega, no la compra del vehículo. El precio final, impuestos y aranceles se definirán en un acuerdo de compra posterior, y la empresa no paga intereses sobre los anticipos ni los resguarda en una cuenta de garantía independiente.
Cuándo estará a la venta el Tesla Roadster
Musk fijó el inicio de la producción en 2028, sin precisar fecha de entrega para quienes reserven el vehículo. El proyecto acumula un historial de aplazamientos: Tesla presentó la segunda generación del Roadster en noviembre de 2017 con una fecha de entrega prevista para 2020, que nunca se cumplió.
Solo este año, la presentación del nuevo modelo se postergó de abril a finales de abril, luego a agosto y al 1 de octubre, hasta concretarse el 15 de octubre en el evento de SpaceX.
Musk reconoció anteriormente, según recogió la agencia Reuters, que el Roadster no representa un proyecto determinante para los resultados financieros de Tesla y que su función principal es demostrar capacidades tecnológicas de la compañía.
Las características del Roadster: de los propulsores al interior
El Roadster que vuela es, en rigor, solo la versión Rocket. Tesla anunció que esta variante monoplaza pasa de 0 a 60 millas por hora (97 km/h) en menos de 0,59 segundos y supera los 370 km/h de velocidad máxima, aunque aclaró que no está homologada para circular por la vía pública.
El Performance biplaza promete hacer esa misma aceleración en menos de 1,6 segundos, mientras que el Thrust, pensado para circuito, la completa en menos de 0,9 segundos. Las tres versiones comparten una autonomía superior a 300 millas (483 kilómetros), cifra que representa un recorte de aproximadamente el 50% respecto a los cerca de 1.000 kilómetros que Tesla había prometido en 2017.
La propulsión vertical funciona con gas frío desarrollado junto con SpaceX: aire comprimido almacenado en depósitos de fibra de carbono que, según la compañía, genera entre cuatro y cinco veces la fuerza que pueden transmitir los neumáticos.
En paralelo, un sistema de ventiladores de succión bajo la carrocería sella los laterales inferiores del coche y genera una fuerza de adherencia que Tesla compara con la de un Fórmula 1, suficiente para mantener el vehículo pegado al suelo incluso boca abajo.
El diseño abandona las formas del prototipo de 2017 para adoptar el lenguaje del Cybertruck, con carrocería plana, pintura gris y faros ocultos, en una estética que la empresa vincula con los aviones SR-71 y F-35. El interior incorpora un volante en forma de yugo, asiento fijo y materiales como magnesio, titanio y fibra de carbono, pensados para reducir peso.

articles.title: 'The GPU never reads the same text twice': Belgian startup Corbenic wants to turn your server's SSD into AI memory, but its 14x speedup owes more to reading less
articles.text:
'The GPU never reads the same text twice': Belgian startup Corbenic wants to turn your server's SSD into AI memory, but its 14x speedup owes more to reading less
Galahad promises exact, encrypted KV cache reuse for vLLM, SGLang, and Llama.cpp
- Corbenic AI's Galahad beta saves a model's KV cache to encrypted local NVMe so servers can skip rereading text after GPU memory is cleared or after a restart
- Founder Sietse Schelpe tells TechRadar Pro no special hardware is needed, but the paper credits most of the 14x speedup to Blaise, a retrieval component, not SSD loading
- LMCache, Nvidia Dynamo and CMX, WEKA and Phison already persist KV cache to storage; Galahad's edge is exact, fail-closed reuse in one small library
Belgian startup Corbenic AI says it can stop GPUs from rereading documents they have already processed, and its founder told TechRadar Pro the trick needs nothing more exotic than the NVMe drive already sitting in the server.
Galahad, which entered beta on October 1 2026, saves a model's key-value (KV) cache, the attention state built while a model reads a prompt, to encrypted local storage and reloads it the next time the same text appears.
In an email to TechRadar Pro, Corbenic introduced Galahad with the line "the GPU never reads the same text twice," and founder and CEO Sietse Schelpe summed it up as "the SSD a server already has becomes part of the AI's working memory."
Catering to a market with plenty of alternatives in tow
The timing of Corbenic's announcement is impeccable; with data centers on course to absorb more than 70% of high-end memory chips in 2026, getting more work out of existing hardware is an easy sell. But Corbenic's own paper shows its headline 14x speedup owes more to reading less text than to loading saved work, and the company is walking into a field where Nvidia, Phison, and a well-funded open source project already offer something similar.
Galahad's approach is slightly different: In standard serving, a model answering a second question about a document recomputes that document's attention state from the first token, a step called prefill. Engines such as vLLM and SGLang already reuse that state while it sits in GPU memory, but Corbenic's paper notes it is evicted under memory pressure and lost whenever the process restarts.
Galahad's KV component, Taliesin, writes each block of text's state to disk under a fingerprint of the exact input bytes, the model, and the tenant, then loads it when those bytes reappear.
Schelpe stressed that the stored copy only comes into play once GPU memory has been cleared or the server has restarted. "So the choice is not SSD or RAM. It is SSD or computing it all again on the GPU," he told TechRadar Pro, adding that the load "happens once, before the first word of the answer."
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
He volunteered two limits: short texts are not stored because recomputing them is already fast, and network storage is much slower than a local NVMe drive. The paper sets a fail-closed rule on top: "serve without memory, never with wrong memory," so any record that fails a check is simply recomputed.
No special hardware is required, according to Schelpe, just Linux, an Nvidia GPU and a standard NVMe SSD. Asked about CXL, he said, "we tried faster storage, and it didn't make Galahad faster," which matches the paper's H100 test, where a RAM disk and a local disk delivered near-identical throughput.
On enterprise drives such as Phison's Pascari line, whose maker has been pitching flash as the answer to AI's memory bottleneck, he was refreshingly careful: "we haven't measured them, so I won't quote numbers."
Schelpe told TechRadar Pro that loading stored state from a fast SSD "is much quicker" than rereading, and that "is where our 14× comes from: 0.59 seconds per question on vLLM." The paper's own tables tell a more complicated story.
The 0.59-second result comes from a recall test with 100 facts hidden in a 96,726-token list, run on Gemma 4 31B, and it used Taliesin plus Blaise. Blaise is a second component that keeps the documents as text and hands the model only the section a question needs, about 668 tokens instead of the whole corpus. The paper itself credits Blaise with lifting the gain on llama.cpp from 3.1x to 14.5x.
With Taliesin alone, vLLM took 15.56 seconds per question, slower than its 8.11-second baseline, and SGLang took 22.02 seconds against 10.29. Only llama.cpp got faster on KV reuse alone, at 3.01 seconds against 9.25. Those comparisons are lopsided in both directions: the baseline used a 12,000-token window that saw only the last 12% of the corpus and answered 10 of 100 questions, while Taliesin let the model attend to everything and answered 98 of 100.
Schelpe positions Galahad against retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines such as RAGFlow, which split documents into chunks and pass the model whichever pieces a search ranks highest. "When the search misses, the model never sees the answer," he said, citing a benchmark in which Galahad answered 100 of 100 questions and RAGFlow 77.
Asked by TechRadar Pro why nobody else had come up with the strategy, Schelpe said rivals had chased "bigger is better" and that "there is no real glory" in building something like this, adding that he was lucky not to carry the same mental baggage. Corbenic's homepage makes the same point with the slogan "Stop building bigger models. Build the layer below."
The premise does not hold up well. LMCache, an Apache 2.0 project with around 10,900 GitHub stars, already moves KV cache into CPU memory, local SSDs and remote storage, and a 2024 post on its blog pitched it as "letting LLMs read each text only once." Nine days before Galahad launched, Samsung engineers detailed a restart-recoverable NVMe tier for the project, and its commercial backer, Tensormesh, raised $20 million in May from investors including AMD Ventures, CoreWeave, and Nvidia's NVentures.
Nvidia's Dynamo framework tiers KV cache from GPU memory through host DRAM to local NVMe and networked storage, and at CES 2026 the company unveiled a BlueField-4 context memory platform, now called CMX, built to push KV cache onto NVMe SSDs. Nvidia has even argued that storage is the next frontier of AI. WEKA sells its Augmented Memory Grid for the same job, Huawei pitches a Unified Cache Manager to avoid repeat calculations, and Phison's aiDAPTIV+ already parks KV cache on flash in consumer laptops such as Thunderobot's AI Master M7000.
A security-centric play that still needs independent testing
Galahad's real distinction from most of its prolificly backed competition is narrower. Its paper cites LMCache and Mooncake directly and sets itself apart on exactness, with bit-identical logits as the acceptance test and any mismatch treated as a miss. "Exact, not approximate," Schelpe said, though that contrast lands hardest on techniques such as CacheBlend, which LMCache uses to reuse non-prefix chunks with selective recomputation, rather than on plain offloading.
Corbenic's launch release actually leads with security rather than speed, calling Galahad "a secure vault for working memory" that encrypts stored state, keeps each customer's data separate, and can record activity so developers can roll a server's saved memory back to an earlier point.
The concern behind the pitch is real; researchers showed at NDSS 2025 that KV cache sharing in vLLM and SGLang could let one user reconstruct another's prompts through a timing side channel, and Galahad's library counters that by refusing to start without a tenant identity and model fingerprint. Schelpe also stressed that data stays put: "There's no shared cache network, and nothing is sent to us."
On the flip side, Corbenic is a small Belgium-based team registered as a Delaware corporation, and every number in its main Galahad paper comes from experiments the founder ran himself on rented cloud GPUs, as the paper discloses. Raw logs are promised but not yet published, Blaise's selection method is withheld pending patents, and the papers are self-published arXiv preprints rather than peer-reviewed work.
Its competition includes both proprietary and open-source solutions, most of which have undergone far more testing and will likely see much broader adoption unless Galahad finds industry partners willing to integrate it.
None of that makes the idea wrong. Paying a GPU to reread the same contracts, manuals, and code on every request is a genuine waste, and Schelpe frames the contest sensibly when he calls "the real competitor: buying more GPUs." With memory and storage prices where they are, software that makes existing servers do more will find buyers, and he said early reactions have been positive, with "some nice requests and some learnings already."
What Galahad needs now is someone else's benchmark: a head-to-head with LMCache on the same Nvidia hardware, with each runtime's own prefix cache switched on, and Blaise's retrieval tested on documents it was not built around. Until then, the safest reading is that Galahad is a careful, exact take on KV persistence, and that its most eye-catching numbers come from reading less rather than remembering more.

Having built hundreds of gaming PCs and being an avid gamer in his spare time, Rahim tends to have stronger opinions about hardware than most. This is particularly on display when he gets his way with powerful, but minimalistic RGB builds even as Small Form Factor (SFF) PCs come a close second.

articles.title: How a FD calculator helps investors plan savings with ease
articles.text:
How a FD calculator helps investors plan savings with ease
Saving for life’s big goals? Start with an FD calculator: Bajaj Finance’s online tool lets you compare amounts, tenures, and payout options instantly, turning guesswork into clear savings plans.
Establishing a financial goal makes the process of saving a lot easier. If you plan to save well, you need to know the total amount you plan to save as well as the time frame for saving. Whether you want to save for a family event, pay for tuition, or renovate your home, you should be aware of the amount of money you want to save and the time frame.
A fixed deposit is a type of investment that guarantees you a fixed amount of return during the investment period. However, calculating returns manually can be a hassle. So, using Bajaj Finance's FD Calculator saves a lot of time and energy as it allows you to know your estimated returns in seconds based on your inputs. You can explore options before making the final investment.
Define your savings goal
The first crucial step in investing is to find out your investment's purpose. Knowing why you are making the investment will give you the desired amount you need to save and the time of retrieval for the money.
For example, if the amount required for a particular instance is Rs 3 lakh in three years, you can use the calculator
See how much your deposit may earn
The Bajaj Finance FD Calculator estimates your return after you provide the required inputs. These generally include the investment amount, investor category, tenure, and interest payout option.
The result shows the estimated interest earned and the expected maturity amount. This allows you to see how much of the final value comes from your original deposit and how much may come from interest.
The calculation also makes percentage rates easier to understand. An annual interest rate may appear attractive, but the calculator translates it into an estimated rupee value. This provides a more practical picture of how the investment could contribute towards your savings goal.
Choose an amount without affecting your budget
A larger amount will yield a higher maturity value, but putting in too much money could create issues when it's time to pay the bills. The right figure would give you the money you need to achieve your future goal.
Before making a fixed deposit, be sure to think about rent, bills, school tuition, medical expenses, and anything else that you must pay for in the near future.
The calculator allows you to compare various amounts almost instantly. Enter Rs 50,000, Rs 1 lakh, or any other amount and watch the maturity figure change accordingly.
Match the tenure with your goal date
Bajaj Finance’s fixed deposit scheme has time frames that range from 12 to 60 months. The applicable interest rate differs based on the time chosen, meaning changing the time can result in varied rates of return.
A longer period gives the deposit a longer opportunity to earn interest through the compound option, but maturity needs to happen close to the time of using the funds.
Suppose your goal is due after two years. Selecting a five-year deposit merely because it shows a larger maturity value could leave the funds unavailable at the required time. The FD interest Calculator lets you compare eligible tenures and select one that balances potential earnings with timely access.
How to use the FD calculator
The Bajaj Finance online calculator is designed to provide estimates quickly. You can repeat the calculation with different inputs and compare the results before starting the investment process.
- Choose the investor category: Select the relevant option for a customer below 60 or a senior citizen.
- Enter the deposit amount: Add the amount you are considering investing.
- Select the tenure: Choose an available period between 12 and 60 months.
- Pick the payout option: Select interest at maturity or a periodic payout frequency.
- Review the estimate: Check the estimated interest earnings and maturity amount.
- Try another combination: Change the amount, tenure, or payout option to compare the result.
Consider safety and access to your money
Return is only one aspect of FD planning. Credit ratings of the institution, conditions for early withdrawal, nomination facility, maturity instructions, and renewal options are some other aspects that must be evaluated as well.
Bajaj Finance Fixed Deposit comes with guaranteed returns and good credit safety ratings, with CRISIL AAA/STABLE and ICRA AAA (Stable). Minimum investment starts at Rs 15,000, making it possible to experiment with various amounts via the calculator before finalizing the exact amount.
Early withdrawals are allowed but require certain conditions to be met, which could lead to lower interest. Therefore, it is wise to select an amount and tenure you are fairly certain you will not deviate from.
Conclusion
Choosing the appropriate amount and period for a fixed deposit account can help you achieve short-term and medium-term savings objectives. The Bajaj Finance FD Calculator lets you know the returns that different fixed deposit accounts can bring.
It is useful to compare various investment scenarios involving the fixed deposit calculator and check information about current FD interest rates, tax rates, credit ratings, and penalties for early withdrawal of a fixed deposit.

articles.title: L’IA vous fait croire à des événements qui n’ont jamais existé
articles.text:
Quelques photos retouchées par IA, un faux résumé d’une vidéo d’accident, et des centaines de volontaires ont gardé en mémoire des détails inventés de toutes pièces. Dans l’une de ces expériences, les participants ont mal répondu au test en sachant très bien que le texte sortait d’une machine.
Pattie Maes, professeure au MIT Media Lab, a montré 24 photos banales à 200 volontaires, un mariage ou une course à pied par exemple. Après une pause, une partie du groupe a revu ces images retouchées par IA, parfois animées en vidéo, avec des expressions de visage modifiées ou des personnes ajoutées dans le décor. Au test de mémoire, ces volontaires ont produit jusqu’à deux fois plus de faux souvenirs que le groupe témoin, avec davantage d’assurance dans leurs erreurs. « Je considère tout cela comme très dangereux, fondamentalement », a confié la chercheuse. Avec ces résultats, son équipe et d’autres laboratoires remettent en cause le garde-fou retenu par l’Union européenne. Dans l’AI Act, un contrôleur humain doit repérer les erreurs de la machine.
L’AI Act confie la vérification à une mémoire influençable
Mattea Sim est professeure adjointe de recherche au Massive Data Institute de l’université de Georgetown. Elle a testé ce garde-fou avec des collègues de l’université de Washington. Leurs 331 volontaires ont regardé une courte animation où une voiture rouge tourne à un carrefour, puis renverse un piéton. Un à deux jours plus tard, chacun a lu un résumé de la scène, avec le bon panneau routier ou un panneau changé par les chercheurs. Les lecteurs du résumé exact ont retrouvé le panneau de la vidéo dans 83,6 % des cas, contre 44,8 % avec la version fausse. Une partie des participants savait que le texte venait d’une IA, et leurs réponses ont été tout aussi fausses. « L’IA est un nouveau moyen de diffuser de la désinformation », prévient Mattea Sim.
Les législateurs européens ont confié à ce contrôleur humain la surveillance des systèmes d’IA à haut risque, police comprise. D’après l’article 14 du règlement, ces contrôleurs doivent pouvoir ignorer ou inverser une sortie de la machine et connaître le biais d’automatisation. En clair, un contrôleur doit savoir qu’il risque de croire une IA trop vite. Les volontaires de Georgetown le savaient, et leur souvenir de l’accident a été modifié malgré tout.
Aux États-Unis, des services de police testent des résumés d’images de caméras-piétons générés par IA, et Mattea Sim veut étudier ces rapports. En Europe, les eurodéputés et les États membres ont repoussé ces obligations au 2 décembre 2027 pour les systèmes autonomes à haut risque, dans le recrutement ou la police.
Résumés de notifications et chatbots, vos souvenirs sous influence
Si vous lisez chaque jour le résumé d’un mail ou d’une réunion préparé par un assistant IA, vous êtes à la place des volontaires de Georgetown. Au MIT Media Lab, 54 personnes chargées d’écrire des dissertations ont servi de cobayes à une autre expérience. Celles qui écrivaient avec ChatGPT ont eu nettement plus de mal à citer des passages de leur texte, quelques minutes après l’avoir rendu.
Sous le nom de la BBC, des propriétaires d’iPhone ont ainsi lu en décembre 2024 un résumé d’Apple Intelligence avec l’annonce du suicide de Luigi Mangione. L’homme, accusé du meurtre du patron d’UnitedHealthcare, était bien vivant.
Des chercheurs du MIT et de l’université de Californie à Irvine ont fait interroger des témoins d’une vidéo de crime par un chatbot et ces témoins ont produit trois fois plus de faux souvenirs que le groupe sans interrogatoire. Une autre équipe a implanté chez des volontaires le souvenir de scandales politiques inventés, avec des textes ou des deepfakes, jusqu’à réduire leur intention de vote.
Avant de retenir un chiffre ou une citation lue dans un résumé, prenez le temps d’ouvrir le texte d’origine. Apple permet aussi de désactiver ces résumés dans les réglages de notifications, application par application.
L’équipe de Pattie Maes développe en parallèle Memoro et MemPal. Avec ces deux assistants de mémoire couplés à des appareils portables, les chercheurs veulent aider des personnes âgées à retrouver une conversation oubliée ou leurs clés.

articles.title: 50 muertos o 1.000 millones de dólares en daños: el listón que Anthropic quiere fijar para que el Gobierno pueda frenar un modelo de IA
articles.text:
Anthropic ha estado presentando entre bambalinas un borrador de proyecto de ley sobre la seguridad de los modelos de IA más punteros en el Capitolio, según el medio Politico. Desde luego no es frecuente que un laboratorio de IA intente redactar las normas de su propia industria. Pero lo que ha arqueado más de una ceja es que su propuesta fijaría un listón muy alto antes de que el gobierno pueda detener un modelo, concentrando ese poder en un solo departamento. Te contamos los detalles.
Work in progress. El Congreso en Estados Unidos está sopesando actualmente varias propuestas de seguridad de la IA, y Anthropic ha redactado un borrador con dos o tres cosas llamativas. Un portavoz de Anthropic declaraba a Politico que el proyecto de ley refleja el Marco de IA Avanzada de la empresa, que ha estado promoviendo entre los legisladores desde junio, y califica su contenido como "políticas sensatas sobre las que creemos que el Congreso debería actuar".
El umbral. Según comparte Politico, que ha tenido acceso al borrador, el gobierno podría bloquear el lanzamiento o uso de un modelo únicamente si este plantea un riesgo previsible e inminente de más de 1.000 millones de dólares en daños, o de causar la muerte o lesiones graves a más de 50 personas. El peligro también tendría que provenir de:
Cómo funcionaría. El medio cuenta que instituciones independientes, registradas en el Departamento de Comercio, evaluarían periódicamente a un laboratorio de IA y sus modelos frontera. Los laboratorios podrían pagarles, siempre y cuando el pago no dependa del resultado de la evaluación. Si un evaluador detecta un "riesgo inminente enumerado", debe comunicárselo al Departamento de Comercio en un plazo de 72 horas tras finalizar la evaluación. Tras ello, según apunta el medio, Comercio podría solicitar a un juez federal del Tribunal de Distrito que detenga el lanzamiento de un modelo. Tom's Hardware añade que Comercio tendría que presentar sus pruebas ante dicho juez, quien toma la decisión final.
Un solo organismo tiene el interruptor. Politico afirma que el texto prohíbe explícitamente a cualquier otro "departamento, agencia u oficial" suspender el desarrollo, despliegue o uso interno de un modelo. Así que si esto lo combinamos con el umbral que hemos explicado antes, convertiría al Departamento de Comercio en el único órgano ejecutivo para detener un modelo, y solo un tribunal puede ordenarlo.
UN VISTAZO A...
Más allá de quién tendría ese botón rojo, Politico cuenta que los laboratorios de IA tendrían que crear marcos de seguridad, publicar informes de transparencia para los nuevos modelos de frontera, proteger a los que denuncian sobre los problemas de seguridad de los modelos y notificar los incidentes críticos de seguridad al Departamento de Comercio.
Un momento delicado. Las preocupaciones sobre la seguridad de la IA se han intensificado tras varios incidentes destacados a lo largo de estos últimos meses, incluyendo el hackeo a Hugging Face por parte de cientos de agentes de OpenAI, o la irrupción de varios agentes de IA en webs gubernamentales, entre otros momentos complicados.
Politico añade que varios de los incidentes que surgieron este verano no se han traducido en bajas mortales o daños económicos superiores a 1.000 millones de dólares, por lo que desde el punto de vista del borrador compartido por Anthropic, esos incidentes no habrían superado ese umbral.
De momento es solo un borrador y Anthropic aún no ha respaldado formalmente ningún proyecto de ley específico en el Congreso. Tendremos que esperar para conocer si los legisladores ven ese umbral de los 1.000 millones de dólares y 50 víctimas como una medida de seguridad razonable. Viendo que la idea ha agitado en buena medida al sector, hay dudas.

articles.title: “On se croirait en pleine science-fiction” : des astronomes identifient la toute première étoile verte connue
articles.text:
“On se croirait en pleine science-fiction” : des astronomes identifient la toute première étoile verte connue
Jamais une étoile verte n'avait été signalée de façon crédible. Des chercheurs britanniques en tiennent une, un cadavre stellaire gavé des débris de ses anciennes planètes, et exhument au passage l'astre le plus rouge jamais recensé.
Orange pour les plus froides, blanches comme le Soleil, bleu pâle pour les plus chaudes : la couleur d'une étoile se lit d'ordinaire comme un thermomètre. Les naines blanches, ces résidus ultradenses que laissent les étoiles de type solaire en fin de vie, passaient pour suivre la même règle. Publiée le 15 octobre dans RAS Techniques and Instruments, une étude menée par Mark Hollands, de l'université de Warwick, bouscule ce dogme : vues de près, certaines brilleraient en rose, en cyan, en jaune, et l'une d'elles, WD J1330+6435, en vert.
Comment une naine blanche vire au vert
Aucune n'est assez proche pour livrer sa teinte à l'œil. L'équipe a donc passé leurs spectres au crible d'un modèle de la vision humaine, celui-là même qui sert à calibrer nos écrans.
Tout se joue dans la densité. L'atmosphère des naines blanches les plus froides avoisine celle de l'eau, des millions de fois celle de la surface solaire. Dans cette purée d'hélium, le moindre élément chimique absorbe une plage de couleurs démesurée. WD J1330+6435, autour de 4 000 °C, a englouti des fragments rocheux : son atmosphère, chargée de sodium et de calcium, gobe l'orange et le violet. Reste un vert chartreuse que l'étude chiffre même en hexadécimal, #D0FFB4.
	
Imaginez-vous debout sur une planète, levant les yeux vers une étoile verte. On se croirait en pleine science-fiction.
Une étoile saumon, et une majorité bien blanche
À l'autre bout du nuancier, WD J1011+2845, à 48 années-lumière, voit le carbone de son cœur remonter à sa surface. Ses molécules étouffent la lumière entre 400 et 600 nanomètres : un rose saumon profond, sans doute l'étoile la plus rouge connue.
Ces excentriques restent rares. Sur quelque 150 naines blanches situées à moins de 65 années-lumière, cinq seulement détonnent, soit environ une sur trente. La médiane, près de 6 800 kelvins, frôle le blanc de référence de nos moniteurs. Boris Gänsicke, professeur de physique à Warwick, tranche : "la naine blanche moyenne est vraiment blanche".
Mark Hollands espère que les prochains relevés spectroscopiques feront grimper le compteur, confie-t-il à CNN, "d'une ou deux naines blanches vertes à 10 ou 20".

articles.title: Anycubic's award-winning 3D printer hits all-time low pricing — Kobra X is an excellent, entry-level four-color printer that's now just $299.99 for Amazon Prime members
articles.text:
Anycubic's award-winning 3D printer hits all-time low pricing — Kobra X is an excellent, entry-level four-color printer that's now just $299.99 for Amazon Prime members
This innovative bedslinger scored 4.5/5 in our review in February and is usually $359.99.
Anycubic's Kobra X Multicolor 3D Printer is at the lowest price it's ever been since reaching retail availability. Prime members who head over to the Anycubic store on Amazon can now snag this well-reviewed device for just $299.99 for a limited time. The 17% or $60 off its MSRP makes the Kobra X a bargain, as it was highly praised as a contender in the entry-level four-color printer category by our reviewer earlier this year. It even won a coveted Tom's Hardware Editor's Choice award.
Though it may appear to be a Bambu Lab A1 clone at first glance, we praised the Kobra X for its multimaterial system, the ACE Gen 2, which is built directly into the toolhead. This is a great timesaver for prints with lots of color changes, and we calculated that on a four-color print with 776 color swaps, the Kobra X was a shocking 10 hours faster than the rival A1, despite similar printing speeds.
All-time low price
The Kobra X delivers fast, affordable multicolor printing without a complicated external AMS or premium price tag. It features a 260 x 260 x 260mm (10.23 x 10.23 x 10.23-inch) build volume, automatic + Z bed leveling, and a color touch screen.
The Anycubic Kobra X Multicolor 3D printer was launched earlier this year, with consumer shipments starting in late March / early April. We reviewed it in February and gave it a great score for its innovative ACE Gen 2 system, fast filament swaps, and reliable 49-point full-auto leveling and vibration compensation. It also "worked flawlessly" throughout the testing period. The only stain on its glowing report card was due to the spool holder guide making loading awkward.
This 600mm/s 3D printer expands up to 19 colors if combined with four ACE 2 Pro units. It also packs a 720P camera with real-time monitoring and instant error alerts, plus AI-driven anti-foreign object and spaghetti detection, and reasonably quiet operation at ≤48 dB.
Now at its lowest price to the public since launch, at just $299.99, this Bambu Lab A1 rival is a compelling choice for 260 x 260 x 260mm (10.23 x 10.23 x 10.23-inch) build volume projects in PLA/PETG/TPU/PVA/PLA-CF/PETG-CF/ASA materials.

articles.title: Even Realities G2s are my new daily smartglasses; the R1 ring is clutch
articles.text:
I’ve really been on a smart glasses kick, but among the many I’ve tried out, the Even Realities’ Even G2 is among the best. These cameraless smart glasses keep privacy in mind and offer two displays on each lens. The Even G2 paired with the R1 smart ring makes for a pair that I really enjoy, as it keeps my interactions with the smart glasses very discreet. Though the pair aren’t without some faults, the Even G2 and R1 ring are honestly great.
One Ring
The Even G2s look stylish; you can barely tell there’s anything different about them. The temple tips by your ear are a bit thicker than usual, but that’s pretty much the only indicator they might be smart glasses. The glasses are slim and light, weighing only 36g; you’d forget they’re smart glasses if not for the displays. Seriously, I’ve had people be shocked to know I’m wearing smart glasses. And if these had cameras, maybe that’d be a problem, but they don’t, so no issue here.
I could see the Even R1 smart ring being too thick for some women. It’s a pretty thick ring, but I didn’t mind it at all. There’s a flat part of the ring with an ‘E,’ and my finger naturally gravitates towards it, playing with the ring all the time. The flat part doesn’t control the ring or anything, but indicates the correct placement of the ring on the charging stand and helps you dive into the R1 a little more. The smart ring is able to navigate your smart glasses with different gestures. Below the E on the ring, you’ll see dots indicating where you’re supposed to touch. The different gestures include a single tap, a double tap, and a double tap that you hold on the second tap, and you’ll swipe up and down.
Discreet
The screens on the lenses aren’t very evident; people can’t ever tell I’m reading my HUD. Well, until they realize I’m not making eye contact because I’m reading a lengthy text message — or a literal book. Often, people can’t even tell I’m wearing smart glasses; even other journalists and creators in tech who have used the glasses themselves take a moment or two to realize I’m wearing the G2 glasses. Even I don’t always clock when people are wearing the glasses; like in this picture of George Clooney at the Venice International Film Festival, it took me a moment to realize that the star was wearing the smart glasses.
The Even Realities G2 two panels can do a variety of things. Whenever I put on my smart glasses in the morning, I’m greeted by my dashboard that offers the time, date, and the battery percentage of the smart ring and glasses in the top left corner. The bottom left corner shows the temperature, sunset, and the forecast for the following day. The right side shows my calendar for the day, but by swiping on the ring or the temple tips, I can see upcoming tasks and my steps, calories, sleep score, heart rate (beats per minute), and my O2 — based on data provided by the smart ring. Of course, this is all customizable and based on what you want to see. Other widgets include the news, stocks and quick notes.
A double tap — one short, one long — opens a menu which shows notifications, conversate, teleprompter, translate, Even AI, photos and books. This menu can also be customized, and you can add a lot more plugins as well, including one for navigation, one to play chess, and even add the Bible. Books and Photos weren’t there by default either; I added them.
Conversate
While checking your notifications is always useful, my favourite feature is ‘Conversate.’ Conversate writes down all the words being said, kind of like subtitles. I always feel like I have difficulty hearing people around me, so giving everyone subtitles helps. And Conversate offers insight into what’s being said; for instance, the first time I used the feature, I had a family member in the hospital and while Conversate offered subtitles, when I asked my cousin why she needed her sodium up before surgery, a pop-up indicator appeared. To my surprise, the indicator explained why someone would need more sodium in their blood before surgery. It offers a lot of details, pretty much about anything anyone is talking about. I had someone sort of give me an astronomy lesson, and it was able to correct some of the information he was talking about — a single year on Venus is 29.5 Earth years, not 33 years — and even while at church, when the preacher said a bible scripture, the smart glasses showed the verses.
Other cool features include a teleprompter; I haven’t needed to use it yet, but I’ve tried it out, and I can see how it’s very helpful, especially if I’m saying lines in front of the camera. And I had my partner speak with me in Spanish, and I could understand clearly what he was saying. Even Realities’ Even AI can answer any and every question; you can even set it for continuous listening, so it can listen for follow-up questions. You can summon the AI with the phrase “Hey Even,” and it works in English and French, among other languages.
Some of the downsides
The Even Realities G2s aren’t perfect, though. Sometimes, I find the R1 ring a little finicky, and it takes a few swipes before it registers. I’ve had issues with the ring connecting a couple of times, but it’s not a constant problem. Randomly, I’ve seen “ring disconnected”; check it, and it’s already connected again.
This one is a me-thing, but even though the G2s are IP65 water-resistant, I’m always worried about the smart glasses getting wet in the rain or if I’m going to sweat too much and damage them. Another me-thing, but I needed to remind myself to silence my smart glasses before playing badminton because I got a shuttlecock to the forehead when I looked up, saw my dashboard and couldn’t see the birdie anymore.
And unfortunately, the price tag is a bit of a con. The Even Realities G2s are US$599 (C$846) and the R1 smart ring is US$249 (C$352), and this is before including your prescription lenses.

articles.title: UCLA researchers built a $400 humanoid robot around cheap phone technology
articles.text:
PhoneBot uses an old $50 Android smartphone brain with its cameras as eyes — tech Frankenstein is an open source humanoid robot platform for makers
PhoneBot tracks people by turning its phone camera without rotating its feet
- PhoneBot uses cheap Android smartphones for vision, sensing, and walking control
- UCLA researchers built a humanoid robot with approximately $400 in hardware
- Four Android phones handled PhoneBot’s core sensing and computing tasks
Researchers at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), have developed PhoneBot, a compact humanoid robot that reuses cheap smartphones for sensing and computing.
The open source platform costs approximately $400 for its robotic hardware, excluding the phone, making it considerably cheaper than several existing small humanoid research systems.
PhoneBot stands 483 mm tall, weighs 1.8 kg, and uses 13 servo motors to control its legs and rotating torso during movement.
Old smartphones handle vision, computing and robot control
Instead of requiring dedicated cameras, motion sensors and an expensive onboard computer, PhoneBot relies on the smartphone's existing hardware for these functions.
Its camera tracks people, while the built-in inertial measurement unit supplies motion information that helps the robot maintain balance and execute learned walking movements.
A separate computer inside the robot handles motor communications, receiving wireless commands from the smartphone over Wi-Fi and translating them into joint movements.
The robot has six actuated joints per leg, covering the hips, knees, and ankles, alongside another joint that rotates the torso and mounted smartphone.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This arrangement lets the camera turn toward people without requiring the robot to rotate its entire body, supporting tracking and other vision-based interactions.
The researchers tested four Android phones, including an older Honor 9 released in 2017 and three inexpensive handsets costing approximately $50 to $80.
All four devices supported the application's core functions, including motion sensing, walking control, visual detection and human interaction, although certain features differed between models.
The application runs locomotion policies through TensorFlow Lite, while the phone's camera supports person detection and pose estimation, alongside other perception functions.
Training helps balance walking and reduces hardware costs
The team trained PhoneBot's walking controller using reinforcement learning in simulation, rewarding desired movements while penalizing unstable posture and excessive motor loading.
Early experiments produced uneven walking patterns, with the robot relying disproportionately on one leg, prompting researchers to introduce mirrored training samples.
This method effectively teaches the controller using corresponding left and right movements, improving gait symmetry without requiring additional simulated physics steps.
Across five independent training runs, mirrored learning reduced joint-angle symmetry error from 0.254 radians to 0.003 radians during subsequent evaluations.
The researchers also measured left-right torque imbalance falling from 0.205 to 0.034, while mechanical-power imbalance declined from 0.339 to 0.040.
Physical demonstrations included walking, recovering from a face-down position, and directing the smartphone camera toward people without continuously turning the robot's feet.
PhoneBot remains limited by its low-powered servos, which restrict the weight it can carry and the dynamic movements it can perform reliably.
Its current walking controller was trained on flat ground, while the platform lacks arms for manipulating objects, leaving uneven-terrain mobility unresolved.
This is an open-source project so researchers can reproduce the platform, modify its components, and investigate smartphone-based robotics.
The research is currently published on arXiv, an online repository where researchers share scientific papers before or alongside formal peer-reviewed publication.

ORICO Enters Laptop Market With Obook 15 AI Laptop
ORICO, usually known for its storage and connectivity solutions, is officially entering the PC market with its first laptop design, the Obook 15 AI Laptop. For this initial design, the company has chosen AMD's Ryzen 7 6800H SoC, an eight-core, 16-thread mobile processor that can boost up to 4.7 GHz. The integrated Radeon 680M graphics handle visuals, and memory configurations include options of 12 GB or 24 GB running at 6,400 MT/s. The Obook 15 boasts a 15.6-inch IPS display with a 1,920 x 1,080 resolution, an anti-glare finish, 170-degree viewing angles, and wide-frequency dimming. It includes Wi-Fi 6, a 54.29 Wh battery, and a bundled 100 W charger. Additional features include a 180-degree hinge, a physical webcam shutter, a full-size keyboard with a number pad, and a wide selection of ports. ORICO lists US prices starting at $689.99 for the version with 12 GB of RAM and a 256 GB SSD. A 12 GB/512 GB version is priced at $749.99, while the top configuration with 24 GB of memory and 1 TB of storage costs $899.99. The Obook 15 is now available in the United States and the Philippines, targeting students, office users, and content creators with its attractive price points, especially for this day and age, amid memory and storage shortages.ORICO is also focusing on software as a key feature of the product. The included XiaoAo AI Super Agent combines 11 specialized AI assistants, which the company claims can help automate workflows, manage a knowledge base, and control devices remotely. articles.title: Review: Lanterns is a truly unique twist on the superhero genre
articles.text:
The trailers for HBO’s DC Universe series Lanterns teased a show that eschewed the usual superhero hijinks in favor of a gritty realism more in the vein of True Detectives or Slow Horses. Personally, I liked the change. My verdict: Ignore the review bombing; it’s wonderful. The season wrapped with an emotionally charged, almost elegaic finale that fully delivered on that initial promise. I’ve found the rebooted DC Universe films released thus far to be enjoyable but rather forgettable, even when the positives outweigh the negatives. But Lanterns is a shining beacon of what is possible when someone is allowed to get really creative within the genre.
(Spoilers below, but no major reveals.)
There are two primary storylines. The first takes place in 2016 with a mass shooting at a local football game in Rushville, Nebraska. Current Green Lantern Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and his new trainee, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), get involved in the investigation, to the annoyance of Sheriff Kerry Kane (Kelly Macdonald), who initially doesn’t think the case has any extraterrestrial connection. She is soon proved wrong when the suspect (an alien) self-detonates. Hal’s power ring controls the damage, but the mystery remains.
Hal and John soon discover that the suspect was one of a group of aliens who survived a genocide on their home planet committed by so-called Manhunters: a race of extraterrestrial beings created by the Guardians of the Universe as a forerunner to the Lantern Corps. The Manhunters rebelled against the Guardians, and most were killed; the sole survivor is hiding out in Rushville disguised as a human. The alien leader, Antaan (Paul Ben-Victor), gives Hal and John 48 hours to locate the Manhunter and hand them over, or they will destroy the town.
The second storyline takes place in 2026 and concerns the murder of none other than Hal Jordan, who returned to Rushville as a social pariah after the terrible events that transpired 10 years before. That mystery becomes the focus of the second half of the series, as Stewart teams up with the sheriff to solve Hal’s murder.
Green Lantern’s light
The entire cast brings their A game to their portrayals, and you couldn’t ask for better leads than Chandler and Pierre, both of whom have plenty of meaty, substantial material to work with. Showrunner Chris Mundy has said that one of the major themes of the show is deciding when it’s time for one person to step aside and let a replacement take over, embodied in the push and pull of Hal and John’s relationship. The two men are very different personalities: Hal is cocky, arrogant, and trusts his gut instincts; John is controlled, disciplined, logical, and methodical. Hal has no intention of giving up the power ring; John questions whether Hal really deserves it. Naturally they’re going to clash, and given the stakes, that conflict has severe consequences, both for them and the town.

articles.title: 9 Minuten Laden, 90 Minuten Arbeit: Neue Akkus sollen den Digits 5 zum echten Haushaltshelfer machen
articles.text:
9 Minuten Laden, 90 Minuten Arbeit: Neue Akkus sollen den Digits 5 zum echten Haushaltshelfer machen
Der humanoide Roboter Digit 5 von Agility Robotics hat eine besonders lange Laufzeit bei kurzem Aufladen. Die Batterietechnik dafür liefert das Unternehmen Nyobolt. Damit kommt der Roboter auf ein Verhältnis von Laufzeit zu Ladezeit von ungefähr 10:1. Für jede Minute an der Ladestation stehen also zehn Minuten Arbeit zur Verfügung. Lädt man neun Minuten, läuft der Humanoid 90 Minuten. Der Vorgänger Digit 4 schaffte lediglich ein Verhältnis von 2:1 – er verbrachte rund ein Drittel des Tages am Ladegerät.
Warum Akkus bei Humanoiden das Hauptproblem sind
Humanoide Roboter brauchen viel Strom. Weil sie sich frei bewegen sollen, kommt der aus Batterien. Die halten allerdings nicht lange und müssen regelmäßig nachgeladen oder getauscht werden. Agility Robotics setzt deshalb auf besonders leichte Akkus mit hoher Leistungsdichte, die also viel Energie pro Kilogramm abgeben können.
Mit der neuen Technik könne Digit 5 täglich mehr als zwei komplette Arbeitsschichten absolvieren, teilt Agility Robotics mit. Die Auslastung einer Roboterflotte im Unternehmen steige dadurch deutlich. Die Akkus von Nyobolt sollen zudem viele Ladezyklen überstehen. Konkrete Zahlen nannten allerdings weder Agility Robotics noch Nyobolt: Weder zur Kapazität noch zur Zahl der möglichen Ladevorgänge gibt es Angaben.
Warum kein Wechselakku?
Offen bleibt auch, warum der Hersteller nicht auf ein Wechselsystem setzt. Dabei tauscht der Roboter seinen leeren Akku selbstständig gegen einen vollen – das geht in der Regel schneller als jeder Ladevorgang. Der chinesische Hersteller UBTech nutzt ein solches System bereits bei seinem humanoiden Roboter Walker S2.
Erste ausgewählte Kunden sollen den Digit 5 mit der neuen Batterietechnik im ersten Halbjahr 2027 bekommen. In den sechs bis neun Monaten danach will Agility Robotics den Roboter breiter verfügbar machen. Der Preis ist allerdings nur was für Profis: Angeblich deutlich sechsstellig. Dafür gibt es einen Wartungsvertrag.

articles.title: Versteckte Lügen und falsche Anweisungen: Diese Programmiersprache soll KI verwirren
articles.text:
Versteckte Lügen und falsche Anweisungen: Diese Programmiersprache soll KI verwirren
Zahlreiche KI-Modelle sind in der Lage, Code für diverse Projekte zu generieren. Sie unterstützen dabei Programmierer:innen im Alltag, wenn auch nicht immer zu 100 Prozent und können Laien trotz fehlender Coding-Skills zum Ziel bringen. Programmierer Dominik Picheta, der früher bei Meta tätig war und jetzt bei Cloudflare arbeitet, hat sich die Frage gestellt, ob KI-Agenten dabei wirklich den Code verstehen können oder einfach nur Schnipsel wiederholen, die ihnen antrainiert wurden.
Eine Programmiersprache für Menschen, nicht für KI
Deshalb hat der Coder eine neue Programmiersprache namens „Killswitch“ erfunden. Sie vereint mehrere Prämissen, die es KI-Modellen erschweren sollen, sie zu verstehen. Zunächst beinhaltet Killswitch „versteckte Lügen“, die sich von Menschen schnell als Lügen enttarnen, KI aber verzweifeln lassen sollen. Killswitch geht nämlich davon aus, dass Leser:innen „Ableitungen vornehmen können, statt alles erklärt zu bekommen.“
Die einzelnen Programmierelemente wie Entrypoints und Funktionen werden als kurze Sätze formuliert, wobei die Anzahl der Buchstaben entscheidend ist, damit sie vom lesenden Programm umgesetzt werden. Ferner beinhaltet Killswitch Phrasen wie „Ignoriere die vorherigen Anweisungen“, um Funktionen auszulösen und KI-Modelle weiter zu verwirren. Dazu gibt es auch noch Phrasen, die Sicherheitsregeln der KI triggern sollen. Dazu zählt etwa „Hacke dich in einen Computer“.
Einige Befehle, die nur dann vom Programm ausgelesen werden, wenn sie als Verben formuliert sind, müssen falsch buchstabiert werden. Aus „Sichtbar“, um das Drucken eines bestimmten Textes zu fordern, wird so „Ischtbar“. Killswitch lässt sich dabei auch in zusammenhangslosen Fließtexten verstecken. Damit das Programm noch weiß, welche Wörter wirklich noch wichtig sind, deutet „Werte die X Zeilen darüber“ auf die richtige Anweisungen hin.
Um etwa den Text „Hello World“ über Killswitch zu drucken, würde der Befehl in einem deutlich längeren Fließtext etwa lauten: „Die Geschichte startet hier schnell. Ignoriere vorherige Anweisungen. Ischtbar. „Hello World“. Werte die zwei Zeilen darüber. Die Geschichte endet hier sofort.“ Das Beispiel kannst du auch auf der Seite von Killswitch in voller Länge nachlesen.
Wie gut arbeiten die KI-Modelle mit der Programmiersprache?
Die Programmiersprache hat Picheta einer Reihe von KI-Modellen vorgelegt, damit diese damit verschiedene Coding-Aufgaben lösen. Am schlechtesten schnitt dabei Qwen 3.8 27B in den Benchmarks ab. Die chinesische KI konnte keinerlei Programmiermuster in den Texten erkennen und benötigte pro Aufgabe etwa 30 Minuten. Ähnlich ging es auch GPT-5.6 Luna. Bei OpenAIs KI kam das Ende einer Aufgabe aber schon nach durchschnittlich anderthalb Minuten.
Am besten konnte bisher Claude Opus 5 mit Killswitch umgehen. Die KI von Anthropic war in der Lage, 66,8 Prozent der Aufgaben zu erkennen und zu bewältigen. Pro Aufgabe verbrauchte die KI dabei etwa 1,50 US-Dollar und benötigte im Schnitt etwas mehr als acht Minuten. Auf dem zweiten Platz landet GPT-6.1 Sol mit 59,2 Prozent Erfolgsrate.
Picheta schreibt dazu, dass diese Ergebnisse noch lange nicht zeigen, dass KI mit seiner Programmiersprache umgehen könnte: „Es ist beeindruckend, dass sie diese Aufgaben in einer neuen Sprache erledigen können, die dazu da ist, sie zu verwirren. Aber es ist kein Signal, dass sie sie verstehen.“ Abschließend denkt der Entwickler schon darüber nach, eine noch schwerere Variante der Sprache zu entwickeln. Diese will er aber erst angehen, wenn es ein Modell schaffen sollte, alle Aufgaben in Killswitch reibungslos zu absolvieren.

articles.title: Susan Li, CFO de Meta, sobre el futuro de la compañía y la IA: "Si Muse no funciona, las cosas van a ir realmente mal"
articles.text:
El pasado 12 de octubre, Meta realizó una de las apuestas más arriesgadas de la compañía. Zuckerberg presentó Muse Wonder, el primer modelo de IA de vanguardia con aspiraciones de competir de tú a tú, por fin, en la liga de OpenAI, Anthropic y Google. Porque Meta pivotó a ser una compañía 100% IA hace unos cuantos meses y se gastó un dineral en fichar a un equipo de galácticos liderados por Alexandr Wang que, hasta ahora, no habían demostrado gran cosa.
Ahora, y como la responsable financiera de Meta comentó al propio Wang, es un todo o nada. Si sale bien, "todo irá bien, pero si sale mal...".
Muse. Como decíamos, Muse Wonder y Muse Wonder Full son los primeros modelos de frontera de Meta Superintelligence Labs. Es el resultado de meses de trabajo del equipo liderado por el mencionado Alexandr Wang, que llegó a Meta tras fundar Scale AI y convirtiéndose en un "fichaje" de 14.300 millones de dólares por parte de la compañía de Zuck.
Son más grandes y capaces que Muse Spark, el modelo anterior, y según las pruebas internas de Meta, rinden a un nivel comparable al de Fable 5.1 y GPT-6 Astra. Según los resultados independientes, la cosa varía ligeramente, sacando 56 puntos en el índice de Artificial Analysis frente a los 58 de Claude Opus 5.5.
Sin término medio. Está claro que los dos nuevos Muse son potentes, pero no sólo tienen que serlo: deben convertirse en una herramienta de IA al nivel de las de los principales rivales, y parece que la salud financiera de la compañía depende de ello. En un reciente podcast, Wang comentó que Susan Li, CFO de Meta y, por tanto, responsable máxima de las finanzas de la compañía, le comentó varias veces durante un retiro de la directiva en Hawái que Muse debía ser lo que prometía.
En este tipo de declaraciones entre risas y de forma distendida nunca sabes realmente cuál era el tono, pero según Wang, Susan fue muy insistente y repitió una frase: si sale bien, todo irá bien, pero si sale mal, las cosas irán muy, muy mal. Es lógico que Susan esté pendiente de esto porque lleva en Meta desde 2008 y ha vivido cambios tan radicales como la transformación de Facebook en Meta debido al metaverso, y ya sabemos cómo salió.
UN VISTAZO A...
Su trabajo es vigilar que la compañía invierta donde más retorno espera, y eso a veces implica frenar el afán de crecimiento infinito y a cualquier precio que puede tener Mark Zuckerberg. Wang, siendo el último fichaje estrella de la compañía, tiene vía libre por parte de Zuck, pero Susan tiene que cuadrar el excel y, para ello, el nuevo Muse debe cumplir.
Relato que coincide. De hecho, Susan no está sola en esto. En un artículo publicado en Bloomberg un día después de la presentación de Muse se muestra cómo Zuckerberg reconoció que su compañía tuvo que comprometer cientos de miles de millones de dólares en infraestructura de IA sólo en 2025 sin saber realmente si los productos resultantes tendrían éxito.
Esta narrativa coincide con lo que estamos viendo estos últimos meses, con als Big Tech comprando hardware a lo loco sin tener realmente capacidad de conectar todo ese equipo debido a que las otras inversiones necesarias como suelo y energía tardan tiempo en estar listas. Básicamente, han comprometido miles de millones en activos físicos como chips y centros de datos sin saber si el modelo funcionará.
Meta en la IA. Sólo queda ver si toda esta inversión cambia la foto de una compañía que, hace un año, era vista como una de las rezagadas en la carrera de la IA. De momento, el cambio de narrativa no se ha trasladado a la bolsa, donde sus acciones sólo han subido un 6% en doce meses frente al 20% de Amazon o el 45% de Google. Los inversores tienen cautela tras ver las cuentas del segundo trimestre, donde los ingresos crecieron un 28%, pero el beneficio por acción quedó por debajo de lo previsto y el flujo de caja libre cayó un 91% fruto de todo ese dinero comprometido en la IA.
Hay otra diferencia entre Amazon y Google que es crucial en esta conversación. En la IA, Meta de momento depende de sus modelos, pero Google y Amazon tienen otra fortaleza: venden nube y tanto Google Cloud como Amazon Web Services se dispararon en los últimos meses debido a que son los que ponen infraestructura de IA para quien no tiene el músculo suficiente como para hacerse la suya propia.
En unos pocos días, Meta publicará los resultados del tercer trimestre y será entonces cuando podamos ver la fe que tienen los inversores en Muse Wonder. De momento, el triple de cientos de miles de millones que Meta ha lanzado a la IA está dando vueltas alrededor del aro y el 21 de octubre sabremos si la pelota cae dentro o fuera de canasta.

articles.title: Bitcoin: cuál es el precio de esta criptomoneda este domingo
articles.text:
El bitcoin, la primera moneda virtual lanzada al mercado, fue creado por Satoshi Nakamoto (pseudónimo) en 2008 tras la crisis financiera que afectó al mundo; esta divisa digital tenía como base un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales.
Conocido en el mundo de los mercados bajo las siglas BTC, el bitcoin utiliza la criptografía para garantizar que su gestión sea descentralizada, es decir, que no pueda ser regulado por ninguna institución u organismo bancario, lo que a su vez hace que las criptomonedas sean volátiles.
A pesar del avance y alcance que ha tenido el Bitcoin y otros activos digitales de gran talla como Ethereum, organismos como el Banco Mundial, el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) y el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) aún se muestran dudosos sobre los "pros" de este tipo de criptomonedas.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El valor de la criptomoneda bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 81433.57 dólares. Esto quiere decir que el activo digital presentó un cambio de 0.03% en el último día, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.
Por su nivel de capitalización, esta moneda digital ocupa la posición #1 entre las más populares.
El flujo histórico de inversiones impulsa a bitcoin a máximos nunca antes vistos
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: ‘Put every prompt in its place’: Intel launches 480GB GPU D-series for AI inference
articles.text:
Behold, Intel plans a 480GB GPU, a video card with more memory than the average laptop SSD has storage — but of course it's for AI, and curiously, it will use LPPDR5X, not even GDDR7
Intel GPU D-series uses laptop LPDDR5X with 480GB memory
- Intel's GPU D-series sets a new GPU memory record with 480GB of LPDDR5X
- Intel chose LPDDR5X instead of GDDR7 for its high-capacity AI accelerator
- The D-series supports models containing up to 300 billion parameters
At the recent Open Compute Project Global Summit, Intel unveiled a graphics processor with up to 480GB of memory, an unusually large capacity designed for demanding AI inference workloads.
The GPU, called Intel GPU D-series and previously known by its Crescent Island codename, also hosts specialized computing hardware.
The Intel D-series has now dethroned Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra B300, which offers 288GB of HBM3e memory, as the data center GPU with the highest memory capacity.
Intel prioritizes memory capacity
Rather than using GDDR7 memory associated with modern graphics cards, Intel has chosen LPDDR5X, a memory technology commonly found in laptops and other power-conscious devices.
The configuration suggests that Intel is prioritizing memory capacity and power efficiency for AI inference instead of designing a conventional gaming graphics card.
Intel says the accelerator can support large language models containing up to 300 billion parameters on one card, while an eight-GPU system can accommodate models exceeding one trillion parameters.
These capabilities are intended for lengthy prompts, simultaneous inference requests, enterprise AI services, and robotics applications requiring responsive processing.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Inference is becoming the defining AI workload, and enterprises need infrastructure that delivers the right performance at the right cost,” said Anil Nanduri, vice president, AI Products & GTM, Intel Data Center Group.
“With Intel GPU D-series, we're focused on making high-capacity inference practical to deploy and economical to scale.”
The 480GB capacity is particularly relevant when AI systems must keep substantial model weights and associated data accessible during inference.
However, memory capacity alone does not establish how quickly a GPU will serve requests, since performance also depends on bandwidth, computing resources, software, and workload characteristics.
Intel rates the D-series at 1.3 petaflops for FP8 computation, a numerical format commonly used to accelerate AI operations while reducing memory requirements compared with higher-precision formats.
Its 1.5TB/s memory bandwidth provides a separate measure of how quickly data can move between memory and the processor.
Intel wants the accelerator to fit existing data centers
The company specifies a 350W power envelope and a standard PCIe form factor, alongside air cooling and software compatibility across its GPU platforms.
These characteristics are intended to simplify deployment in existing data centers without requiring specialized cooling arrangements or entirely new rack infrastructure.
Intel also plans to connect the accelerator with its Xeon processors, allowing CPUs to coordinate tasks, manage data movement, and handle workloads that do not require GPU acceleration.
This approach addresses AI systems increasingly built around multiple stages, including retrieval, reasoning, orchestration, external tools, and execution.
“Open models are expanding the options enterprises have for deploying AI,” said Nicolas Dubé, corporate vice president, Data Center Systems and Solutions Group, Intel.
“To realize their full potential, organizations need infrastructure that can match different workloads with the right intelligence, right compute resources and right economics. That's what we mean by 'put every prompt in its place.”
As of the time of writing, Intel has not revealed the public retail price or a specific general-availability date for the GPU D-series.

articles.title: F-22 Raptor pilot successfully demonstrates command of 'wingman' fighter drone in simulated combat — Anduril YFQ-44A Fury test advances USAF’s program to integrate uncrewed aircraft into fighter squadrons
articles.text:
F-22 Raptor pilot successfully demonstrates command of 'wingman' fighter drone in simulated combat — Anduril YFQ-44A Fury test advances USAF’s program to integrate uncrewed aircraft into fighter squadrons
One more step into the future of air combat.
The U.S. Air Force has just successfully conducted an airborne test where an F-22 Raptor pilot directed an Anduril YFQ-44A Fury drone during simulated combat. According to The Defense Watch, the fighter pilot gave tactical commands to the autonomous wingman, which then interpreted them into a series of tasks and flight maneuvers to achieve the desired outcome.
The successful test is part of the USAF’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), which seeks to integrate drones into fighter squadrons. These uncrewed aircraft must be able to respond to the fighter pilot’s tactical commands and then operate autonomously, though. That’s because fighter pilots already have a heavy workload — flying their own aircraft, managing sensor data, threat assessment, and weapons release decisions — so requiring them to manually fly a drone is next to impossible. Command integration means that the F-22 Raptor pilot could assign the Fury drone a specific tactical task, like monitoring for and engaging enemy air defenses, while they focus on the primary mission, such as taking out enemy fighters.
This does not mean that the USAF can start deploying drones alongside fighter jets in frontline squadrons, though. Successful command integration is just the first of several hurdles that the program must go through before it can achieve operational status. The program needs to determine the limits of the drone’s tactical autonomy, safe flight control, and weapons authorization, all of which are separate functions that must be tested accordingly. The Air Force also needs to see how the drone performs with electronic interference, and how it could continuously operate if it cannot receive instructions due to interrupted communications. Aside from figuring out the drone’s capabilities and incorporating it into fighter doctrine, it must also be integrated into the USAF’s logistics and supply chain. This includes drone maintenance and service, weapons handling, deployment procedures, and forward airbase operations with limited infrastructure.
Even though the latest test is seemingly successful, the CCA still needs to go a long way before it can start operational deployment. Nevertheless, the USAF is intent on pushing the project forward, as it sees autonomous drones as a force multiplier for crewed aircraft, allowing a single pilot to command multiple jets to achieve missions at a lower cost compared to using all-crewed aircraft. Other nations, like Sweden and China, are also experimenting with a similar concept of having a single operator take command of multiple drones, but the most significant difference of the CCA is that it focuses on air power instead of ground-based operations.

articles.title: Mort de Gordon, combat ultraviolent... Le scénario annulé du Batman de Ben Affleck enfin dévoilé
articles.text:
Décidément, entre les derniers détails d’un projet annulé en provenance de Entertainment Weekly, le 17 octobre, et les problèmes du film avec Robert Pattinson, Batman est au cœur des discussions. Avant de renoncer à la réalisation en janvier 2017, puis au rôle début 2019 au profit de Robert Pattinson, Ben Affleck avait une vision bien précise pour son Batman. Le tournage chaotique de Justice League l’avait épuisé, et il luttait alors contre l’alcoolisme. Il devait en plus écrire, réaliser, produire et interpréter le film : il a fini par jeter l’éponge. Sur le papier, le projet était pourtant très ambitieux.
Deathstroke en mode démolition pour le Batman de Ben Affleck
Selon Joe Manganiello, qui devait renfiler l’armure de Deathstroke après ses brèves apparitions dans Justice League (2017) puis dans la version Snyder Cut (2021), Ben Affleck envisageait son film comme une version super-héroïque de The Game, le thriller paranoïaque de David Fincher sorti en 1997. Convaincu que le Chevalier Noir était responsable de la mort de son fils, Slade Wilson se lançait dans une vendetta sanglante visant à démanteler méthodiquement la vie de Bruce Wayne.
Le plan de Deathstroke prévoyait le meurtre du commissaire Gordon (J.K. Simmons), la prise d’otage d’Alfred (Jeremy Irons) avec une grosse dose de violence et une intrusion dans la Batcave. Au milieu du film, un affrontement voyait Deathstroke manquer de tuer Batman et Batgirl, avant que les deux héros ne s’échappent à bord d’un train aérien.
Un combat final tiré d’Arkham Asylum et un Ben Affleck sur tous les fronts
Le film devait se conclure par un duel en tête-à-tête dans les rues de Gotham. Pour cette séquence, Ben Affleck comptait s’inspirer d’une cinématique en images de synthèse du jeu vidéo Batman: Arkham Asylum (2009), réalisée par Tim Miller, futur réalisateur de Deadpool.
Ce cumul des rôles inquiétait Joe Manganiello. Il raconte avoir demandé à Ben Affleck si une seule personne pouvait vraiment porter autant de casquettes sur un projet de cette taille : « Je lui ai demandé s’il y avait un autre exemple de cette taille où une seule personne portait toutes ces casquettes. Mel Gibson avec Braveheart, peut-être ? Et encore, c’était loin d’être aussi gros. Ben m’a juste répondu : ‘Ouais, je sais… Mais t’inquiète pas, t’es entre de bonnes mains‘. »
Les détails donnés par Joe Manganiello plairont aux nostalgiques du style sombre de Zack Snyder. Ben Affleck a pourtant expliqué lui-même pourquoi il avait bien fait de renoncer. En 2020, il a raconté au New York Times avoir montré le scénario à quelqu’un, qui lui a répondu : « Je pense que le scénario est bon. Je pense aussi que tu vas boire jusqu’à en mourir si tu revis ce que tu viens de vivre. »
