articles.title: How Operation Sindoor reshaped India's private defence tech industry
articles.text:
How Operation Sindoor reshaped India's private defence tech industry
From faster procurement to direct engagement with the armed forces, Operation Sindoor has opened new opportunities for private defence companies developing critical military technologies.
Following Operation Sindoor, India's private defence technology sector is seeing a shift in how the armed forces engage with domestic manufacturers. The transformation is marked by faster procurement, greater private-sector participation, and renewed emphasis on developing critical military technologies domestically, according to industry executives.
At TechSparks 2026, Ankit Kumar, Co-founder and Chief Business Officer of Tonbo Imaging; Priyanka Singhal, Founder and CEO of Ammunic Systems; and Radhika P, Co-founder of Pinaka Aerospace; discussed how Indian private companies contributed to recent military operations and what the country must prioritise to prepare for the battlefield of 2035.
In a panel discussion titled 'War Room 2035: What technologies must India build for the battlefield' moderated by Adith Charlie, Managing Editor of YourStory and The CapTable, the founders pointed to growing opportunities for indigenous companies in night-vision systems, electronic warfare, smart munitions, and autonomous defence platforms.
Operation Sindoor and the private sector's growing role
Priyanka Singhal, Founder and CEO of Ammunic Systems, a defence R&D firm specialising in electronic fuzes and munition technologies, described Operation Sindoor as a turning point for the industry. “The operation was an eye opener,” she said, adding that it had exposed the limitations of traditional defence procurement cycles.
Singhal said Ammunic supplied loitering munitions and gravity-drop bombs during Operation Sindoor, working with drone platform partners to integrate its weapons into systems used in the operation. According to her, the armed forces have begun moving away from an excessive focus on procedural compliance towards deploying equipment that meets immediate battlefield requirements. Initiatives such as iDEX and emergency procurement mechanisms have helped accelerate the process, she said.
Radhika P of Pinaka Aerospace echoed this assessment. Previously, private defence companies often worked through defence public sector undertakings (DPSUs), the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), and other established channels. Following Operation Sindoor, she said, the armed forces had increasingly engaged directly with private companies, particularly in electronic warfare, avionics, and sensor technologies.
Radhika said Pinaka had contributed to the indigenisation of missile systems that were deployed during the operation. She argued that the effectiveness of military equipment increasingly depends on its payloads, including sensors and electronic warfare systems, rather than the platform alone.
“If there is an electronic countermeasure system, it can neutralise a platform which is probably 10 times more expensive,” she said, underscoring the strategic importance of developing indigenous payload technologies.
Kumar of Tonbo Imaging, which specialises in electro-optical and infrared technologies, said the shift towards indigenous defence procurement had begun even before Operation Sindoor, particularly following developments along India's eastern border. That had encouraged the armed forces to reduce their dependence on technologies sourced from countries sharing land borders with India.
Tonbo, which has spent nearly two decades developing indigenous imaging systems, was positioned to benefit from that shift, Kumar said. Its night-vision technologies have been deployed across several Indian military operations, including Operation Sindoor, when air-defence systems used the company's capabilities, he added.
Kumar said close engagement with the armed forces, including product trials and feedback from users, had helped Tonbo develop its technologies. “We've learned things the hard way. We've learned things on the ground. We've learned things with the customers,” he said.
What India must build by 2035
Looking towards 2035, Kumar said defence systems would increasingly move towards autonomy, reducing the need for direct human involvement in certain operations. He pointed to the potential use of autonomous systems in air combat and on the ground, including the possibility of humanoid robots supporting border operations.
As military platforms become more autonomous, sensors and intelligence will become critical to their ability to detect threats, interpret their surroundings and respond without constant human intervention.
“For autonomy, sensors, intelligence, both are very critical, very important,” Kumar said.
He argued that India had strengths in both areas, particularly in developing intelligence capabilities that can operate directly on military platforms. Such technologies, he said, could improve operational efficiency and reduce dependence on human operators, but they needed to be developed as sovereign capabilities rather than sourced from overseas suppliers.
“Intelligence, connectivity, sensing, these will be the mainstay of how the wars will be fought tomorrow,” he said.
For Radhika, a key battlefield priority is control over the electromagnetic spectrum, which underpins radar, communications, electronic warfare, and several other military capabilities. She argued that future military advantage would increasingly depend on how effectively forces detect, interpret and disrupt electromagnetic signals.
That also makes ownership of the underlying technology critical. Developing or assembling defence platforms in India is not sufficient if the software, electronics architecture and intellectual property remain controlled by foreign suppliers.
“It is very important to have good control on the source code, the board design, and things like that,” Radhika said.
She also emphasised that technology transfer should strengthen India's ability to develop and integrate systems independently, rather than create continued dependence on overseas suppliers. Control over intellectual property and systems integration would be especially important in reducing the risks associated with foreign supply chains, she added.
Closing the gaps in research and deployment
Singhal, meanwhile, called for greater integration across the three armed services.
She argued that the Army, Navy and Air Force needed better-connected platforms and weapons systems to coordinate effectively during emergencies. She also highlighted materials research as an area requiring greater attention.
Advanced materials would play an increasingly important role in developing next-generation weapon systems, including those requiring greater effectiveness and stealth capabilities. India, she said, needed to place more emphasis on materials R&D alongside investments in autonomous systems and other defence technologies.
The founders also identified persistent challenges in bringing together the armed forces, government research institutions and private industry. Singhal said startups and smaller defence companies could move faster than government research programmes, which often face bureaucratic delays.
Radhika said the challenge stemmed partly from differing expectations. The armed forces want sophisticated systems delivered quickly, research organisations operate through lengthy validation cycles and private manufacturers need commercially viable development timelines.
One way forward, she suggested, was to involve private industry from the prototype stage, with the armed forces funding development projects, research organisations working alongside manufacturers and clearer pathways to production orders.
She pointed to the Development-cum-Production Partner model as a mechanism that could help bridge the gap between research, development and large-scale manufacturing if implemented effectively.
For India's private defence technology industry, the next challenge is not simply to manufacture more equipment domestically. It is to develop and control the technologies that make military platforms effective, while building a procurement and research ecosystem capable of moving those technologies from the laboratory to the battlefield.

articles.title: Se sigue buscando al autor de la presa que convirtió un río de los Pirineos en su piscina privada durante dos años
articles.text:
En cualquier pueblo de montaña, el río es la piscina del verano. Ya lo contábamos a propósito de las piscinas naturales andaluzas. Pero mientras Madrid quiere construirse la piscina más grande de España, lo que no es habitual ver es a alguien derivando parte de un río para montarse su propia obra. Y eso es lo que hizo alguien en Osséja, un municipio de los Pirineos franceses: levantó una barrera en el cauce del Vanéra para que el agua se remansara y tener una poza donde bañarse. Ha estado así dos años. Hasta el pasado viernes 9 de octubre, que entró una excavadora Kubota y retiró las piedras, según cuenta Diario Vasco.
Dónde. No ha sido en territorio español. Osséja está en la Cerdaña francesa, dentro del departamento de los Pirineos Orientales. El Vanéra, que en catalán se llama Llavanera, es un río transfronterizo con España, según L’Indépendant. Tras un tiempo recopilando información, los equipos técnicos del ayuntamiento entraron con la máquina en el lecho del río para desmontar una presa levantada sin permiso. Los pescadores ya habían dado la voz de alarma. Según L’Indépendant, la asociación detectó la obra hacía meses y avisó de que se veían cada vez menos peces en el río.
En la operación participó también la asociación La Fario de la Vanéra, y contó con el visto bueno de la Dirección Departamental de los Territorios y del Mar (DDTM) y de la Oficina Francesa de la Biodiversidad (OFB). Dice el consistorio que la estructura funcionaba en verano como una especie de piscina natural.
Presa casera. El problema no era solo que estuviera sin permiso. El ayuntamiento advierte de que una barrera así cambia de forma notable la circulación del agua, favorece que se acumulen sedimentos y hace que suba la temperatura. Todo eso puede desequilibrar el ecosistema del río y dañar el hábitat de las truchas que viven en él. Aunque su fin fuera recreativo, la presa era una alteración artificial del cauce.
Quién y cuánto. Del autor de la presa se sabe poco. Melty habla de un vecino que convirtió el río en piscina, y su identidad no ha trascendido. Lo que sí se repite en todos los medios es la cifra de 1.500 euros. Pero la sanción no se ha impuesto aún ni de momento consta cómo avanza el expediente.
Qué dice la ley. La legislación francesa prohíbe desde hace años obstaculizar a propósito el libre flujo del agua en los cursos fluviales. El Código de Medio Ambiente prevé para esa infracción una multa de quinta clase, que puede llegar a los mencionados 1.500 euros. Existe además un escalón más serio: si la obra necesitaba autorización o declaración previa y se hizo sin ella, puede constituir delito, con hasta un año de prisión y 75.000 euros de multa. Nada indica que se esté yendo por esa vía. Es el marco legal y no lo que han anunciado las autoridades.
Pero ojo: en Francia, quien tiene las dos orillas de un arroyo es también dueño del lecho, y puede mantenerlo y limpiarlo. Eso sí, el agua se considera patrimonio común de la nación, así que cortarle el paso para hacerse una poza exige permiso.
Qué falta por saber. Más allá de saber quién es el autor (imposible salvo que lo confiese motu propio o alguien que haya disfrutado de la piscina dé el soplo) queda por reconstruir el cauce. Tras la “demolición” de la presa artificial, también queda por saber si ya se ha levantado un atestado o habrá denuncia formal. Lo que viene después puede ser una reclamación del coste de retirar la presa (y unas horas de excavadora no son baratas, te lo aseguro).
Tras esto, si se aplicará solo la multa de 1.500 euros o se abrirá la vía penal ya queda en manos de las competencias. De momento, la prensa local habla de riesgo y no de sentencia. Lo único cierto es que la poza ya no existe y que el Vanéra ha vuelto a correr sin obstáculos.
¿Y en España? En España, los inventos de hidráulica casera caen peor. Aquí la multa sería bastante más alta. Ley de Aguas castiga las obras sin autorización en un cauce con sanciones que van de hasta 10.000 euros (leves) a 1.000.000 (muy graves), según el daño causado. Según un anuncio de la Región de Murcia, el reglamento califica de leve la infracción por debajo de 3.000 euros de daños y de grave entre 15.000 y 150.000. De regalo, las confederaciones hidrográficas pueden imponer multas coercitivas y paralizar la obra. Lo habitual es una multa y el desmontaje a costa del infractor.
La cárcel solo entra en juego si hay daños graves. El artículo 325 del Código Penal prevé de seis meses a dos años de prisión para quien, incumpliendo las leyes ambientales, haga extracciones, excavaciones o captaciones de agua que causen o puedan causar daños sustanciales a las aguas, a animales o a plantas, y de dos a cinco años si se perjudica gravemente el equilibrio natural. Desviar agua sin permiso también puede acabar en multa penal de 3 a 6 meses. Una presa casera para bañarse difícilmente alcanza ese umbral por sí sola, pero la desobediencia a la Administración o los caudales importantes sí podrían hacerlo.

articles.title: Acheter une voiturette électrique pourrait bientôt coûter moins cher grâce à cette aide
articles.text:
Bonne nouvelle si vous comptiez acheter une voiturette électrique. Le gouvernement a présenté l’acte 2 de son plan d’électrification, avec une aide pouvant aller jusqu’à 2 000 euros selon la catégorie du véhicule. On décrypte ensemble les contours de l’aide.
Jusqu’à 2 000 euros d’aides
Le plan d’électrification en arrive à son acte 2. En plus du coup de pouce pour l’achat d’une voiture électrique, les catégories inférieures, L7 et L6, vont profiter également d’une aide à l’achat. Concrètement, si vous souhaitez acheter une voiturette électrique, vous pouvez espérer une aide à l’achat allant jusqu’à 2 000 euros, ce qui est plutôt généreux quand on sait que le bonus écologique pour tous sur une voiture électrique à moins de 47 000 euros est de 3 500 euros.
Mais attention, cette aide de 2 000 euros est atteinte uniquement pour les voitures électriques de la catégorie L7, c’est-à-dire des véhicules pouvant rouler jusqu’à 90 km/h, avec au moins 150 km d’autonomie, la possibilité d’installer quatre personnes et une production en Europe. Autant dire que les modèles commercialisés en France et répondant à ces critères sont très peu nombreux, le Dacia Hipster pourrait bientôt arriver sur ce marché très spécifique.
Une aide plus généreuse pour les sans-permis ?
Les voiturettes sans permis (VSP) pourraient aussi voir arriver une aide généreuse. Si 2 000 euros sont accordés aux L7 limitées à 90 km/h, on peut espérer une nouvelle aide plus généreuse pour les VSP L6 électriques, limitées à 45 km/h, qui constituent le véritable cœur du marché actuellement.
Si un bonus allant jusqu’à 900 euros avait déjà été accordé, les VSP L6 électriques n’ont plus droit qu’à une prime CEE comprise entre 200 et 500 euros, selon le modèle choisi, ce qui est maigre pour des voitures vendues entre 10 000 et 15 000 euros.
Toutefois, les Citroën Ami et Fiat Topolino ne sont pas sûres d’y avoir droit. En effet, cette aide est réservée aux véhicules produits en Europe. Les VSP électriques du groupe Stellantis sont fabriquées au Maroc. Même si un accord commercial existe entre l’UE et le Maroc, rien n’assure formellement qu’elles seront éligibles à la nouvelle aide, qui doit être lancée le 1er janvier 2027.
Avec cette aide à l’achat des L7, le gouvernement français veut favoriser l’achat de petits véhicules électriques produits en Europe, favorisant ainsi les activités d’acteurs comme Ligier, Aixam, Microlino ou encore Silence. Mais si l’aide la plus généreuse est accordée uniquement à des véhicules quatre places capables de rouler jusqu’à 90 km/h et nécessitant le permis, pourquoi ne pas opter finalement pour une citadine électrique comme une Renault Twingo E-Tech ou une Citroën ë-C3, qui ne coûte pas beaucoup plus cher grâce à un bonus écologique plus généreux et qui offre surtout une meilleure polyvalence ?

articles.title: Alors que les températures baissent, ce chauffage mural connecté de 2 000 W passe sous les 110 € — Frandroid
articles.text:
Avec le retour du froid, allumer tout le système de chauffage de la maison n’est pas toujours nécessaire. Pour chauffer rapidement une chambre, un bureau ou une pièce un peu fraîche, le Dreo 517S est une excellente solution d’appoint. Fixé directement au mur pour ne pas encombrer le sol, ce modèle de 2 000 W est idéal pour les espaces de 15 à 25 m². Il se pilote très facilement via son application dédiée, et voit justement son prix chuter sous la barre des 110 euros.
Les forces du Dreo 517S
- Une puissance de 2 000 W avec trois niveaux de chauffe
- Un thermostat réglable de 5 à 35 °C, degré par degré
- Une sortie d’air inclinable à 30° pour orienter la chaleur
Affiché à 119,99 euros, le Dreo 517S tombe aujourd’hui à 109,99 euros sur Amazon.
Un chauffage qui reste au mur
L’un des grands atouts du Dreo 517S, c’est sa simplicité d’installation au mur. En plus de prendre bien moins de place au sol qu’un radiateur classique, cette fixation évite de se prendre les pieds dans le câble de passage ou de risquer de le faire basculer. Il se branche directement sur n’importe quelle prise secteur et se contrôle très facilement depuis son panneau tactile avec écran LED sans passer par son smartphone.
Côté diffusion, pas de balayage automatique qui bouge tout seul de haut en bas : le Dreo 517S mise plutôt sur un volet orientable à la main jusqu’à 30°. L’idée est toute simple : vous inclinez la grille vous-même pour envoyer l’air chaud exactement là où vous en avez besoin — vers le lit, votre fauteuil ou vos pieds sous le bureau — plutôt que de laisser la chaleur monter inutilement et stagner au plafond. Une fois l’angle idéal trouvé, le flux reste ciblé et continu.
Une chauffe rapide et un mode ECO
Niveau performances, grâce à sa technologie céramique, il ne faut que quelques secondes pour ressentir la chaleur. L’appareil offre jusqu’à 2 000 W de puissance et vous laisse ajuster la température au degré près, de 5 à 35 °C.
Pour éviter de le laisser tourner inutilement, tout se pilote facilement depuis votre smartphone via l’application Dreo. On peut y configurer des plannings sur mesure et programmer le chauffage à l’avance, pour que la pièce soit à la température parfaite au moment exact où vous en avez besoin.
Sur le papier, l’appareil se fait très discret avec un niveau sonore annoncé à seulement 28 dB. Gardez toutefois en tête qu’avec ses 2 000 W sous le capot, la facture d’électricité peut vite grimper s’il tourne à plein régime toute la journée. Le 517S est plutôt à réserver à un chauffage d’appoint ponctuel, sans en faire le chauffage principal du logement.

articles.title: Free web-based chip fab engineering game goes viral in Taiwan — game is a realistic and stressful simulation, ‘basically a horror game’ say some players
articles.text:
Free web-based chip fab engineering game goes viral in Taiwan — game is a realistic and stressful simulation, ‘basically a horror game’ say some players
Fab24hr: A Day in the Life of a Semiconductor Wafer Factory Worker is a no-install 3D web game with a 12-chapter story mode.
A new 3D web game where you live "A Day in the Life of a Semiconductor Wafer Factory Worker" has gone viral in Taiwan, where it was developed. Available in Chinese, English, and Japanese, Fab24hr is a work simulator where you play one of several semiconductor engineer roles in a blocky isometric 3D factory. Though the graphics might look basic, Taiwan’s TVBS news says that the game is so realistic that it resonates with fab workers but not always in a good way – some have likened it to "a horror game" or "prison" [machine translation].
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
If you head over to the Fab24hr site, the game UI loads pretty quickly and you are asked to input a character name and ‘Clock in.’ Then two game modes are presented. You can play the main story, dubbed ‘The life of a chip’ where you character works through 12 chapters shepherding a hearing-aid chip from the R&D line into the hands of an end user. In this mode your blocky fab worker character will simulate dealing with equipment failures, process anomalies, and production progress emergencies. You might also have to file reports about operational errors. Apparently there are three endings to this 12-chapter game, depending on your progress and decisions.
Another game mode is called ‘A day in the fab.’ Here you pick a factory location and role. For example, you can choose to be a Process Engineer. Your day started with the ETCH-03 semiconductor tool breaking, and “everyone is waiting for you to say what time it will be fixed.” Though this might sound like you’ve been thrown in at the deep end, if you pay attention to the handover from the previous shift, there should be clues to get you by. Technical terms are explained in the game so even those with no semiconductor industry experience should be able to ‘enjoy’ this escapade.
I briefly tested the game in my browser, where it ran without issues. It didn’t take long to understand why some Taiwanese fab veterans felt this simulator was kind of stressful, or even “super scary.” It isn’t the kind of free-time escapism I’m looking for.

articles.title: Universal Cart: Warum Googles neuer Warenkorb für Händler zur Machtfrage wird
articles.text:
Ein Warenkorb für alle: Wie Google die Kontrolle über den Onlinehandel ausbaut
Google hat in den USA ein neues Einkaufs-Feature vorgestellt, den Universal Cart. Dabei handelt es sich um einen intelligenten Warenkorb, der das Shoppingerlebnis über unterschiedliche Händler hinweg ermöglichen und vereinfachen soll. Google sieh das Konzept als eine zentrale Anlaufstelle für Einkäufe. Die Idee dahinter klingt plausibel: Anstatt etliche Browser-Tabs offenhalten, Screenshots anfertigen zu müssen und Produkte in verschiedenen Merklisten und Warenkörben zu speichern, könnten Nutzer:innen in Zukunft Artikel und Angebote verschiedener Händler:innen in einem zentralen Warenkorb verwalten.
Google hatte das Konzept schon im Mai auf seiner Entwicklerkonferenz Google I/O präsentiert. Zunächst erfolgt eine Einbindung an zentralen Stellen wie der Google-Suche und in der Gemini-App. So kann an den zentralen Stellen auf bestimmte vorgemerkte Produkte verwiesen werden. Die Auswahl bleibt bestehen, sodass ein möglicher Einkauf jederzeit fortgesetzt werden kann. Perspektivisch sollen auch weitere Anwendungen wie Gmail und Youtube hinzukommen, was mittelfristig auch das Werbegeschäft bei den betreffenden Diensten verändern wird.
Zunächst testet Google das Feature in den USA und arbeitet hier mit Händlern wie Nike, Target, Walmart und Wayfair zusammen – sowie mit zahlreichen Shops auf Basis von Shopify. Ob und wann das Konzept auch in Deutschland ausgerollt wird, lässt das Unternehmen offen. In der Vergangenheit war Deutschland recht oft bei den ersten europäischen Ländern, in denen Services bereitgestellt wurden. Wenn es soweit ist, dürften Unternehmen, die auf einer Shopify-Basis arbeiten, ziemlich einfach anzubinden sein, wenn man den aktuellen Aussagen von Handelsexperten glauben darf.
KI überwacht Preise und sucht nach Rabatten
Googles neuer Warenkorb arbeitet dabei im Hintergrund und setzt auf den Shopping Graph des Konzerns, der nach Googles Angaben über 60 Milliarden fortlaufend aktualisierte Produktangebote bereitstellt. Der Universal Cart protokolliert und beobachtet Preisentwicklungen und Lagerbestände und weist Kund:innen entsprechend auf Veränderungen hin. Wenn etwa der Preis eines vorgemerkten Artikels sinkt oder ein bis dato ausverkauftes Produkt wieder verfügbar ist, erhält der Kunde einen entsprechenden Hinweis, wie man das von Preissuchmaschinen kennt.
Zudem zeigt Google hier, wie sich ein durchgängiger Handelsfunnel bezahlt macht: Denn durch die Anbindung an Google Wallet kann der Warenkorb die Vorteile bestimmter hinterlegter Kreditkarten berücksichtigen und etwa darauf hinweisen, mit welcher Karte sich zusätzliche Bonuspunkte oder Vergünstigungen erzielen lassen. Auch dazu passende Rabattcodes werden direkt im Warenkorb angezeigt. Das ist vor allem auch dann relevant, wenn Google hier bestimmte Vorteile wie ein Prime-Abo oder ein bestehendes Liefer-Abo berücksichtigen kann.
Auch hier wird es wieder darauf ankommen, wie nah Händler:innen die Plattform an sich heranlassen. Denn beim Kaufabschluss stehen zwei Möglichkeiten zur Verfügung: So können Nutzer:innen bei teilnehmenden Händlern die Bestellung mit wenigen Klicks direkt innerhalb der Google-Oberfläche über Google Pay abschließen oder aber die ausgewählten Produkte in den Warenkorb des jeweiligen Händlers übertragen und diese wie gewohnt über das Händler-UI kaufen.
Google setzt dabei auf das Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), einen gemeinsam mit Handelspartnern entwickelten offenen Standard, der für den Datenaustausch zwischen KI-Systemen, Handelsplattformen und den Shopsystemen der Händler gedacht ist.
Einzelnen Händlern bleiben weiterhin erster Ansprechpartner
Eine Beschränkung gibt es dabei aber schon: Denn der gemeinsame Warenkorb bedeutet, dass weiterhin jeder einzelne Händler Ansprechpartner für den eigentlichen Kaufvorgang sowie für Reklamationen und Retouren bleibt. Daher kommen auch Bestellbestätigungen sowie der Kundenservice vom jeweiligen Handelspartner.
Dennoch ist der Universal Cart eine entscheidende Veränderung, mit der Google seinen Status als Gatekeeper und Plattformbetreiber im Onlinehandel stärkt. Stand der Konzern in der Vergangenheit vor allem als Vermittler zwischen Produktsuche und Onlineshop, ändert sich das in Zukunft, weil Google hier zusätzliche Aufgaben übernimmt: bei der Produktauswahl, in der Preisüberwachung und nicht zuletzt in der Anbahnung der Kaufabwicklung. All das ist die Voraussetzung für einen funktionierenden Agentic Commerce, an dem Gemini, Shopping Graph, Google Wallet und UCP gleichermaßen beteiligt sind.
Auch wenn all das noch nicht komplett autonom funktioniert, können Händler erkennen, dass der Grad an Unterstützung durch die KI zunimmt – und man an Google auch in Zukunft schlecht vorbeikommt. Das ist entscheidend für die Händler, weil der alte Onlineshop einen Teil seiner Bedeutung verliert, wenn Kund:innen Produkte mehr als bisher bei Google auswählen, vergleichen und möglicherweise auch bezahlen.
Der Universal Cart ist damit auch ein weiterer Hinweis darauf, wie sich der Onlinehandel durch KI verändert. Zukünftig wird neben der Sichtbarkeit eines Händlers in Suchmaschinen wichtiger, ob seine Produkte und Schnittstellen für die Einkaufsassistenten der großen Plattformen zugänglich sind.

articles.title: JEP 543 Finalizes Structured Concurrency in JDK 28, Ending Seven Preview Rounds
Microsoft hizo que Windows 11 ande 20% más rápido en las computadoras con menos memoria
articles.text:
Microsoft anunció el jueves que Windows 11 funciona hasta 20% más rápido que antes, con mejoras de memoria pensadas específicamente para las computadoras con apenas 8 gigabytes de RAM. El cambio llega en medio de una suba histórica en el precio de esos chips de memoria.
Qué cambia exactamente
Según el anuncio publicado en el blog oficial de la empresa, firmado por Navjot Virk, vicepresidenta corporativa de Experiencias de Windows, el sistema ahora puede mantener hasta 2 gigabytes adicionales de datos activos en la memoria RAM en lugar de moverlos al almacenamiento, que es mucho más lento.
Esa mejora apunta directamente a mantener la fluidez cuando el usuario tiene varias aplicaciones o pestañas del navegador abiertas al mismo tiempo. Virk explicó que la ganancia “puede marcar una diferencia especialmente significativa” en las computadoras con 8 gigabytes de memoria o menos.
En esas máquinas, los widgets del escritorio ahora se cargan recién cuando el usuario los abre, en lugar de precargarse en segundo plano. Esa sola decisión libera más de 200 megabytes de memoria disponibles para otras tareas, de acuerdo con la empresa.
Microsoft aseguró que la mejora de 20% en la velocidad general se midió comparando los tiempos de respuesta de Inicio, el Explorador de archivos, la Búsqueda, la Herramienta Recortes, Microsoft 365 y el navegador Edge entre dos versiones distintas del sistema operativo. La compañía aclaró que esa cifra es un máximo y que el resultado real varía según el equipo y el uso que se le dé.
Una respuesta a la crisis de precios de la memoria
El anuncio se da en un contexto puntual: los precios de los chips de memoria RAM subieron con fuerza este año porque buena parte de la producción mundial se redirigió a abastecer los centros de datos que entrenan modelos de inteligencia artificial.
Esa escasez empujó a varios fabricantes de computadoras a volver a ofrecer modelos con 8 gigabytes de RAM como opción más económica, después de años en los que 16 gigabytes se había vuelto el estándar de facto para un uso cotidiano sin sobresaltos.
Microsoft venía prometiendo este trabajo de optimización desde marzo, cuando Pavan Davuluri, presidente de Windows y Dispositivos, se comprometió públicamente a reducir el consumo de memoria del sistema operativo. En mayo, durante el podcast interno Inside Windows, Davuluri había planteado que la memoria solo debería consumirse “cuando realmente se usa esa capacidad”.
En julio, la compañía convirtió la “optimización de memoria para equipos de 8 gigabytes o más” en un área de trabajo formal. Las mejoras anunciadas esta semana son, según Microsoft, las primeras cifras concretas que entrega sobre ese esfuerzo.
Qué no cambia para el usuario
Las mejoras no modifican los requisitos de hardware de otras funciones de Windows. Las computadoras llamadas Copilot+ PC, que ejecutan funciones de inteligencia artificial de forma local, siguen exigiendo un mínimo de 16 gigabytes de RAM, aunque el sistema operativo general sea ahora más eficiente.
Microsoft también incluyó en el mismo anuncio otras mejoras ajenas a la memoria: el emparejamiento de auriculares Bluetooth, incluidos los AirPods de Apple, sería hasta 15 segundos más rápido, y el inicio de sesión con reconocimiento facial o huella digital de Windows Hello funcionaría de forma más confiable.
Las mejoras de velocidad y memoria ya están disponibles para los usuarios del programa Windows Insider y Microsoft prometió extenderlas de forma gradual al resto de los equipos con Windows 11 durante lo que resta de 2026.

articles.title: Planning to go to an Apple Store to pick up an iPhone Duo on Friday? You might be disappointed
articles.text:
'Nothing short of extraordinary': high iPhone Duo demand means you probably won't be able to pick up Apple's foldable by walking into a store on October 23
Apple's foldable is proving popular
- iPhone Duo shipping dates have slipped to January worldwide
- Stock may be limited if you're trying to pick one up in an Apple Store too
- Retail availability and the first preorder shipments due on October 23
We've already had one indication that iPhone Duo sales were going rather well when shipping dates for preorders started slipping into next year, and now Apple is apparently telling retail staff that availability will be limited inside stores too.
According to Apple Store employees speaking to MacRumors, Apple has said that customers without a preorder should be warned against heading to their local outlet in the expectation of picking up an iPhone Duo on Friday, October 23.
That's the designated day when online preorders are due to start shipping out to buyers, and when — in theory — the iPhone Duo becomes available to buy in store. This latest report suggests that might not be possible right away.
It isn't clear if the instructions given to the Apple Store employees speaking to MacRumors apply across the US or globally, but set your expectations accordingly: don't assume you'll be able to walk into an Apple Store on Friday and get yourself a shiny new iPhone Duo.
Keeping up with demand
With shipping times for online preorders now slipping into 2027, it's possible there will be quite a few Apple fans interested in the iPhone Duo who are thinking about taking the walk-in retail route — but it seems stock will be very limited there too.
Before the phone was unveiled, there had been some chatter around a launch delay due to production problems, and this may be following on from that. Whatever the full story, Apple apparently can't keep up with demand for the time being.
The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable phone, and starts at $1,999 / £1,999 / AU$3,499. A quick check on the Apple site at the time of writing shows preorders scheduled to ship in January for the cheapest 256GB model in the US, UK, and Australia.

articles.title: PS4 Exclusive Driveclub Now Runs Natively on PC Through Fan-Made Recomp
articles.text:
Sunday, October 18th 2026
PS4 Exclusive Driveclub Now Runs Natively on PC Through Fan-Made Recomp
Driveclub, Evolution Studios' 2014 PS4 racer, now runs natively on Windows through DriveClub Recomp, a fan project released on GitHub by OverkillLabs3. While PlayStation emulation has been progressing rapidly, this one doesn't use CPU emulation. The game's own x86-64 code runs directly on the PC's processor, while the PS4 system libraries are reimplemented and GPU commands are translated to Vulkan. The port supports resolutions from 720p to 8K, ultrawide displays, and an unlocked frame rate that doesn't speed up the game. It also replaces the original anti-aliasing with NVIDIA DLAA on RTX cards or AMD FSR 3.1 on any GPU, both at native resolution, and RTX owners can swap between the two in-game with F10.
The developer says the game holds about 60 FPS at 4K in its heaviest scenes on an RTX 5070 Ti paired with a Ryzen 7 5800X3D, and the v0.2.3 update pushed one 4K test race from roughly 62 to 71 FPS. It is still rough around the edges, however. Some reflections look too bright, shaders compile during the first few minutes, slower CPUs drop frames in busy scenes, and online features don't work. It has also only been tested on NVIDIA hardware so far. A second project, DCport by qnfn, takes a similar route with FSR 3.1 and FSR 4 support. Both need the player's own dump of version 1.28. It's in the same vein as how modders recently got Gran Turismo Sport running on PC. These recomps arrive a couple of months after a ShadPS4 patch let Driveclub run at up to 8K, quite the jump for a game that shipped at 1080p and 30 FPS.

articles.title: Microsoft acaba de hacer algo inesperado con Linux y podría cambiar la seguridad de millones de PCs
articles.text:
Linux ha pasado de ser un bicho raro de servidores a convertirse en una verdadera alternativa para quienes están hartos de Windows. Ese crecimiento ha provocado que los ordenadores se conviertan en el objetivo perfecto para los atacantes, sobre todo aquellos que trabajan en desarrollo. Debido a ello, Microsoft ha lanzado su antivirus Defender en Linux, para que los usuarios que dejaron atrás Windows.
De acuerdo con una publicación en su blog, Microsoft ha llevado Defender a los escritorios Linux en fase de vista previa pública. La iniciativa busca ofrecer el mismo nivel de protección empresarial que Windows, pero ahora en los dispositivos con el sistema operativo libre. Los usuarios tendrán acceso a la versión más reciente del antivirus, con análisis de amenazas en tiempo real.
Microsoft señala que los ordenadores con Linux que usan los desarrolladores suelen tener acceso a información esencial para su día a día. En ella se incluyen los repositorios de código, infraestructuras en la nube, entornos de contenedores y sistemas internos críticos. En caso de que uno de esos equipos resulte comprometido, un atacante podría obtener una puerta de entrada a un proyecto mayor de desarrollo y distribución de software.
Entre las herramientas que se incluyen en Microsoft Defender destacan las funciones de Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) y la plataforma de análisis de amenazas. A esto se suma el módulo MDVM, que identifica y corrige vulnerabilidades y configuraciones inseguras. Microsoft Defender puede identificar si el dispositivo es un servidor o una estación de trabajo Linux, por lo que los administradores no tendrán que desplegar un agente específico para escritorio.
El lanzamiento de Defender se da a unos días de que Microsoft anunciara los contenedores nativos de Linux en Windows 11. Esta característica permite ejecutar aplicaciones empaquetadas dentro de Windows sin recurrir a herramientas de terceros, como Docker Desktop. Windows 11 los integra de forma nativa, lo que facilita ejecutar cargas de trabajo directamente en el sistema operativo y sin reiniciar.
A diferencia del Microsoft de hace 20 años, los de Redmond ven ahora a Linux como una "plataforma estratégica de ejecución" para cargas de inteligencia artificial y aplicaciones nativas de la nube.
Microsoft Defender es compatible con Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, CentOS, RHEL, SLES y Oracle Linux, independientemente del entorno de escritorio que utilices. El software de seguridad funciona en las distribuciones que ya admite la versión de servidores. El único inconveniente es que necesitarás una suscripción a Microsoft 365 E5 o E7 para poder acceder después de la vista previa pública.

articles.title: 10 African startups named semi-finalists for $2m Milken-Motsepe Prize in Circular Economy - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Ten African startups have been named semifinalists for the Milken-Motsepe Prize in Circular Economy, and will share US$500,000 in unrestricted funding as they compete for the US$1 million grand prize.
The Milken-Motsepe Prize is aimed at companies in Africa revolutionising using different technologies to revolutionise the circular economy on the continent. Run by the Milken Institute and the Motsepe Foundation, the prize will distribute a total of US$2 million in non-dilutive capital to companies using technology to scale circular economy solutions across Africa. Alongside funding, participants receive mentorship, investor connections and global exposure.
The 10 semi-finalists have now been announced, who will be whittled down to five finalists by judges assessing them on commercial viability, scalability, workforce and social impact, and environmental impact. The grand prize winner will be announced at the 2027 Milken Institute Global Conference in Los Angeles, with a US$250,000 runner-up prize also on offer.
Kenya leads the way with three semi-finalists. Bottle Logistics East Africa combines digital reverse logistics with industrial glass recovery to turn discarded glass into returnable packaging, cullet and other products; Sanergy converts urban sanitation and organic waste into organic fertiliser, biochar and other agricultural inputs; and Safi Organics turns rice husks and sugarcane bagasse into a carbon-negative organic fertiliser.
Ethiopia, Tanzania and Egypt each have two startups in the running. From Ethiopia, EKT Trade and Investment manufactures products from plastic waste, and Zafree makes tree-free pulp and paper for the packaging industry using banana farm waste. Tanzania’s Country Materials uses AI to identify, trace and recover scrap metal for the continent’s steel industry, while SafeSip recycles plastic waste into pressure-rated resin and drip irrigation equipment.
The Egyptian contingent comprises Papyrus Egypt, which converts banana plantation waste into biodegradable packaging and liquid fertiliser, and Triple M Electrical and Electronic Contracting, which extends the lifespan of power infrastructure by purifying transformer oil and refurbishing transformers, switchgear and panels.
Nigeria’s Cold Hubs, which builds and runs solar-powered cold rooms, refrigerated trucks and reusable crates for food markets and farm clusters, completes the list.
“Africa is uniquely positioned to lead in this transition,” said Emily Musil, managing director at the Milken Institute, who added that the prize backs entrepreneurs turning resource efficiency into competitive, job-creating businesses.

The money will go towards five new Even hospitals in Bengaluru over the next six months, beginning with Indiranagar. The company runs two hospitals in the city at present.
The Pant Project bags Rs 109 Cr to accelerate retail expansion
The Pant Project, a premium menswear label specialising in trousers and other bottomwear, has raised Rs 109 crore in a Series B funding round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investments.
Existing investor Sorin Investments also participated, alongside family offices and angel investors including Anisha Saraf, B&K Securities, MGA Ventures and B2V Ventures. The company has also secured venture debt from Alteria Capital, with IndigoEdge advising on the equity transaction.
Founded by brothers Dhruv and Udit Toshniwal, The Pant Project began as a digital-first business focused on fit, fabric performance and comfort for Indian men. Its products include Malai Pants and Inklock No Fade Black Jeans, and it sells through its website, Myntra, Amazon and physical stores.
Other News
AngelBot AI launches TeamSync to secure enterprise knowledge with AI-powered search
AngelBot AI has launched TeamSync, an AI-native platform designed to help enterprises securely search, manage and extract insights from fragmented documents and information repositories.
The platform combines natural-language document interaction, semantic search and permissions-aware AI, with citations and audit trails to support reliable information access. Its capabilities also include metadata extraction, electronic signatures, contract lifecycle management and eDiscovery.
Targeting mid-sized and large enterprises across regulated and document-intensive sectors, TeamSync offers subscription-based software, platform licensing and implementation services. The launch builds on AngelBot AI’s document management work, including IMIR, which has received recognition from the Indian Air Force.
VETO launches sports carnival, offers 300+ hours of subscription-free live sports
VETO, India’s subscription-free OTT platform, has launched the VETO Sports Carnival, offering more than 300 hours of live sports streaming across cricket, football, weightlifting and tennis during October and November.
The line-up includes an international ODI tri-series, Test matches, the IWF World Senior Championships, SAFF Championship, Billie Jean King Cup Play-offs and Davis Cup Finals.
The initiative expands VETO’s live sports portfolio as it seeks to make international sporting events accessible to Indian audiences without a subscription fee. The platform also offers 60+ live TV channels across 12 languages and more than 10 content genres.
Yes Madam revenue hits Rs 402 Cr annualised run rate, grows 3.9x in two years
At-home beauty and wellness platform Yes Madam has reported a 3.9-fold increase in revenue and 3.5-fold growth in Net Transaction Value (NTV) between Q2 FY25 and Q2 FY27. The company’s annualised revenue run rate reached Rs 402 crore, while its NTV run rate stood at Rs 836 crore.
In Q2 FY27, revenue rose 69% year-on-year to Rs 79.4 crore, while NTV grew 75% to Rs 165.8 crore.
Founded in 2016, Yes Madam operates across more than 55 cities with a network of 10,000-plus service professionals. The company plans to expand services, strengthen its network and invest in technology.
So/Facet raises Rs 10 Cr seed funding led by Sauce to build lab-grown diamond jewellery brand
So/Facet, a premium lab-grown diamond jewellery brand founded by former Unilever executives Aarushi Agrawal Naulakha and Abhishek Naulakha, has raised Rs10 crore in a seed funding round led by Sauce.
The company will use the capital for brand building, design, technology, hiring and an omnichannel retail expansion. Set to launch online in November 2026, So/Facet plans to open more than 30 premium stores over three years.
The brand aims to position lab-grown diamonds as expressions of personal style rather than jewellery reserved for traditional milestones. Its six launch collections feature IGI-certified diamonds and contemporary, in-house designs.
Guttify targets Tier II markets in three states, eyes 5x growth in annual recurring revenue
Gut-health startup Guttify plans to expand into select Tier II markets across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Punjab through pilot initiatives in FY27, targeting fivefold growth in annual recurring revenue (ARR).
The company has served over 30,000 consumers and reported 67% quarter-on-quarter growth. Its Rs 399 DIY Gut Scan Kit sold approximately 15,000 units between January and August 2026, with around half of buyers subsequently purchasing other products.
Guttify plans to expand its portfolio with products including Poopie, a fibre-based constipation-support product, and RISE, a morning greens blend, while strengthening personalised recommendations, consumer education and expert guidance.
As You Asked raises Rs 45 lakh pre-seed funding to expand children’s nutrition products
As You Asked, a nutrition startup focused on children aged 2–12, has raised Rs 45 lakh in an equity-funded pre-seed round backed by ISB D-Labs and angel investors. The company will use the funds to support its market launch, product development, manufacturing and distribution.
Its planned portfolio includes daily nutrition powders, hydration mixes and micronutrient gummies without added sugars. The startup has engaged more than 100 parents, conducted over 200 child taste tests and run an early pilot involving 200-plus customers to inform its product development. It aims to make everyday nutrition simpler, accessible and easier for families to incorporate into daily routines.

articles.title: Google Traduction : la grande refonte de l'interface arrive enfin sur Android
articles.text:
Google Traduction s’offre un lifting important sur Android. Repérée sur plusieurs smartphones tournant sous la version 10.39.34.99 de l’application, la nouvelle interface évolue pour se rapprocher des standards graphiques Material 3 Expressive que l’on retrouve sur d’autres services de la marque.
Une nouvelle barre de navigation et plus de place pour saisir le texte
La barre de navigation en bas de l’interface adopte désormais un positionnement similaire à celui que l’on trouve déjà dans Google Photos ou Google Lens, par exemple. On remarque également que le champ de texte au centre est bien plus grand que sur la version précédente de l’interface.
L’ancien design à gauche, le premier redesign au milieu et le nouveau design à droite. – Source : Android Authority
Le bouton à trois points qui regroupait auparavant le sélecteur de modèle de traduction et l’option d’écriture manuscrite disparaît également. Cette dernière fonctionnalité bascule directement à l’intérieur de la boîte de texte, placée juste à côté d’une icône de microphone (légèrement modifiée elle aussi). Enfin, l’option pour coller le texte se trouve désormais sur la gauche.
Quelques compromis inévitables
En revanche, l’agrandissement important de la zone de saisie du texte laisse malheureusement trop peu de place pour afficher les raccourcis contextuels, comme celui de l’entraînement du jour ou de la reprise rapide d’une conversation. Les autres sections de l’application comme les onglets Traduction instantanée, Appareil photo et Entraînement, ne subissent pas de modifications majeures.
Source : Android Authority
À lire : Google Traduction veut faire le ménage dans nos hésitations orales
Côté graphique, on retrouve une cohérence des couleurs et des nouveaux éléments avec le style Material 3 Expressive de Google. Le déploiement de cette nouvelle version de Google Traduction se poursuit au compte-gouttes, ce qui signifie que vous devriez le voir arriver sur vos smartphones et tablettes Android dans les semaines à venir, si ce n’est pas déjà le cas.

articles.title: Dark Souls 2 cachait un immense colisée qui n’a jamais intégré le jeu
articles.text:
En avril 2026, nous vous parlions d’une scène coupée d’Elden Ring, retrouvée par des datamineurs dans les fichiers du jeu. Le titre de FromSoftware cachait une séquence cinématique qui n’avait jamais été intégrée au jeu, mais dormait encore dans ses profondeurs.
Des découvertes de ce genre, les datamineurs en font régulièrement. La dernière en date concerne, une fois encore, un jeu de FromSoftware. Doneda, un datamineur habitué à fouiller dans les jeux du studio, a publié le 5 octobre 2026, sur sa chaîne YouTube, une vidéo consacrée à la mystérieuse zone du Colisée de Dark Souls 2. Relayée par PC Gamer le 18 octobre, elle montre ce prototype de niveau, abandonné tôt dans le développement et jamais intégré au jeu.
La vidéo dévoile des couloirs interminables et des structures en pierre à l’architecture impossible, vestiges d’une zone jamais terminée par les développeurs. Le Colisée domine l’ensemble. Posé au milieu d’une zone inachevée, il rappelle l’esthétique des espaces liminaux et confère à l’ensemble une étrangeté presque onirique.
Le datamineur a par ailleurs découvert plusieurs environnements distincts, dont des mines, une portion de crypte et une tour souterraine qui aurait pu accueillir une série d’arènes. Impossible, malheureusement, de connaître leur fonction précise, ni de savoir où ces différentes zones auraient pu s’insérer dans la version finale de Dark Souls 2. Au vu de leur niveau de finition, ces environnements semblent avoir été abandonnés assez tôt dans le développement.
D’après PC Gamer, certaines portions semblent avoir formé une zone interconnectée, et l’ensemble pourrait être lié à ce qui est devenu la Crypte des Morts Vivants, la crypte que l’on traverse en fin de partie.
Une zone cachée de Dark Souls 2 explorée grâce à Elden Ring Nightreign
Pour explorer ces vestiges, Doneda a utilisé Elden Ring Nightreign, dans lequel il a importé les données des anciennes zones de Dark Souls 2 afin de pouvoir les parcourir. Une manipulation rendue possible par son travail de modding. Par le passé, il avait déjà réussi à adapter certains environnements du jeu à Nightreign, dont Eleum Loyce, une zone issue d’un contenu additionnel de Dark Souls 2.
Pour comprendre pourquoi certaines parties de Dark Souls 2 ont été abandonnées en cours de développement, il faut revenir sur la production mouvementée du jeu. Dans une interview publiée dans l’artbook Dark Souls II Design Works, traduite en anglais par le site Barnard Translations en 2018, le réalisateur Yui Tanimura reconnaît que le développement a été difficile : à mi-parcours, l’équipe a dû repenser le jeu dans son ensemble et revoir sa conception depuis le début. Plutôt que de tout recommencer, elle a dû réutiliser et adapter une grande partie des environnements et des éléments déjà créés, tout en respectant les délais.
Ce remaniement explique sans doute pourquoi de vastes zones inachevées dorment encore aujourd’hui dans les fichiers du jeu.

articles.title: iPhone Duo : la coque officielle d’Apple a une contrainte inattendue qui risque d’agacer les utilisateurs
articles.text:
L’iPhone Duo sort dans moins d’une semaine, et ses accessoires officiels sont déjà disponibles à l’achat. La coque officielle réserve pourtant une mauvaise surprise : elle tient sur le téléphone non pas grâce à des aimants, mais via un adhésif.
Vous aviez probablement déjà de nombreuses raisons de ne pas vouloir vous procurer l’iPhone Duo, à commencer par son prix exorbitant. Alors que les précommandes ont débuté il y a quelques jours, et que l’appareil se revend déjà à prix d’or sur eBay, les premiers accessoires de l’iPhone Duo commencent à arriver entre les mains des premiers acheteurs. Et l’une des protections officielles d’Apple pourrait bien ajouter une raison supplémentaire à cette liste : sa coque en silicone nécessite un adhésif pour tenir en place.
iPhone Duo : une coque en silicone qui nécessite un adhésif
Apple propose deux protections à l’achat : une coque en silicone à 89 euros et un folio avec béquille à 149 euros. C’est le modèle d’entrée de gamme qui nous intéresse aujourd’hui. Des utilisateurs ayant passé leur commande en avance ont remarqué, une fois le produit entre les mains, que la fixation ne fonctionnait pas exactement comme ils l’avaient imaginé. En effet, pour qu’elle reste correctement fixée au téléphone, il faut retirer le film qui protège l’adhésif intégré à la coque.
Pour son iPhone Duo, Apple a donc choisi une solution différente de la fixation magnétique que l’on retrouve sur certains accessoires. Sans cet adhésif, la coque risquerait de ne pas tenir suffisamment en place. Bien que ce type de fixation ne soit pas vraiment inédit pour les protections destinées aux smartphones pliants, force est de constater qu’il détone avec les habitudes de la marque à la pomme en matière d'accessoires.
Sur le papier, le principe peut évidemment fonctionner. Il impose en revanche une manipulation supplémentaire au moment de la première installation. Et surtout, il change la manière dont on manipule la coque au quotidien. Là où une protection classique se retire et se remet facilement, celle de l’iPhone Duo dépend d’un adhésif dont l’efficacité devrait diminuer après plusieurs manipulations.
Changer de coque deviendra forcément moins pratique
C’est là que la contrainte risque de se faire sentir auprès des utilisateurs. Ceux qui aiment alterner entre plusieurs coques, ou qui souhaitent tout simplement retirer leur protection de temps à autre (pour la nettoyer, par exemple), ne pourront pas le faire aussi librement qu’auparavant. Une fois la coque décollée, l’adhésif devrait perdre une partie de son efficacité, ce qui compliquera fatalement sa réinstallation.
Pour rappel, l’iPhone Duo est commercialisé à partir de 2 339 euros pour la version 256 Go, et il faut débourser pas moins de 3 889 euros pour la variante embarquant 2 To. La coque en silicone étant elle-même proposée à 89 euros, on aurait légitimement pu espérer de la part d’Apple un système plus robuste à ce niveau de prix.
Pour les utilisateurs que cette contrainte rebute (et qui en ont les moyens), la coque folio à 149 euros constitue donc la seule autre alternative officielle d’Apple. Plus chère, elle intègre néanmoins une béquille et ne semble pas être équipée du même système d’adhésif.
Source : 9to5Mac

articles.title: Mobilfunk aus dem All: Was europäische Anbieter planen – und warum Starlink wohl außen vor bleibt
articles.text:
Mobilfunk aus dem All: Was europäische Anbieter planen – und warum Starlink wohl außen vor bleibt
Europas große Telekommunikationskonzerne ziehen an einem Strang, um Handynutzer auch in entlegenen Gebieten mit Mobilfunk aus dem Weltall zu erreichen. Die Deutsche Telekom, der britische Anbieter Vodafone, Telefónica aus Spanien und Orange aus Frankreich teilten mit, dass sie gemeinsam für Frequenzen für mobile Satellitendienste bieten wollen. Eine entsprechende Absichtserklärung sei unterzeichnet worden. Es geht um Frequenzen, die aller Voraussicht nach 2029 frei werden und bislang etwa für Internetverbindungen im Flugzeug genutzt werden.
Man wolle eine flächendeckende Versorgung auch in unterversorgten Gebieten erreichen, die Resilienz mobiler Netze stärken, kritische Kommunikation schützen und die Entwicklung einer europäischen Satellitenkonstellation unterstützen, hieß es von den Unternehmen. Mit der Zusammenarbeit wolle man die eigenständige Position Europas im Bereich der Weltrauminfrastruktur sicherstellen. Man plane, zentrale Infrastrukturen am Boden sowie wichtige Koordinierungs- und Steuerungsfunktionen in Europa aufzubauen.
Weltraum-Funktion kommt erst noch in den Massenmarkt
Den Handykunden sollen Direct-to-Device-Dienste (D2D) angeboten werden – das Smartphone wird also da, wo bislang kein Handynetz ist, direkt mit Satelliten im Weltraum verbunden. Die meisten Smartphones haben diese D2D-Funktion bislang nicht integriert, in den kommenden Jahren dürfte das aber im Massenmarkt ankommen.
Es geht um weiße Flecken – also dort, wo Stand jetzt nicht mehr das veraltete 2G-Netz verfügbar ist. Bei der Deutschen Telekom waren das im Juni laut Bundesnetzagentur 1,2 Prozent der Fläche Deutschlands, bei Vodafone 1,7 Prozent und bei O2 Telefónica 1,6 Prozent. In solchen Gegenden sollen die Handynutzer künftig mit Satelliten im Weltraum verbunden werden. Wer der Satellitenbetreiber ist, ist noch unklar. Das Raumfahrtunternehmen SpaceX mit seinem Internetdienst Starlink von Elon Musk dürfte es nicht sein, da es bei dem Vorhaben der vier Firmen um europäische Souveränität geht.

articles.title: Disney+ : 10 films parfaits à voir en streaming pour Halloween 2026

Disney+ : 10 films parfaits à voir en streaming pour Halloween 2026
En quête du film idéal pour frissonner devant Disney+ ? Les Numériques vous propose sa sélection des dix meilleurs titres à voir sur la plateforme de streaming pour l'édition 2026 de Halloween.
C'est officiel : nous sommes en plein mois d'octobre, et dans la "spooky season" de Halloween ! Et entre une sculpture de citrouilles et une chasse aux friandises, rien de tel que de s'installer devant un film doucement terrifiant à voir sur Disney+.
La plateforme de streaming propose une belle sélection de longs-métrages pour se faire peur, mais encore faut-il savoir ce qui vaut le coup. C'est pour ça que Les Numériques a sélectionné pour vous 10 valeurs sûres et dix des meilleurs films à regarder pour frissonner à tous les âges.
Quels sont les meilleurs films à voir sur Disney+ pour Halloween ?
Casper
Un tout jeune fantôme, Casper, ronge son frein et s'ennuie à mourir en compagnie de ses oncles dans le manoir de Whipstaff. Quand une petite fille et son père viennent s'installer dans la maison hantée, il pense pouvoir enfin s'amuser...

Cette comédie musicale déjantée commence par une nuit d'orage, quand la voiture de Janet et Brad, un couple coincé qui vient de se fiancer, tombe en panne. Obligés de se réfugier dans un mystérieux château, ils vont faire la rencontre de ses occupants pour le moins bizarres, qui se livrent à de bien étranges expériences.

Les essais sur un babouin sont peu convaincants et après des fuites dans la presse, il décide de se téléporter lui-même. Seulement il ne s'aperçoit pas qu'une mouche fait partie du voyage.

articles.title: From Microservices to Agents: The Next Evolution of Distributed Systems
articles.text:
Key Takeaways
- Agentic AI systems shift distributed systems design from orchestrating services to orchestrating decisions made at runtime.
- Unlike microservices, agentic systems introduce non-deterministic execution paths driven by context, reasoning, and tool selection.
- Decision quality becomes a first-class reliability concern alongside latency, availability, and throughput.
- Production failure modes often manifest as silent degradation in reasoning quality rather than explicit system errors.
- Effective agentic architectures require bounded autonomy, evaluation loops, and hybrid deterministic fallback systems.
| This article is part of the "Agentic AI Architecture" article series. In this series, we try to establish agentic AI architecture as a new type of software architecture that will likely dominate the industry for years to come. The articles, written by industry experts, cover various elements and aspects of agentic AI architecture. We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream. | 
Distributed Systems Are Entering a New Phase
Over the past decade, microservices have reshaped how large-scale software systems are designed and operated. They enabled teams to decompose monoliths into independently deployable services, scale ownership boundaries, and evolve systems incrementally. For many organizations, microservices became the dominant model for building distributed systems at scale.
At their core, microservices solved a fundamental problem: how to decompose functionality across services and teams in a way that supports independent evolution while maintaining system reliability. They introduced explicit service boundaries, well-defined APIs, and predictable execution flows.
A new architectural shift is now emerging, driven by advances in large language models (LLMs) and reasoning systems. Rather than focusing on decomposing functionality, this new paradigm focuses on decomposing decisions. Systems are beginning to move from static orchestration models toward adaptive, runtime decision-making systems. This is the foundation of what is increasingly referred to as agentic AI.
Agentic systems differ from traditional services in a fundamental way. Instead of executing predefined logic, they dynamically determine which actions to take, which tools to use, and how to sequence multi-step reasoning processes. Execution is no longer fully specified at design time; it emerges at runtime based on context, goals, and intermediate outcomes.
This shift introduces new capabilities. Systems can become more adaptive, more context-aware, and better able to handle ambiguous or evolving inputs. At the same time, it introduces new forms of complexity that are not well addressed by traditional distributed systems thinking.
The goal of this article is to explore this transition in depth: how agentic AI architectures differ from microservices, what architectural patterns are emerging, what failure modes we are beginning to observe in production systems, and how observability and reliability practices must evolve. The discussion is grounded in experience operating large-scale distributed systems in domains such as search, recommendation, and serving infrastructure.
Microservices Solved Service Decomposition — Agents Solve Decision Decomposition
Figure 1: Execution Model: Microservices vs Agentic Systems
(Source: created by the author with OpenAI ChatGPT)
[Click here to expand image above to full-size]
Microservices architecture introduced a clear model for structuring distributed systems. Instead of a single monolithic application, systems were decomposed into services aligned with business capabilities. Each service owned a bounded context — a clearly defined domain of responsibility and data ownership — communicated via APIs, and could evolve independently.
This decomposition enabled faster deployment cycles, clearer ownership boundaries, and improved scaling characteristics. However, despite their flexibility, microservices still rely on deterministic execution. The control flow of a request is explicitly defined through service-to-service interactions.
In a typical microservices-based system, a request follows a well-understood path: it enters a service, is processed, calls downstream services in a defined sequence, and returns a response. Even in highly complex systems, the execution path is known in advance and encoded in the system's logic.
Agentic AI systems introduce a different model of execution. Instead of defining the full sequence of operations upfront, systems determine execution paths dynamically. Decisions about which tools to invoke, which data sources to query, and which strategies to apply are made at runtime.
This represents a shift from service decomposition to decision decomposition. Rather than distributing functionality across services, systems distribute reasoning across components that participate in a dynamic decision loop.
In practice, this means that execution is no longer a fixed pipeline but an adaptive process. A system may choose different candidate sources depending on context, dynamically adjust ranking strategies, or re-evaluate outputs based on intermediate results. The structure of execution becomes contingent on both input and evolving system state.
This change has profound implications for how we reason about distributed systems. It introduces flexibility but also reduces predictability. It replaces static workflows with dynamic reasoning paths, which are inherently more difficult to trace and debug.
What Makes Agentic Systems Fundamentally Different
Figure 2: Agentic System Architecture
(Source: created by the author with OpenAI ChatGPT)
[Click here to expand image above to full-size]
Agentic systems differ from traditional distributed systems in three key dimensions: control flow, state management, and failure semantics.
Control flow is no longer fixed. In microservices architectures, execution paths are designed and encoded ahead of time. In agentic AI systems, execution paths are determined at runtime based on context and intermediate reasoning. This introduces flexibility but also variability in system behavior, since different requests may trigger entirely different execution paths depending on user intent, retrieved information, or prior decisions made during execution.
The state also becomes more fluid and less strictly defined. Traditional systems rely on explicit state transitions and well-defined persistence models. Agentic systems, by contrast, often operate over an evolving execution context that is continuously updated as reasoning progresses. This context may include conversation history, intermediate plans, retrieved documents, ranking signals, tool outputs, or prior evaluation results.
Managing this evolving context becomes a core systems concern. Context often must propagate across multiple agents, tools, and services while remaining sufficiently consistent to support coherent downstream reasoning. In practice, many systems introduce shared context stores, execution-scoped memory, or structured reasoning artifacts to avoid context fragmentation and contradictory decisions across execution steps. As execution chains become longer, context management begins to resemble distributed state coordination problems seen in earlier generations of distributed systems.
Failure semantics also change. In traditional systems, failures are typically binary: a request succeeds or fails, a service responds or times out. In agentic systems, failures often manifest as degraded decision quality. The system may continue to operate but produce suboptimal outcomes due to incorrect reasoning, poor tool selection, stale context, or incomplete interpretation of intermediate results.
These differences fundamentally change how distributed systems behave in production environments. They also require new architectural patterns to manage complexity, reliably propagate context, and maintain predictable system behavior at scale.
Architectural Patterns in Agentic AI Systems
As agentic systems begin to appear in production environments, several architectural patterns are emerging. These patterns are not formal standards but rather recurring structures that help manage complexity and control variability in decision-making systems.
One common pattern is the separation of planning and execution responsibilities. In this model, a planning component is responsible for interpreting intent and determining a high-level strategy, while execution components perform deterministic operations such as data retrieval, transformation, or ranking. This separation allows systems to isolate non-deterministic reasoning from deterministic execution, improving reliability and traceability.
A second pattern involves the specialization of agents. Instead of relying on a single general-purpose agent, systems are increasingly composed of multiple specialized agents, each responsible for a distinct capability such as retrieval, ranking, evaluation, or orchestration. These agents collaborate to produce final outcomes.
This structure resembles service decomposition in microservices architectures, but applied to decision-making rather than data processing logic. While specialization improves reasoning quality and modularity, it also introduces coordination overhead and increases system complexity. Latency becomes more variable, and failure modes can propagate across agent interactions.
A third pattern is the integration of evaluation directly into execution loops. Instead of treating evaluation as an offline process, systems increasingly evaluate outputs during runtime. Based on evaluation results, systems may dynamically refine, retry, or adjust strategies.
This introduces feedback loops into execution, enabling more adaptive behavior. However, it also requires careful control to avoid excessive retries or runaway execution cycles. Constraints such as latency budgets, iteration limits, and confidence thresholds become essential for maintaining system stability.
A further emerging pattern is the introduction of tool abstraction layers. As agents interact with a growing number of services and APIs, teams are creating standardized interfaces for tool use. These abstraction layers decouple agent reasoning from underlying service implementations and provide a consistent mechanism for capability discovery and invocation.
Over time, this abstraction layer begins to resemble a platform for capabilities rather than a collection of individual services. It becomes a critical enabler for scaling agentic systems across teams and domains.
Across these patterns, a consistent theme emerges: complexity is shifting from service orchestration to decision orchestration. Systems are no longer primarily concerned with how services interact, but with how decisions are made, evaluated, and adapted over time.
Failure Modes in Agentic Distributed Systems
Figure 3: Silent Failure Modes in Agentic Systems
(Source: created by the author with OpenAI ChatGPT)
[Click here to expand image above to full-size]
Agentic systems introduce new failure modes that differ significantly from those observed in traditional distributed architectures. While microservices typically fail due to latency, availability issues, or data inconsistencies, agentic systems often fail due to degraded decision quality.
One important failure mode is cascading decision degradation. In traditional pipelines, failures propagate through explicit dependencies. In agentic systems, early incorrect decisions can subtly influence downstream reasoning, compounding degradation in output quality. For example, if a system selects suboptimal candidate sources early in execution, subsequent ranking and evaluation steps operate over reduced-quality inputs, amplifying the initial error.
This pattern is particularly relevant in large-scale search and recommendation systems, where early-stage candidate generation significantly influences downstream ranking quality. Even when infrastructure remains healthy, small shifts in early decisions can lead to noticeable changes in system outcomes.
Another failure mode is retry amplification driven by evaluation loops. Agentic systems often include mechanisms for evaluating output quality and retrying when results are insufficient. While this improves adaptability, it can also lead to excessive iteration cycles. Unlike traditional retry mechanisms tied to explicit errors, these retries are driven by subjective quality judgments, making them harder to bound and control.
Without proper constraints, evaluation-driven retries can increase latency, amplify backend load, and create unpredictable execution patterns.
A third failure mode is silent quality degradation. In many cases, system performance may degrade without triggering traditional operational alerts. Infrastructure metrics such as latency and error rate may remain stable, while user-facing quality deteriorates due to changes in decision-making behavior.
This is especially common in systems that rely on ranking, personalization, or recommendation logic. Small shifts in tool selection, reasoning strategies, or context interpretation can accumulate over time, leading to gradual but significant changes in system behavior. Detecting these issues requires evaluation-aware monitoring rather than infrastructure-centric observability.
Coordination overhead and latency accumulation also emerge as important concerns. As systems distribute reasoning across multiple agents, execution paths become more complex and less predictable. Each additional coordination step introduces variability in latency and increases the risk of partial failures.
Finally, state drift and context inconsistency can lead to reasoning errors across multi-step execution flows. When context is updated incrementally across agents or steps, inconsistencies in state propagation can result in contradictory or incomplete decisions. This is analogous to consistency challenges in distributed systems but manifests as reasoning drift rather than data inconsistency.
Observability and Reliability for Agentic Systems
Traditional observability models based on metrics such as latency, throughput, and error rate remain necessary but are insufficient for agentic systems. A new dimension of observability is required: decision quality.
Instead of only observing system health, teams must observe how decisions are made. This includes tracing tool selections, reasoning steps, intermediate outputs, and evaluation outcomes. Decision-level tracing provides visibility into how system behavior evolves over time and where degradation originates.
Monitoring changes in system behavior also becomes important. Over time, shifts in tool usage patterns, strategy selection frequencies, fallback rates, or retry behavior can indicate that the system’s decision-making process is drifting. For example, a sudden increase in retries or a strong preference toward a single strategy may signal degraded reasoning quality, stale context, or poor evaluation signals.
These behavioral shifts often surface problems earlier than traditional user-facing metrics such as engagement or latency. Observing how decisions are distributed across the system can therefore serve as an early warning mechanism to detect quality degradation before it becomes operationally visible.
Evaluation infrastructure plays a central role in reliability. Rather than being treated as an offline validation mechanism, evaluation becomes part of the runtime system. It provides feedback loops that guide execution and help maintain quality. However, these loops must be carefully constrained to avoid excessive iteration or instability.
Reliability in agentic AI architectures also depends on bounded autonomy. Systems must operate within clearly defined constraints such as latency budgets, retry limits, and reasoning depth boundaries. These constraints ensure that flexibility does not come at the cost of predictability.
Fallback mechanisms remain essential. Deterministic execution paths provide stability when agentic reasoning becomes uncertain or when system confidence is low. In many production systems, hybrid architectures that combine agentic decision-making with deterministic fallback pipelines offer a pragmatic balance between flexibility and reliability.
Progressive rollout strategies are also critical. AI-based capabilities should be introduced gradually through experimentation, shadow execution, and controlled deployment. This allows teams to build confidence in the system's behavior while limiting exposure to risk.
Ultimately, reliability in agentic systems requires a shift in mindset. Instead of treating failures as binary events, systems must be designed to degrade gracefully in decision quality while maintaining a predictable user experience.
The Road Ahead
Agentic AI architectures represent a natural evolution of distributed systems. Microservices enabled the decomposition of functionality; agentic systems enable the decomposition of decision-making.
This shift introduces new capabilities in adaptability, personalization, and dynamic execution. It also introduces new challenges in observability, reliability, and system design.
The most important implication is that distributed systems are no longer only about orchestrating services. They are increasingly about orchestrating decisions. This requires extending established principles of distributed systems engineering to a new layer of abstraction.
As organizations adopt agentic architectures, success will depend on combining flexibility with discipline. The same principles that enabled microservices to scale—clear boundaries, observability, reliability engineering, and platform thinking—will be essential in this new paradigm.
We are still early in this transition. However, the direction is becoming clear. Distributed systems are evolving from systems that execute workflows to systems that make decisions. Understanding and shaping this shift will define the next generation of large-scale software architecture.
