articles.title: ZIPIIH fala sobre preconceito nos games e a importância da representatividade LGBTQIA+
articles.text:
O universo dos games pode representar um espaço de acolhimento, diversão e conexão entre pessoas. Entretanto, para mulheres e integrantes da comunidade LGBTQIA+, participar desse ambiente ainda pode significar enfrentar preconceito e discriminação.
Em entrevista ao Olhar Digital, Zee “ZIPIIH” Oliveira, criadora de conteúdo, apresentadora, caster e ex-jogadora competitiva de League of Legends, falou sobre sua trajetória na indústria e a importância de ampliar a representatividade nos jogos e nos esportes eletrônicos.
Atualmente, ZIPIIH produz conteúdos voltados à cultura gamer e pop, com foco na inclusão de mulheres e pessoas LGBTQIA+.
De jogadora profissional a criadora de conteúdo
A relação de ZIPIIH com os videogames começou ainda na juventude, quando encontrou nos jogos uma alternativa para lidar com situações de bullying e com as limitações de viver em uma cidade pequena.
Foi em League of Legends que ela descobriu o cenário competitivo. Na época, a criadora enxergava a carreira profissional como uma das poucas possibilidades de conquistar visibilidade dentro dos esports.
“Eu achava que o único lugar e a única maneira de eu chegar nesse holofote era jogando profissionalmente”, contou.
Durante sua trajetória, ZIPIIH chegou a integrar a CNB, mas decidiu deixar as competições diante da pressão e da rotina intensa de treinamentos.
Na pandemia, passou a investir em transmissões ao vivo e na produção de vídeos, atividade pela qual já demonstrava interesse desde a infância.
A decisão também foi influenciada pelo contato com outras pessoas LGBTQIA+ que atuavam como criadoras de conteúdo e apresentadoras, mostrando que existiam oportunidades além da carreira de jogadora.
Preconceito ainda dificulta a participação nos jogos online
Apesar do crescimento da representatividade nos games, ZIPIIH considera que mulheres e pessoas LGBTQIA+ ainda enfrentam dificuldades para participar de partidas online.
Segundo a criadora, situações de discriminação podem começar em interações simples, como utilizar o chat de voz para se comunicar com outros jogadores.
Ela cita VALORANT como um dos ambientes em que vivenciou esse problema.
Para ZIPIIH, a hostilidade não está relacionada apenas à comunidade de um jogo específico, mas também a questões sociais que se reproduzem nos ambientes digitais.
A criadora também questionou a necessidade de separar determinadas competições em categorias inclusivas e mistas. Embora reconheça a intenção de ampliar a participação de grupos historicamente excluídos, ela defende que o objetivo de longo prazo deve ser permitir que todas as pessoas tenham oportunidades de competir nos mesmos espaços.
Representatividade ajuda a construir comunidades mais inclusivas
Durante a entrevista, ZIPIIH destacou a importância de encontrar identificação tanto nos personagens quanto em outros jogadores e criadores de conteúdo.
Ela recomenda que pessoas que enfrentam dificuldades para encontrar ambientes acolhedores procurem comunidades com interesses semelhantes, acompanhem criadores LGBTQIA+ e construam suas próprias redes de apoio.
A experiência pessoal também influenciou seu trabalho. Ao perceber a ausência de determinados perfis nos espaços que desejava ocupar, decidiu buscar essas oportunidades e contribuir para que outras pessoas pudessem fazer o mesmo.
“Não deixa de fazer as coisas que você gosta e que você ama, porque não tem um espaço para você”, afirmou.
Para a criadora, a representatividade precisa ir além da presença de personagens diversos nos jogos. Ela também deve alcançar as transmissões, a produção de conteúdo, os campeonatos e as oportunidades profissionais dentro da indústria.
Criação de conteúdo como ferramenta de inclusão
Atualmente, ZIPIIH utiliza suas plataformas para produzir vídeos, realizar transmissões e promover discussões sobre diversidade nos games e na cultura pop.
A criadora também mencionou iniciativas como um campeonato inclusivo de VALORANT, além de conteúdos voltados à linguagem e às experiências da comunidade LGBTQIA+.
Entretanto, reconhece que manter esses ambientes exige esforço constante, especialmente diante de conflitos e manifestações de preconceito nas redes sociais.
Para ZIPIIH, valorizar criadores que trabalham pela inclusão é uma maneira de fortalecer comunidades e ampliar a presença de diferentes públicos na indústria.
Sua trajetória mostra como a criação de conteúdo pode abrir caminhos profissionais nos esports e contribuir para uma discussão mais ampla sobre respeito, pertencimento e representatividade no universo gamer.
Rachele Victoria é formada em Letras, MBA em Inovação e atua há 10 anos com comunicação e conteúdo gamer.

articles.title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
articles.text:
A hacker broke into more than 100 websites using an army of AI agents that mostly operated on their own, according to findings from the AI security firm Norforge. Though Norforge doesn’t name the targets, Reuters reports that the victims included companies like John Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins.
A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
The AI agents carried out the attacks with little involvement from the human hacker.
Concerns over AI-powered cybersecurity breaches have grown as the technology grows more advanced, with hackers using the tools to carry out large-scale attacks. At the same time, rogue AI agents are carrying out attacks of their own after escaping from testing environments.
Researchers at Norforge uncovered the attacks through exposed work on Cairn, an open-source AI platform that describes itself as a “general-purpose problem-solving engine.” With Cairn, users set a start and end point for the AI agents, which document their progress as they move forward with the task. However, as noted by Norforge, hackers can also use the tool to orchestrate cyberattacks using AI agents.
The hacker who broke into more than 100 sites was the “most active” among the exposed Cairn instances discovered by Norforge, waging attacks on companies based in the US, Canada, Australia, and Japan, as reported by Reuters. This attacker laid out “preferred intrusion tactics” using fewer than 100 Chinese characters, with successful breaches taking about 23 hours, according to Reuters. Overall, Nordforge found more than 20 exposed Cairn instances that are “likely malicious.”
In a statement to Reuters, a John Deere spokesperson said there is “no indication that sensitive information was accessed” as a result of the attack, while Cummins said it’s “investigating the report of a potential cyber-attack on a website operated by one of our third-party vendors.”
Meanwhile, SharkNinja says the breach impacted a standalone site with product support information, and that it has contained the threat. John Deere, Cumms, and SharkNinja didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.
Nordforge says it’s working to get the malicious Cairn instances taken down. Cairn’s creator, who goes by @le1xia0, said earlier this month that the platform “was never a ‘hacking tool,’” adding that “misuse is a human decision, not a feature of the engine.”

articles.title: Why Physical AI Is So Hard To Engineer
articles.text:
Integrating sensors, compute, and actuators into autonomous systems adds new challenges for chip design.
Key Takeaways:
Physical AI is changing how chips are designed and used, integrating sensing, AI inference, and real-time control into machines that can safely and predictably interact with the physical world.
The challenges extend well beyond just performance. Engineers need to account for corner cases stemming from unpredictable environments, ensure these systems are safe and reliable, and they need to future-proof these systems by ensuring they are serviceable and upgradable. This will require new tools and methodologies, as well as some new design approaches.
“AI is leaving the screen,” says Anthony Matarazzo, head of physical AI, digital twins, simulation-driven AI, and accelerated computing at Synopsys. “It is no longer about generating text or code. It is entering the physical world. It needs to understand, interact, sense, make decisions in a physical environment. We are moving from generative AI to agentic workflow orchestration to physical AI (see figure 1.) That is literally making intelligence actionable. But the consequences of being wrong fundamentally change. Life or death, plus or minus 1%.”
Fig. 1: Three Eras of AI. Source: Synopsys
Physical AI must see and interact with the real world. “It is challenging to make artificial intelligence see the world correctly,” says Chun-Ting “Tim” Wang-Lee, signal integrity application scientist at Keysight EDA. “Real-world information comes from the sensors, and the data has to be moved somewhere and processed so that the AI can decide and then act. There are decisions that need to be made.”
This changes the design priorities. “Physical AI usually gets framed as a compute story,” says Justin Endo, director for marketing and sales at Mixel, A Silvaco Company. “But from our perspective it has really been an imaging story. Every robot, drone, and autonomous system comes down to cameras feeding an inference engine.”
Physical AI builds on some of the connectivity and sensing technologies developed for the Internet of Things. “IoT was largely about connecting and monitoring things,” says Brad Rex, head of physical AI, UX at Renesas Electronics. “Physical AI is about giving machines the ability to perceive and act autonomously in unstructured environments. This is a completely orthogonal engineering problem, and it requires a step-change in system-level content — more sensing, more real-time compute, more sophisticated power management, and more safety considerations per device.”
Within physical AI, there are two distinct classes of devices: “Those that can rely on a cloud connection and those that must operate fully locally without relying on connectivity,” says Ashley Stevens, director of product management and marketing at Arteris. “For example, vehicles cannot rely on continuous connectivity, as there are many locations where cellular coverage is inadequate. In contrast, an industrial robotic arm moves but is constrained to a particular location within a factory setting, and therefore can be connected to the cloud.”
Others agree. “Unlike traditional AI applications that primarily generate information, physical AI systems influence real-world outcomes through continuous interaction with their environment,” says William Chen, product marketing group director for design IP at Cadence. “Traditional IoT often focused on collecting and transmitting data. Physical AI adds real-time interpretation and action. The result is a shift from connected devices to intelligent systems operating within sensing and control loops.”
This requires new architectures and new methodologies. “The entire architecture is very different,” says Satish Radhakrishnan, head of semiconductor and electronics at Vinci. “Time-to-market is going to be much slower because people are still learning. Physical AI is the next step that they want, but the switch to it is not going to be easy. The easiest entry point will be a repetitive action, but people are not willing to pay much for that. They want it to do a lot more. That’s why it is going to take a more complex architecture to build, make reliable, and make it work for at least a day on a single charge.”
It also requires significant processing power. “Robotics and drones require powerful, efficient compute capable of multimodal processing and accurate, real-time responsiveness in dynamic settings,” says Sameer Sharma, associate vice president for MediaTek’s IoT business. “Because of latency and bandwidth constraints, these devices require silicon capable of handling AI workloads at the edge, including AI acceleration for machine vision and object classification.”
As systems get larger or more capable, additional challenges emerge. “You need longer reach through moving joints, aggregation of many cameras into few ports, and the functional safety expectations coming over from automotive,” says Mixel’s Endo. “But the standard is already moving in that direction. The mobile camera interface is becoming the robot’s optic nerve, and that mobile-proven maturity is hard for any alternative to match.”
How quickly physical AI is adopted by different markets will vary, but the overall projections are noteworthy. At a high level, PwC estimates the global physical AI market will reach ~€430 billion by 2030, with “significant upside potential as systems scale and mature.” Deloitte, meanwhile, found that 58% of companies report at least limited use of physical AI today, with that number projected to rise to 80% within two years.
Not all sectors will adopt this technology at the same time. “Physical AI is not just AI at the edge,” says Frank Schirrmeister, executive director of strategic programs for system solutions at Synopsys. “It is broader than just robotics, but it will be uneven. The question is how quickly each industry will adopt physical AI. It requires you to go beyond the chip to the full physics. The growth inflection comes when you have this full loop of sensing, reasoning, physical action, and then autonomy. It’s really a platform transition where everything is being elevated up to the system level.”
New markets have repeatedly driven changes in the semiconductor ecosystem. “We believe physical AI is one of the most disruptive AI opportunities of the next several years,” says Sanjay Gupta, co-founder and president at Velaura AI. “We see it as a category of its own, rather than another set of IoT products. Industry estimates vary, but several point to a multi-trillion-dollar total addressable market over the next 10 years across robotics, drones, industrial automation, logistics, healthcare, and defense.”
In many cases, it will be market pressure that dictates when a sector advances. “The clearest near-term applications are in industrial and logistics settings,” says Renesas’ Rex. “Humanoid and non-humanoid robots handling repetitive or physically demanding tasks in factories, warehouses and supply chains, where labor shortages make automation valuable, and the environment is structured enough to deploy safely today.”
While many point to safety and security concerns, there are multiple ways to look at that. “Physical AI is enabling new ways to make essential work safer, more efficient and more productive,” says Robert Day, director of go-to-market, physical AI at Arm. “We’re already seeing autonomous machines move toward practical work in manufacturing, logistics and transportation. These industries represent an estimated $200 billion annual compute opportunity in the 2030s.”
Deployment in some sectors will likely be slower than others, but the overall industry could show rapid growth. “Each category is going to be separate and see slow growth, but there will be many sectors growing in parallel,” says Vinci’s Radhakrishnan. “Each requires new-age AI, new compute, and this will impact the speed at which it’s going to develop. One area may take longer to grow deep, but before it fully penetrates one market segment, it will enter multiple new market segments. Together it’s going to grow.”
But they all require some advances in areas such as training and simulation before that happens. “We know that the Internet trained generative AI, but what’s going to train physical AI?” asks Synopsys’ Matarazzo. “This is the big question that companies are asking. Reality has rules.”
Modularity
Physical AI systems are not like mobile phones that quickly get replaced when a new model comes out. Cars, robots, and drones have much higher initial cost, and they are expected to last many years. This indicates that many physical AI systems will need to be updatable, not just in terms of software or even AI models, but hardware, sensors, and actuators, as well.
Physical AI systems will continue to evolve as models and use cases change. “A consistent compute foundation across development and deployment can help teams carry software forward instead of rebuilding individual components for each generation,” says Arm’s Day. “Turning the opportunity into growth will ultimately depend on making autonomous machines efficient, responsive and reliable enough to deploy at scale.”
“Autonomous vehicles have been there for some time, but the older ones can’t be retrofitted to the newer techniques, camera sensors, etc.,” says Radhakrishnan. “The design of physical AI needs to go into some form of modular systems. Maybe you have a compute system that can be taken out and replaced, or a new sensor. People may be okay with paying 10% of the original cost every two or three years to update certain things, and the software updates keep coming in. This is what is going to keep refreshing this.”
The ability to do this needs to be addressed at the initial design stage. “Given how quickly robot architectures are evolving, we design for headroom rather than attempting to predict a fixed end state,” says Rex. “That means greater compute margin, scalable power architectures, and modular subsystem designs that can absorb additional sensing or intelligence without a full redesign. We are developing next-generation devices and evaluating how to optimize across multiple vectors such as power, compute, scalability, and efficiency to determine the right balance. We also rely on distributed architectures, so that as capability needs grow, it is often a matter of adding or upgrading a subsystem rather than replacing the entire platform. That approach, combined with software and reference-design platforms that can be updated over time, helps customers avoid designing themselves into a corner.”
More future-proofing is required than in many previous embedded or edge systems. “Physical AI deployments often have long operational lifetimes, yet must accommodate evolving AI models, new sensors, changing workloads, and increasing autonomy requirements,” says Cadence’s Chen. “Therefore, future-proofing is less about maximizing raw performance and more about building architectural flexibility. Multi-die architectures, scalable memory subsystems, high-speed interconnects, and standards-based interfaces provide mechanisms for adapting systems as requirements change. The challenge is that many infrastructure decisions become difficult to change once they are embedded into the system. Memory architecture, communication fabrics, and interface choices frequently determine the practical limits of future expansion.”
Real-time constraints
While real-time constraints have been a fundamental aspect of many embedded systems, physical AI will take this to a much higher level of complexity. It may not be possible to make many of the simplifications used in the past, such as not using cache memory because it introduces non-predictable response times.
The scale of the compute problem alone is unprecedented. “For chips designed for physical AI, the biggest limitation is predictability under real operating conditions,” says Alex Burlak, executive vice president of engineering and customer success at proteanTecs. “Consider a humanoid robot. It may have a powerful central compute system serving as its ‘brain,’ but throughout its body there can be dozens of MCUs and other devices controlling motors, joints, sensors, power and communications. A timing issue or degradation in one of those devices may not simply mean an application runs a little slower. It could mean a joint responds differently than expected, a sensor input arrives late, or an actuator behaves outside its intended parameters.”
Translating a system’s understanding of its surroundings into precise actions is complex. “Physical environments are unpredictable, and sensor data can be noisy, so systems need to handle uncertainty and continue adapting as conditions change,” says MediaTek’s Sharma. “That requires a software stack that connects perception, navigation, decision-making, and control, and supports the application-specific models, runtimes, and tools.”
This requires a different focus. “Traditional AI infrastructure is often optimized for throughput, utilization, and scale,” says Chen. “Physical AI systems must satisfy latency, power, reliability, safety, and environmental requirements while responding to continuously changing inputs. A correct answer delivered too late may be operationally equivalent to a wrong answer. As a result, physical AI introduces a different optimization target. The goal is not simply maximizing compute performance. It is maintaining predictable system behavior across sensing, memory, compute, communication, and actuation.”
It becomes a more complex optimization problem. “Physical AI systems need to process sensor data, and reason and act in real time within tight constraints on size, power, and weight,” says Day. “They require more than capable AI models. Hardware and software must be designed together around these workloads, from low-power sensing and real-time control to demanding AI processing.”
The whole system becomes a part of the timing constraint. “This is a prime example of where hardware/software co-design matters most,” says Rex. “The complexity across multiple domains will become even more significant going forward, spanning not only electronics, but mechanical design and battery technology, as well. Many of these disciplines, which were once addressed somewhat independently, now represent a larger challenge because they must be solved concurrently rather than in isolation. Because physical AI systems have to reconcile AI inference with deterministic, safety-critical control, the silicon and the software cannot be optimized separately and expected to integrate successfully. The system architecture, the real-time software, and the underlying compute and power hardware all have to be designed together from the outset.”
This methodology change has been brewing for a long time. “Physical AI arguably represents one of the strongest cases for hardware/software co-design,” says Chen. “Control-loop behavior emerges from interactions between sensing, memory access, inference execution, communication, and actuation. Improving software alone cannot overcome infrastructure bottlenecks, and faster hardware does not automatically improve system behavior if data delivery, synchronization, or timing remain constrained. The architecture must be considered end-to-end.”
What does real-time AI even mean? “Will AI always be fast enough to get this control back to the actuator?” asks Synopsys’ Schirrmeister. “The engineering challenges are behavioral. Get those real scenarios done, then deal with the uncertainty of making sure that it’s not leading to catastrophic failures. Hardware software will become even more critical. You really need to be flexible in being able to upgrade and then also, for safety reasons, stop where you can’t go.”
The challenge is not simply building faster chips or more capable AI models. Physical AI systems must coordinate sensing, computation, and actuation while remaining predictable under changing operating conditions. That will require new approaches to system architecture, hardware/software co-design, and verification, particularly as these machines become more autonomous and remain in service for longer periods.
Editor’s note: Future stories in this series will examine how physical AI systems learn and adapt, how engineers account for aging and degradation, and how verification methodologies can help prevent incorrect or unsafe behavior.

articles.title: Researchers train AI to detect concealed handguns using Wi-Fi signals — open-source WiFireNet achieves precision detection on older 802.11a standard by analyzing how weapons distort wireless signals
articles.text:
Researchers train AI to detect concealed handguns using Wi-Fi signals — open-source WiFireNet achieves precision detection on older 802.11a standard by analyzing how weapons distort wireless signals
The experimental prototype cannot pinpoint the weapon's location on the carrier
A group of AI researchers at the Swedish Defense Research Agency (FOI) has developed an AI system that can identify concealed handguns using Wi-Fi signals, offering a non-intrusive alternative to visible cameras and cumbersome metal detectors. Detailed in a paper posted on arXivWi-Fi on October 13, the system, called WiFireNet, analyzes channel state information from how an object distorts ambient Wi-Fi signals. The full system comprises a Wi-Fi transmitter, a Wi-Fi receiver, and the WiFireNet AI.
When ordinary Wi-Fi signals encounter an object in their path, they penetrate and bounce off in ways specific to that object, based on its shape, orientation, and material. This data, the channel state information, can be analyzed to identify the object with high accuracy. Security researchers previously disclosed a technique that lets ordinary Wi-Fi routers identify people with 99.5% accuracy.
To build the WiFireNet system, the researchers first created a dataset, dubbed the WiFire Dataset, by simultaneously recording RGB footage and the reflected Wi-Fi signals of people walking around with objects ranging from phones to handguns. The researchers then trained a deep learning model on the massive dataset, using video clips to match the visuals of a concealed handgun with its specific Wi-Fi signature, or channel state information. To ensure the system could specifically distinguish a handgun from everyday items of similar shape or material, the researchers trained it on recordings of a plastic handgun, a metal water bottle, a real metal handgun, and a phone.
After training, the final AI system, WiFireNet, could detect concealed handguns solely based on Wi-Fi CSI, with varying accuracy. In controlled trials tracking up to four moving individuals in a small indoor space, the system achieved an average handgun-detection precision of 72.5%. However, under stricter localization requirements, such as pinpointing the weapon’s exact location on the carrier, precision dropped to 53.8%. The neural network also struggles to perform accurately in unfamiliar, untested indoor layouts.
That said, the system is still experimental, with a roadmap of planned improvements. The prototype was built using a modified implementation of the older 1999 wireless IEEE 802.11a standard to establish proof of concept. Subsequent phases will use modern Wi-FI 7 and Wi-Fi 8 networks with higher-resolution CSI for better detection. The researchers made the project open source, releasing the code, models, and dataset to support further research in the field. Wi-Fi sensing is gaining popularity as an effective surveillance technology that doesn't require complex gear or setups. However, critics argue that the technology's ubiquity and the lack of regulatory frameworks raise serious privacy concerns.

He is a mechanical engineer and senior technical writer with over nine years of experience in documentation and reporting. He is deeply passionate about all things engineering and technology, and is an expert in gadgets, manufacturing, robotics, automotive, and aerospace.

More likely this is some data that will be proven wrong by a different group in the future. The guys that wrote it seem similar to university groups that must publish stuff to keep there funding. Little is done when the published studies are found to be incorrect in the future. At best they write a small disclaimer but they are too busy publishing their next set of nonsense so they keep getting their paycheck from some source that tends to funded by taxpayers. Reply

articles.title: The Pant Project bags Rs 109 Cr to accelerate retail expansion
articles.text:
The Pant Project bags Rs 109 Cr to accelerate retail expansion
The Pant Project is targeting a larger role in premium menswear after raising Rs 109 crore to expand retail outlets and develop new product categories.
The Pant Project, a premium menswear label specialising in trousers and other bottomwear, has raised Rs 109 crore in a Series B funding round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investments.
Existing investor Sorin Investments also participated, alongside family offices and angel investors including Anisha Saraf, B&K Securities, MGA Ventures and B2V Ventures. The company has also secured venture debt from Alteria Capital, with IndigoEdge advising on the equity transaction.
Founded by brothers Dhruv and Udit Toshniwal, The Pant Project began as a digital-first business focused on fit, fabric performance and comfort for Indian men. Its products include Malai Pants and Inklock No Fade Black Jeans, and it sells through its website, Myntra, Amazon and physical stores.
Sorin partner Mandar Dandekar said revenue had grown “more than 5x” since its Series A, alongside what he described as “industry-leading repeat rates.”
The new capital will help the company expand from 25 exclusive stores to more than 150 over the next two to three years. It also plans to widen its range to jeans, athleisure, meaning clothing suited to exercise and everyday use, and casualwear, while investing in retail technology to connect online and in-store shopping.
Chief executive officer Dhruv Toshniwal said its digital beginnings had provided “the data, the product knowledge and the brand equity to now go deep offline.”
The expansion highlights a wider shift among direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, which sell directly to customers through their own channels. A recent report by WPP Media, Google and Elevation Capital, in partnership with Kantar, said brands need broader distribution to grow from around Rs 100 crore to Rs 500 crore in revenue.
A CMAI-1Lattice estimate projects India’s apparel market to grow from $96 billion in 2025 to $146 billion by 2029.
The Pant Project is entering a competitive funding market. Menswear brand Snitch raised $40 million in a Series B round led by 360 ONE Asset in June 2025. Meanwhile, House of Chikankari raised Rs 25 crore from Cap Alpha Ventures in April 2026 to expand its product range and physical presence.
On the manufacturing side, the government revised its textile production-linked incentive scheme in October 2025, widening eligible man-made-fibre apparel and fabric categories and easing investment requirements. The application window was subsequently extended through March 2026.

articles.title: Des agents IA de Google DeepMind ont bouclé Minecraft en 27 heures en se répartissant les tâches
articles.text:
Ils s’appellent janesick, gyldenia, auratian et bulicame. Ce sont des joueurs de Minecraft, mais pas des humains. Ils ont pourtant bouclé le jeu de Mojang en 27 heures et 14 minutes.
Sans l’aval de Microsoft ni de Mojang, des chercheurs de Google DeepMind ont lancé quatre agents Gemini 4 Argon, modèle d’IA haut de gamme présenté le 30 septembre et déployé depuis le 13 octobre. Maxence Faldor a présenté les résultats sur X le 16 octobre : les quatre agents ont terminé Minecraft, alors qu’ils n’ont même pas été développés pour cette tâche.
Il n’a fallu qu’un peu plus d’une journée au dernier modèle d’IA de Google pour terminer Minecraft
Maxence Faldor explique qu’aucun rôle n’a été assigné aux quatre agents, qui ont « planifié, écrit et débuggué tous les programmes d’eux-mêmes ». Selon les chercheurs, c’est la première fois que des agents d’IA terminent Minecraft de bout en bout sans aide humaine, sur un monde tiré au hasard et sans outil propre au jeu écrit par des humains. Gemini 4 Argon s’est appuyée sur ce qu’elle avait lu de Minecraft sur le web pendant son entraînement. « Les agents n’ont jamais vu le moindre pixel ni appuyé sur aucune touche. Chaque agent agissait en écrivant un court programme, du type « marche jusqu’à ces coordonnées et mine tout le minerai de fer situé dans un rayon de 16 blocs ». Ils lisaient également le résultat produit par l’exécution du programme, notamment la mise à jour de leur position, de leur santé et de leur inventaire, ou l’erreur générée », explique Maxence Faldor.
Dix minutes à peine après avoir été lâchés dans Minecraft, les quatre agents s’étaient réparti les tâches sur le chat du jeu. L’un fabriquait les outils, un autre rassemblait de la nourriture, un troisième creusait à la recherche de diamants et le dernier construisait le portail vers le Nether. Maxence Faldor résume l’enjeu : « Terminer Minecraft nécessite de maintenir un plan cohérent à travers des milliers d’étapes dépendantes les unes des autres pendant plus d’une journée. En collaborant avec succès, en dépassant de multiples échecs et en poursuivant un objectif commun sans aucune intervention humaine, ces agents ont prouvé qu’ils sont capables de gérer la résolution de problèmes complexes, ouverts et à long terme, nécessaires aux tâches d’ingénierie logicielle et de recherche. »
Les agents ont fini par abattre l’Ender Dragon, le boss final, que des cristaux soignent en continu. Le combat a engendré 69 morts, sur les 605 de toute la partie. Entre chaque échec, ils ont su tirer des enseignements pour être meilleurs lors de la tentative suivante. Détruire les dix cristaux qui le régénèrent puis abattre le dragon ont quand même nécessité près de 14 heures, soit plus de la moitié de la performance.
Pour situer le résultat, il faut environ 45 heures pour boucler l’aventure principale (en médian), selon le site HowLongToBeat. Le record de vitesse sur un monde tiré au hasard est, lui, sous les sept minutes. Les agents vont donc plus vite qu’un joueur moyen, mais avec bien plus d’échecs et de tâtonnements qu’un humain aguerri.
Si impressionné soit-il, Maxence Faldor note quand même quelques limites : les agents ont joué en mode facile et se sont appuyés sur Mineflayer, une bibliothèque de code libre qui leur indiquait exactement où se trouvaient les blocs et les créatures, même derrière la roche, ainsi que sur un module qui calculait leurs trajets. Notez qu’un cinquième agent s’est chargé de mener des observations, notamment pour déceler des triches. Ni lui ni les chercheurs n’en ont relevé. « L’agent observateur indépendant et notre audit manuel des journaux d’événements ont confirmé que l’équipe a gagné uniquement grâce à des mécaniques de jeu de survie classiques », assure Maxence Faldor. Il estime que ces résultats pourront être appliqués afin de « relever des défis complexes du monde réel, en apportant une intelligence collaborative et à long terme à l’ingénierie logicielle, la recherche scientifique, le design et la robotique ».

articles.title: FritzOS 8.40 steht bereit: Was das Labor-Update auf deine Fritzbox bringt
articles.text:
FritzOS 8.40: Was die Labor-Version bringt – und welche Fritzboxen das Update jetzt erhalten
Updates für Fritzboxen können im ersten Moment etwas verwirrend sein. Denn nicht alle Geräte bekommen dieselben Aktualisierungen spendiert. Manche Fritz-Router bekommen langsamer neue Versionsnummern, während andere immer die neuesten Funktionen erhalten. Dazu kommt, dass es neben den fertigen Updates auch noch Laborversionen für Fritzboxen gibt. Dabei handelt es sich um das Betaprogramm, mit dem du vor allen anderen einen Blick auf neue Updates werfen kannst.
FritzOS 8.40 steht für diese Router bereit
Und genau ein solches Labor-Update wurde jetzt für eine Reihe von Fritzboxen bereitgestellt. FritzOS 8.40 wurde zunächst nur für einige wenige Router veröffentlicht. Jetzt hat Fritz den Test aber auf weitere Modelle ausgeweitet. Diese Fritz-Router können das Update jetzt herunterladen:
- Fritzbox 4050
- Fritzbox 4630
- Fritzbox 4690
- Fritzbox 5590 Fiber
- Fritzbox 5690 Pro
- Fritzbox 5690 XGS
- Fritzbox 6660
- Fritzbox 6670
- Fritzbox 6850 5G
- Fritzbox 6850 5G V2
- Fritzbox 6850 4G
- Fritzbox 6850 LTE
- Fritzbox 6690
- Fritzbox 6690 Pro
- Fritzbox 7510
- Fritzbox 7530 AX
- Fritzbox 7590 AX
- Fritzbox 7590
- Fritzbox 7620
- Fritzbox 7630
- Fritzbox 7690
- Fritz-Repeater 6000
- Fritz-Repeater 3000 AX
- Fritz-Repeater 1200 AX
- Fritz-Mesh-Set 1600
Um an der Beta teilzunehmen, müssen interessierte Fritz-User:innen das Update für die Router manuell von der Webseite des Herstellers herunterladen. Anschließend kannst du in die Weboberfläche des Routers wechseln und dort unter „System“ den Bereich „Update“ aufrufen. Dort lässt sich die FritzOS-Datei einfügen und auf dem Router installieren. Wie bei allen Betaprogrammen solltest du dir aber im Klaren sein, dass es noch zu etwaigen Problemen kommen kann. Muss deine Fritzbox rund um die Uhr reibungslos funktionieren, solltest du lieber auf den finalen Release von FritzOS 8.40 warten.
Was steckt in FritzOS 8.4?
Je nach Modell sind die Neuerungen von FritzOS 8.4 recht unterschiedlich. Die Fritzbox 5590 Fiber bekommt etwa neue Filterlisten für DNS-Anfragen aus dem Heim- und Gastnetz sowie mehr Auslöser für Smarthome-Routinen und eine Überlastungsschaltung für smarte Fritz-Steckdosen. Bei anderen Modellen wie der Fritzbox 7590 AX ist die Liste der Neuerungen schon deutlich länger.
Denn das Spitzenmodell von Fritz bekommt eine neue Priorisierungsfunktion, die automatisch für die beste Internetverbindung sorgen soll, einen Einrichtungsassistenten für den Wechsel von DSL auf Glasfaser sowie eine automatisierte Erkennung und Priorisierung von Videokonferenzen. Neu für viele Fritzboxen ist zudem ein SOS‑Ruf, mit dem vier Notfallnummern hinterlegt werden können, die automatisch im Ernstfall nacheinander kontaktiert werden.
Zudem gibt es einen einfachen Modus für Fritz-Fon, um die Barrierefreiheit beim Telefonieren für ältere Menschen zu verbessern. Für Menschen mit körperlicher Einschränkung lassen sich bei DECT-Telefonen mit FritzOS 8.40 zudem Softkeys als Schnellwahltasten einrichten und so mit einer Funktion oder einer Rufnummer belegen. Sämtliche Funktionen und Neuerungen für deine Fritzbox kannst du auf dieser Fritz-Webseite sehen, wenn du dein Fritzbox-Modell aus dem Dropdown-Menü auswählst.

articles.title: British payments unicorn Zilch invests €91 million in larger London headquarters amid continued growth | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Zilch, the British intelligent payments unicorn with 6 million customers, has today announced it is committing €91 million (£77 million) to double its London office capacity with a move to a significantly larger headquarters in Victoria.
This comes off the back of a €150 million debt and equity raise back in November in 2025 – as covered by EU-Startups.
The move will see Zilch take over floors four and five of 40 Grosvenor Place, a 33,160sq ft space that can accommodate more than 400 employees. The investment will go towards a 10-year lease as the business continues to scale its operations and plans to create more jobs in the UK.
Philip Belamant, co-founder and CEO of Zilch, says: “It has been a transformational year for the business with a number of significant milestones, and our customers moving beyond £8 billion of spend across every region in the UK.
“As we continue to expand rapidly, our new headquarters reflect the scale of our ambition and the momentum behind our growth. This is an important investment in Zilch’s future, giving our team an incredible base to attract exceptional talent at home and beyond. We are proud to be investing further in the UK as we enter the next phase of growth.”
Zilch’s headquarters investment comes amid financing activity across European consumer credit and payments in 2026.
According to EU-Startups’ coverage, fellow UK companies Primer raised €86.2 million to develop its AI-powered payments infrastructure, Vuelo secured €64 million for its travel financing platform, and Plend obtained a credit facility of up to €58.3 million.
Elsewhere, Barcelona-based ID Finance secured €545 million in debt and equity to expand its Plazo consumer finance platform, while Madrid-based BCAS raised €30 million for flexible education financing.
Together with the €83 million secured by London-based Sokin and Manchester-based Ryft’s €23 million Series B, these announcements represent approximately €889.5 million in disclosed financing and credit facilities during 2026.
This data paints the FinTech sector, especially the UK FinTech sector, to be a rich and highly active ecosystem – providing context for Zilch’s competition and growth.
City Minister Rt Hon Lucy Rigby KC MP adds: “This is a major milestone for Zilch and it’s brilliant to see their continued success. The UK is a FinTech powerhouse and I’m committed to backing the sector to thrive and grow.”
Founded in 2018, Zilch is an intelligent payments platform, combining debit, credit, instalments, earned wage access, credit building, deals and rewards.
The new headquarters is the latest announcement in a period of growth for Zilch, including the acquisition of Fjord Bank (announced back in January 2026), which is expected to complete in the first half of 2027 and will lay the foundation of its European expansion, a multi-year strategic partnership with Visa and becoming Arsenal FC’s Official Way to Pay.

articles.title: Une étoile morte brille en vert, et les astronomes viennent de comprendre pourquoi
articles.text:
On n’avait jamais recensé une étoile verte avant WD J1330+6435. Des astronomes de l’université de Warwick expliquent la teinte de cette naine blanche par des débris rocheux de son ancien système planétaire, tombés dans une atmosphère d’une densité hors norme.
La couleur d’une étoile dépend presque uniquement de sa température. Une étoile froide est orangée, une étoile très chaude d’un bleu pâle. Quand une étoile de la taille du Soleil épuise son combustible, elle laisse derrière elle une naine blanche, et les astronomes pensaient que ces astres morts suivaient eux aussi la règle des couleurs. Mark Hollands, chercheur en astrophysique à l’université de Warwick, a voulu vérifier cette idée avec trois collègues. Leur équipe a converti la lumière de naines blanches réparties dans tout le ciel en couleurs perçues par l’œil humain, et l’une d’elles est ressortie d’un vert chartreuse. Il faut remonter jusqu’aux restes de son ancien système planétaire pour comprendre d’où vient ce vert.
Du sodium tombé d’anciennes planètes
Les chercheurs estiment la température de surface de WD J1330+6435 à environ 4 000 °C, d’après leur étude parue mi-octobre dans la revue RAS Techniques and Instruments. Des fragments rocheux de son système planétaire sont tombés dans son atmosphère et ont apporté avec eux du sodium. C’est lui qui donne sa couleur à l’étoile. Ces débris sont récents à l’échelle astronomique, car les éléments lourds coulent vite sous la surface d’une naine blanche et disparaissent de la vue.
Dans une étoile ordinaire, le sodium absorbe une seule raie orange, très étroite. Les vieux lampadaires au sodium doivent leur teinte à cette raie. Chez les naines blanches les plus froides, la densité de l’atmosphère est d’environ un gramme par centimètre cube, autant que l’eau et des millions de fois plus que celle de la surface visible du Soleil. Dans ce plasma d’hélium très comprimé, le sodium absorbe une grande partie du jaune et de l’orange, et le calcium, lui aussi apporté par les débris, efface une part du violet. Le pic de la lumière émise est alors situé autour de 500 nanomètres, dans le vert.
« Les traces de sodium dans l’atmosphère de cette naine blanche absorbent la partie orange du spectre et laissent derrière elles une lueur verte fantomatique », a expliqué Mark Hollands. « Imaginez-vous sur une planète, en train de lever les yeux vers une étoile verte. On se croirait dans un film de science-fiction », a-t-il ajouté.
Certains titres anglophones ont fait de l’étoile un « zombie cosmique » mangeur de planètes. Selon Nature World News, l’étude montre seulement que des fragments rocheux sont tombés sur l’étoile, sans prouver que des planètes entières ont été englouties d’un seul coup.
Une couleur calculée, jamais vue à l’œil nu
Si vous pouviez vous approcher de WD J1330+6435, vous la verriez d’un vert jaunâtre. Aucune naine blanche n’est cependant assez proche de la Terre pour que sa couleur soit visible directement, et l’équipe de Mark Hollands a travaillé à partir des spectres. Dans un spectre, la lumière d’une étoile est décomposée longueur d’onde par longueur d’onde. Les chercheurs ont fait passer chacun de ces relevés dans un modèle standard de la vision humaine des couleurs, puis ont converti le résultat en valeurs affichables sur un écran d’ordinateur.
Personne n’a donc vu l’étoile briller en vert, et elle est bien trop faible pour un télescope d’amateur. Le spectre de WD J1330+6435 est assez bruité et sa teinte exacte pourrait légèrement différer, reconnaissent les chercheurs. Avec plusieurs modèles d’atmosphère, l’équipe obtient malgré tout un vert.
Les chercheurs ont aussi repéré deux naines blanches d’un vert plus pâle. WD J1011+2845, à 48 années-lumière, est d’un rose saumon profond, car la convection a fait remonter à sa surface du carbone issu de son cœur. À l’œil, elle est sans doute l’étoile la plus rouge connue.
L’équipe a ensuite passé en revue les 152 naines blanches situées à moins de 65 années-lumière de la Terre. Cinq seulement ont une teinte vraiment inhabituelle. Deux sont jaunes, trois sont roses, et les auteurs en déduisent qu’environ une naine blanche sur trente brille d’une couleur hors norme. La température de couleur médiane des 147 autres est d’environ 6 800 kelvins, soit un blanc presque pur. L’image de naines blanches bleutées est le fruit d’un biais d’observation, car les plus chaudes sont aussi les plus lumineuses et les astronomes les repèrent de plus loin dans les relevés. « Si l’on prend la médiane d’une population représentative de naines blanches, la naine blanche moyenne est vraiment blanche », a souligné Boris Gänsicke, professeur de physique à Warwick.
À environ 4 000 °C, WD J2356-2054 est elle aussi chargée de sodium, mais elle est d’un bleu vif à l’œil. D’après Mark Hollands et ses coauteurs, d’autres naines blanches d’un vert ou d’un cyan vif existent sans doute entre ces deux cas, et les astronomes pourraient les repérer dans de futurs relevés.

articles.title: One Compromised Login Exposed Millions of California Students’ Records
articles.text:
Personal information on current and former California public school students was copied from a file transfer system belonging to Educational Testing Service (ETS), according to the California Department of Education (CDE).
ETS is a nonprofit that handles state and federally mandated testing under a contract with the state. The organization supports California’s CAASPP and ELPAC assessment programs and relied on a secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) site to share testing data with CDE.
The organization spotted unauthorized activity on the site on September 25, but the earliest access dates back to late May.
“The investigation determined that an unauthorized party used a compromised login credential at various times during the period from May 22, 2026 to September 18, 2026 to access the SFTP site to copy files containing California student information,” according to the CDE’s breach notice.
No victim count has been provided, but the notice says, “Information about California students, including but not limited to all students enrolled in the three previous school years, was accessed and copied.”
CDE’s own enrollment figures put that in perspective: more than 5.7 million students were enrolled in California public schools in 2025-2026. The department’s incident FAQ notes that the impacted population also extends to students who left a California school as far back as 2006 and whose transfer to another school was not confirmed with CDE.
Compromised records can include information such as student name, birth date, home address, school, district and grade, state and local ID numbers, gender, race or ethnicity, primary language, country of origin and English learner status.
Some entries go further, revealing disability and Section 504 status, the primary disability type, testing accommodations, English proficiency data, and test registration and results. They may also indicate whether a student qualifies for Title I, McKinney-Vento or military-connected student designations.
The notice says the files did not contain Social Security numbers, passwords, or financial account or payment card details. Information on parents and guardians was not involved either.
ETS shut down the account the intruder used and pulled the SFTP site offline. Its response also includes building a replacement site with stronger safeguards.
The official disclosures do not explain how the login credential was compromised, and they do not identify the attacker.
“After working with law enforcement as well as with cybersecurity experts, ETS has taken steps to reduce the potential risk of the data being made publicly accessible,” the notice states. ETS did not elaborate, but said its web monitoring has so far found no evidence that the data has been published.
CDE informed county and district superintendents and charter school administrators of the incident in a letter dated October 2, two weeks before family notifications started. According to that letter, ETS stopped its regular processing of enrollment data and suspended some testing work while its systems’ security was evaluated.
Student notifications started going out on October 16, and CDE expects them to continue into early November. Affected current and former students can sign up for two years of free identity protection services.

articles.title: E Ink annonce le Kaleido 4, son nouvel écran couleur pour liseuse — Frandroid
articles.text:
E Ink, l’entreprise taïwanaise qui fabrique l’écran de presque toutes les liseuses du marché, vient de dévoiler le Kaleido 4, la nouvelle version de son écran couleur. Dans son communiqué, la marque promet deux fois plus de couleurs, des blancs plus lumineux et 50 % de contraste en plus par rapport au Kaleido 3. Ces promesses répondent aux principaux défauts qu’on associe souvent aux liseuses couleur actuelles, même récentes. Leur écran est ainsi plus terne que celui d’une liseuse noir et blanc, et les couleurs sont délavées.
Le Kaleido 3, qui est sorti en 2022 et commence donc à dater, équipe toujours la plupart des liseuses couleur vendues en France, jusqu’à la toute récente Boox Note Air6 C.
Des blancs moins gris et des couleurs plus vives
Avec le Kaleido 4, E Ink garde le principe classique d’un écran à encre électronique. Un filtre de couleurs (rouge, vert, bleu) est apposé sur l’encre électronique noir et blanc classique. Ce filtre permet de garder un affichage rapide et une bonne autonomie. Mais c’est aussi ce filtre qui absorbe une partie de la lumière, ce qui assombrit l’écran. Il réduit aussi la résolution de moitié (on passe généralement de 300 ppp à 150 ppp).
Selon E Ink, le Kaleido 4 doublerait le volume de couleurs que l’écran peut reproduire. Le blanc gagnerait aussi 15 % de réflectance : en pratique, le fond de page devrait ainsi paraître moins gris, ce qui ferait monter le contraste et améliorerait beaucoup le confort de lecture. La promesse de la marque : un contraste amélioré de 50 %.
Côté électronique, grâce à l’introduction de nouveaux algorithmes, l’E Ink Kaleido 4 pourrait lire des vidéos jusqu’à 18 images par seconde, là où le Kaleido 3 plafonnait à 12.
En revanche, E Ink n’a pas communiqué sur la résolution max de ce nouvel écran.
Kobo et Boox attendus pour 2027
Pour l’instant, un seul appareil utilise le Kaleido 4 : il s’agit de la M10C II, une tablette de prise de notes de Hanvon, qui est vendue uniquement en Chine.
Alors quand et où espérer voir ce nouvel écran ? Kobo, Onyx Boox, Bigme et Nook pourraient sortir des modèles avec le Kaleido 4 en 2027, sans plus de précision. À voir si Amazon pourrait utiliser à terme ce nouvel écran pour ses Kindle. Côté reMarkable, la marque norvégienne utilise des écrans E Ink Gallery 3, qui reposent sur une autre technologie qui n’utilise pas de filtre couleur et offre ainsi une meilleure résolution (mais un moins bon rafraîchissement d’écran).

South Africa wants all ATMs to become unbranded
South Africa is not trying to kill cash. It is trying to make using it cheaper.
The South African Reserve Bank (SARB) wants the country’s more than 30,000 automated teller machines (ATMs) to become a shared, unbranded network. Small withdrawals, deposits, and balance enquiries would be free below a set limit, regardless of which bank owns the machine.
What happened? A pilot starts in January 2027. By March, the central bank wants to create a national cash utility, then begin folding cash centres run by companies such as SBV and Fidelity into that system by mid-year. The first white-label ATMs are expected before the end of 2027.
Explain like I’m new here: Today, each bank runs its own ATM network, cash centres, and logistics. That means duplicated machines, vehicles, routes, and vaults, all moving physical money around. SARB wants to pool much of that infrastructure and make ATMs work more like a national utility.
The economics explain the urgency. South Africa has about R180.65 billion ($10.9 billion) in cash in circulation, according to the SARB. The broader annual economic cost of using cash—including fees, travel, time, and crime-related losses—is estimated at nearly R90 billion ($5.5 billion). Cash accounts for about 56% of consumer transactions in South Africa, according to a Reserve Bank-commissioned study using 2024 as its base year, even as digital payment alternatives expanded.
Between the lines: Fewer cash transactions do not automatically make ATMs cheaper to run. The machines, guards, cash vans, and vaults still cost money. When those costs are spread across fewer transactions, each withdrawal costs more. Rural and low-income areas are usually the first places where banks cut machines.
A shared network flips that model. Banks stop duplicating the same infrastructure, while the central bank can place ATMs where access is most needed.
What to watch: The difficult part will be getting banks to surrender some control over machines they currently brand, price, and use to keep customers in their banking networks. If the model works, South Africa will not have fewer ATMs. But it will have fewer reasons for every bank to have its own.

Capital Market
Banque du Caire may raise IPO stake to 45%
Egypt may make one of its biggest upcoming listings even bigger.
Banque Misr is considering selling up to 45% of Banque du Caire, Egypt’s sixth-largest commercial bank by assets, in its upcoming initial public offering (IPO), up from the 30% announced on October 11. Investment banks working on the deal recommended the bigger sale after roadshows drew strong investor interest globally.
Here’s a simple back-of-napkin maths: At Banque du Caire’s reported valuation of EGP 80 billion–EGP 80.5 billion ($1.5 billion–$1.51 billion), according to local publication Asharq Business, a 45% stake would be worth between EGP 36 billion–EGP 36.2 billion ($670 million–$674 million), compared with EGP 24 billion–EGP 24.2 billion ($447 million–$451 million) for 30%.
Those figures assume the shares sell at the reported valuation. Bloomberg reported on Sunday that the bank was seeking up to EGP 24.25 billion ($454 million) from a 30% sale and could increase the stake to 45%, depending on demand. The larger offer would take Egypt past that target, becoming the country’s largest listing in years.
Catch up: This IPO has been a decade in the making. Egypt first announced plans to float 20% of Banque du Caire in March 2016. The bank’s shares were provisionally listed on the Egyptian Exchange in 2017, but the sale was delayed. Another attempt in 2020 was shelved after COVID-19 hit global markets.
Another important detail: Banque du Caire will not receive the money. The IPO entirely consists of existing shares owned by Banque Misr, its state-owned shareholder. Selling 45% puts about 6.86 billion shares into investors’ hands compared with 4.58 billion under the current plan. Trading is expected to begin in November.
Between the lines: Going bigger does more than raise extra cash for the state. It leaves more Banque du Caire shares available for investors to trade after the IPO, which could help make the stock more liquid. More importantly, increasing the sale because investors asked for more would signal that foreign appetite for Egypt’s privatisation programme is returning.
Zoom out: Egypt’s stock exchange already has a strong line-up for Q4. MNT-Halan, the country’s first fintech unicorn, would begin trading on October 20, after its floated shares were at least three times oversubscribed. The planned listing aims to raise $150 million, with wide retail investors’ participation expected. With Banque du Caire taking over the following month, there’s a lot of excitement in Egypt right now.

Telecoms
Vodacom keeps control of Safaricom amid ongoing court case
In June, Vodacom, one of Africa’s largest telecom companies, bought a majority stake in Safaricom, the operator of M-PESA. Four months later, a Kenyan court said it should undo the sale. Now, the shares remain in Vodacom’s custody as the legal battle over who gets to keep them moves to the next round.
What happened? On October 13, Kenya’s Court of Appeal ordered that the current position around the Safaricom shares and the $1.9 billion purchase price remain unchanged while it fast-tracks the appeal. That means Vodacom remains the registered holder of the 15% stake it bought from the Kenyan government.
Explain like I’m new here: Vodacom bought 15% of Safaricom from the Kenyan government, plus another effective 5% from Vodafone, its subsidiary, taking its stake from 35% to a majority of 55%. However, the deal ran into legal trouble.
Critics, including broadcaster Tony Gachoka and academic Frederick Ogola, challenged the sale, arguing that the government had not properly involved the public in the decision. The court froze it in March, then unfroze it in June. In September, the High Court declared the transaction unconstitutional and ordered the stake returned to the Kenyan government, throwing a spanner in the state’s plan to finance projects from those proceeds.
What’s the state of Safaricom’s ownership? Because Vodacom remains the registered holder of the shares, it can continue exercising the rights attached to its majority stake, including voting as a shareholder and participating in decisions that require shareholder approval. If the High Court judgment survives the appeal, Vodacom would lose the 15% stake it bought from the government and fall back to roughly 40%.

True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. Regulation
Ghana is changing how it collects VAT from foreign digital services
Ghana is looking to increase revenue, and taxing customers on the foreign digital services they use—such as Netflix, YouTube, and WhatsApp—is one strategy.
On October 15, the country launched Real-Time VAT (RTVAT) that lets the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), the country’s taxman, collect value-added tax (VAT) on qualifying digital services when customers pay foreign providers through Ghana-issued cards, mobile money accounts, and other digital payment channels.
The system applies to non-resident companies selling electronic services to customers in Ghana, including streaming platforms, cloud storage providers, software subscriptions, online advertising, and digital marketplaces.
Explain like I’m new here: This didn’t start today. Ghana has required foreign digital service providers to register for VAT since 2022. The GRA created an online registration and filing system for non-resident e-commerce businesses, requiring them to declare their Ghanaian sales and remit the taxes they collect.
However, Ghana cannot send a tax officer to a provider’s office monthly to check whether the right VAT was paid. Under RTVAT, when a Ghanaian customer pays for an eligible foreign digital service using a Ghana-issued card, mobile money account, or wallet, the payment provider can identify the transaction, withhold the applicable tax, and send it to the GRA.
Why is Ghana doing this? The GRA said that as of October 14, about 92 non-resident digital service providers were registered on the tax collection portal, while about 100 others either failed to collect the required taxes or haven’t remitted them. The authority previously estimated that an automated collection system could raise more than GH¢2.5 billion ($213 million) annually, compared with roughly GH¢515 million ($44 million) a year it currently collects.
What changes for users? If your Netflix bill already includes Ghanaian taxes, the GRA said RTVAT should not make you pay them twice. However, if a foreign provider previously didn’t collect the required tax, your final bill could now rise by 20%.
Zoom out: Banks, mobile money operators, payment service providers and other licenced payment processors handling these transactions must integrate with the RTVAT system. They must now correctly identify taxable transactions, collect and remit the right amount, and reverse the tax when refunds or chargebacks happen.

articles.title: YouTube en Argentina: los 10 videos que son tendencia este sábado
articles.text:
Desde su aparición en el 2005, YouTube se ha convertido en uno de los sitios web más importantes en la vida moderna, llegando a ser un fenómeno global que revolucionó la forma en la que se consume el contenido audiovisual.
Actualmente, aunque otras redes sociales como TikTok, Facebook o Instagram están apostando cada vez más por los videos, lo cierto es que YouTube sigue siendo el rey y para prueba de ello las cifras: es el segundo sitio electrónico más visitado en el mundo sólo detrás de Google; además tiene presencia en 104 países y está disponible en 80 idiomas.
Asimismo, a la plataforma estadounidense se suben alrededor de 500 horas de contenido por minuto y se cree que al día son vistos cinco mil millones de videos, dejando ganancias estimadas de 15 mil millones de dólares al trimestre.
Ante la facilidad que tienen los usuarios para perderse en un mundo de clips, Youtube ha creado diversas listas para consultar a los artistas más escuchados, más vistos y cuáles son las tendencias del día en tiempo real.
Estos son los videos que están en tendencia este sábado 17 de octubre
1. EL ALBAÑIL CUMBIERO (El Lauti) ENGANCHADO en VIVO en LA JUNTADA DE LOS ARTISTASArtista/canal: La Juntada De Los Artistas
2. Q'LoKura, Santiago Cañete - Me duele Amarte Te Fuiste De Aquí Ya Me EnteréArtista/canal: Q' Lokura
3. Que LloroArtista/canal: La Juntada De Los Artistas y El Lauti
4. VuelveArtista/canal: Anuel AA
5. Uriel Lozano - Debajo De Tu Ombligo (Video Oficial)Artista/canal: Uriel Lozano
6. NecioArtista/canal: Romeo Santos
7. BbY WOWArtista/canal: KAROL G, rusowsky y Judeline
8. Te Entiendo (En Vivo Movistar Arena)Artista/canal: Q' Lokura y Luciano Creiner
9. Pimpinela - Yo sabía (video oficial)Artista/canal: Pimpinela
10. Pobre CorazónArtista/canal: La Juntada De Los Artistas y El Lauti
El éxito de YouTube
YouTube vio la luz en febrero de 2005, cuando tres antiguos empleados de la compañía de Paypal ―Chad Hurley, Steve Chen y Jawed Karim― se unieron y la crearon luego de que experimentaran dificultades para compartir entre sí un par de videos tras asistir a una fiesta.
El dominio fue activado el 14 de febrero de 2005 y casi un mes después, el 23 de abril, fue cargado el primer clip a la plataforma que llevaba por nombre “Me at the Zoo”. Fue cuestión de tiempo para que todo el mundo comenzara a cargar contenido y a compartir los enlaces a través de otras redes sociales como MySpace.
Una de las grandes empresas que vio el potencial de YouTube fue la marca Nike, que subió una publicidad protagonizada por Ronaldinho, lo que hizo que otras grandes compañías voltearan a ver a YouTube y se sintieran atraídas.
Tal fue la gran acogida de los internautas por YouTube que para diciembre de 2005 la plataforma pasó de las 50 millones de visitas al día a 250 millones de visualizaciones luego de que un canal subiera el clip musical Lazy Sunday, transmitido originalmente por Saturday Night Live.
Para el año siguiente, en el 2006, el sitio fue comparado por el gigante del internet, Google, por un valor de 1650 millones de dólares. En ese entonces eran visualizados 100 millones de videos al día y 65 mil clips se añadían a diario. También firmaron acuerdos con disqueras para poder reproducir videos musicales.
Las polémicas de YouTube
Desde que fue puesto en marcha, YouTube fue un sitio que llegó a hacer una revolución no sólo en internet, sino también en la forma en la que los usuarios miran contenido. Muestra de ello el reconocimiento que la revista Time le otorgó en noviembre del 2006 al ser nombrado el “Invento del Año”.
Convertido en el mejor medio de difusión, el gozar de tanta popularidad también ha metido a sus dueños en aprietos como cuando albergar peleas escolares o en donde hay bullying, clips relacionados al terrorismo, narcotráfico u otros temas considerados delicados por su contenido íntimo o por mostrar delitos como asesinatos y más.
Para Estados Unidos uno de los temas más delicados es el de los tiroteos escolares, por lo que YouTube ha estado más de una vez en el ojo del huracán por alojar contenido filmado por los atacantes, como fue el caso de la masacre de Virginia Tech, cuando Cho Seung-Hui, el atacante, subió previamente a los hechos un discurso.
Más recientemente, tras el surgimiento de la pandemia del coronavirus, también ha surgido inquietud sobre cómo la plataforma permite la monetización de contenido que puede ser engañoso y riesgoso para la población.
Aunque no todo es malo, pues a través de dicha plataforma muchas personas han podido ser reconocidas por su talento, como fue el caso de Susan Boyle, quien participó en el programa Britain’s Got Talent cuyo extracto subido a YouTube logró que la mujer pasara a ser una completa desconocida a una de las personas más viralizadas, famosas y aclamadas del internet.

articles.title: Pourquoi vous devriez vérifier les paramètres de votre Amazon Fire TV Stick dès aujourd'hui
articles.text:
Les paramètres à désactiver sur votre Fire TV Stick pour limiter la collecte de données
Par défaut, votre Amazon Fire TV Stick suit tout ou presque ce que fait et regarde l'utilisateur. Pour retrouver un peu de sérénité, voyons comment désactiver cette reconnaissance automatique du contenu (ACR).
Comme les téléviseurs connectés, les boîtiers multimédia d'Amazon, Apple et autres Xiaomi qui y sont branchés sont gourmands en données personnelles. Que cela soit pour "améliorer l'expérience utilisateur" ou surtout afficher des contenus et des publicités personnalisés, les constructeurs passent par l'ACR (Automatic Content Recognition), ou reconnaissance automatique du contenu. Ce système de tracking, dont le nom et les fonctionnalités peuvent légèrement différer d'un fabricant à l'autre, permet généralement d'identifier le contenu consommé par l'usager en le comparant à de gigantesques bases de données, mais aussi d'analyser ses habitudes.
Tout cela n'est pas idéal pour la vie privée, vous en conviendrez. S'il n'est pas possible de faire disparaitre totalement la publicité sur les Stick d'Amazon (surtout les derniers modèles sous Vega OS, toujours plus fermés), il est en revanche autorisé de réduire (au moins partiellement) les données envoyées à Amazon et ses partenaires via l'ACR.
Après avoir vu comment désactiver l'ACR sur un téléviseur à l'aide de ce guide pour chaque marque, voyons la marche à suivre sur Amazon Fire TV.
Comment désactiver l'ACR sur Amazon Fire TV
Notez que les chemins d'accès et dénominations des fonctionnalités évoqués ci-dessous peuvent varier en fonction de l'ancienneté de votre Stick.
1/ Ouvrez les Paramètres du Stick (via la roue crantée sur votre photo de profil à droite et direction l'entrée Préférences ;
2/ Ouvrez ensuite le menu Paramètres de confidentialité ;
3/ Là, trois options activées par défaut doivent être désactivées. Il est question de Données d'utilisation de l'appareil (données personnelles collectées par le système d'exploitation à des fins marketing et d'améliorations du produit), Collecter les données d'utilisation (informations sur la fréquence et la durée d'utilisation des applications tierces) et Publicités basées sur vos centres d'intérêt. Pour ce dernier point, il est aussi possible de supprimer son identifiant publicitaire unique depuis ce menu afin de repartir de zéro et de se voir proposer des publicités "neutres".
Notez qu'après une mise à jour système, Amazon peut réactiver ces fonctionnalités. Il est donc préférable d'aller vérifier de temps en temps. De plus, même en désactivant toutes ces fonctionnalités il n'est pas assuré qu'aucune donnée personnelle ne sera envoyée à Amazon. Pour cela il faudrait désactiver l'accès à Internet au Stick, ce qui réduirait grandement son intérêt.

articles.title: .NET 11 Release Candidate 2: Go-Live License and Updates Across Libraries, F#, MAUI, and WinForms
articles.text:
Microsoft has released .NET 11 Release Candidate 2 with a go-live license for production use, as stated in the announcement. The build is supported in Visual Studio 2026 Insiders and in Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. As reported, it brings changes across the libraries, runtime, SDK, NuGet, F#, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, and Windows Forms, with no new C# language features.
In the libraries, CborReader can now read a payload delivered in chunks, using isFinalBlock and SlideData, in Lax conformance mode only. Two experimental cryptography types arrive: CompositeMLKem combines post-quantum and classical key encapsulation, and Hpke provides Hybrid Public Key Encryption with classical DHKEM suites only.
Both require opting in through SYSLIB5009 and SYSLIB5006, as described in the release notes. ValidationAttribute.FormatMessage lets a host supply a message template for the attribute to fill in, and SocketsHttpHandler.InitialHttp2MaxConcurrentStreams caps streams on a new HTTP/2 connection until the server's SETTINGS frame arrives.
The runtime release focuses on reliability but carries one breaking change. CoreCLR now disables advisory file locking by default on iOS and tvOS, because, as stated, FileStream lock in RC 1 could cause the OS to terminate an app entering the background. FileShare restrictions are no longer enforced there, and setting DOTNET_SYSTEM_IO_DISABLEFILELOCKING to 0 restores locking, according to the release.
ASP.NET Core has few new features but several changes for apps upgrading from RC 1. QuickGrid's AnchorMode and ItemComparer parameters are no longer experimental. IValidationMessageFormatter has been removed in favor of FormatMessage, the Blazor BasePath component moved to the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components namespace, and the experimental device-bound sessions package was pulled from this build. As reported, the remaining AddRazorRuntimeCompilation overloads now warn with ASPDEPR003.
In the SDK, file-based programs accept quoted values in #:property directives, and the #:package, #:project, and #:ref directives take trailing Name=Value item metadata. MSBuild gains faster wildcard matching during project evaluation, which, as reported in Microsoft's Windows benchmarks, puts it at 10–13% faster with 16–34% fewer allocations.
NuGet adds --min-publish-age-hours to dotnet nuget add source and update source, and restore fails with NU1020 when a package cooldown leaves no eligible floating version.
F# ships several preview features. The compiler gains return and await intrinsics for building custom computation-expression builders on the runtime-async model, though FSharp.Core does not yet ship such a builder, as stated in the notes.
let calculation () =
    runtimeTask {
        let captured = 40
        let! delta = delayed 2
        return captured + delta
    }
The reraise() now works inside the with handler of async and task expressions. Outside preview, more List and Array functions inline their callbacks to cut allocations, Async.parallelLimit bounds concurrent work, and bitwise operators on non-integer enums now fail at compile time with FS0001.
The .NET MAUI maui template gains a --ui csharp option that generates the app, shell, and main page in C# rather than XAML, and the multi-project template adds an --avalonia option for an Avalonia desktop project.
MauiIcon accepts Apple Icon Composer .icon bundles, and UseiOSShellHandler opts into a handler-based Shell on Apple platforms. Android adds API 37.2 bindings and JDK 25 support, while Apple workloads now require Xcode 27.0 and apps built with its SDKs must adopt the UIKit scene lifecycle, as described in the breaking changes.
Windows Forms refines the .NET 11 visual styles. Application.SetDefaultVisualStylesMode selects the renderer version, but ToolStrip and DataGridView keep Classic rendering even under Net11 for now. Application.SystemVisualSettings exposes a snapshot of the Windows accent color, text scaling, and high-contrast state, and FormRevealMode defers a top-level form's first presentation to reduce background flashes.
New analyzers WFO3000 to WFO3002 flag code that cannot round-trip through the Designer, which the release notes say is particularly useful when AI tools generate or refactor forms.
Other changes in this release are MSBuild property expansion in launch-profile arguments, an F# RequireNamedArgumentsAttribute, a private-member R8 obfuscation default on Android, SuspendPainting and KioskModeManager for Windows Forms, EF Core SaveChanges and JSON projection fixes.
On Reddit, discussion focused less on the features than on upgrade cadence. Commenters asked how many teams still skip odd-numbered releases, and others replied that since .NET 9 a standard-term release shares its end-of-support date with the preceding LTS version, moving to .NET 11 costs no support time.
Other developers reported MAUI workloads breaking on every preview upgrade, questioned Blazor server-side rendering performance against Razor Pages and MVC, and welcomed the KioskModeManager component for Windows Forms.
For interested readers and developers, the full release notes for .NET 11 RC 2 are available on the dotnet/core repository on GitHub.
